# dsh-publish-gate — 帮你发布 DSH 插件的一键三连门禁

> **这个插件是给插件作者用的**：你写完一个 DSH 插件，想发 GitHub + npm + 插件市场，它帮你把发布前该查的全部查一遍，再给你照抄的命令清单。
>
> 发布一个 DSH 插件有七步，每一步都有一个**直到你付出代价才说话的坑**：`files` 忘了 `lib/` 于是发出去一个空包、PowerShell 写下的 BOM 让 `JSON.parse` 报一个不提 BOM 的错、patch 的 insert 行缩进错了于是插件装上了但**永远不加载**、裸包名让 granular token 收到一个既不说 token 也不说 scope 的 403。这个插件把整条链路的每个静默坑变成一条确定性检查。

十四个 agent 工具：全量门禁、运行时注册检查、发后校验、patch 专项、市场条目校验、版本推进、多插件体检、发布命令清单、本地开发链路诊断、装前试跑、CI 模板、更新前预检、机械修复。

门禁分三层：**清单层**看 package.json / patch / 入口源码，**产物层**真的跑一遍 `npm pack --dry-run` 看 npm 到底会发出什么，**运行时层**在独立子进程里 `import()` 入口并 `apply(ctx)` 一遍，看它到底注册了什么。

### 自检：看不见的 finding

`severity` 不是 `error`/`warn`/`info` 的 finding 会被所有计数器忽略，等于规则从没触发过。`publish_gate` 现在会把这类 finding 提升成一条 `internal-bad-severity` 的 error，测试里还有一条源码扫描盯着 `F(...)` 的第二个参数。这条网加上当天就抓到了我自己的同一个错误。

### 测试层：门禁真的会跑一遍你的测试

`tests-fail` / `tests-timeout` / `tests-not-run` 三条规则会以 `node --test` 在插件目录里真跑一次（不经过 `npm test`，因为脚本内容由作者决定、可能 shell 出去）。子进程会去掉继承来的 `NODE_TEST_CONTEXT`——否则当门禁本身跑在 `node --test` 里时，子进程进入 test-child 模式、一个摘要都不打印，看起来像"没有测试"。

## 📮 提建议 / 报问题 / 说它判错了

**这个插件最想要的反馈是「你判错了」。** 它全部的价值就是一句绿色的结论可信；任何一条规则把好包判成坏包、或者放过一个坏包，都比缺十个功能严重。

| 你想说的 | 请带上什么 |
|---|---|
| **误报**：这条规则不该出现 | `publish_gate(dir, { format: "markdown" })` 的整段输出 + 你的仓库地址 |
| **漏报**：我的插件踩了坑它没说话 | 那次发布失败时的**原始报错**，和你的插件目录 |
| **建议**：还该查什么 | 你发布时最怕、现在还得靠人肉记着的那一步 |

三个入口，按顺手程度排：

1. **GitHub Issues（推荐）** — <https://github.com/bushizhanghan/dsh-publish-gate/issues>，`误报 / 漏报` 模板就是照上面那张表问的。
2. **直接对 agent 说** — 把仓库路径给我，我拿 `publish_gate` 复现一遍，比你描述快。
3. **市场条目**下的讨论区。

说你踩过的坑，会被做成 `test/corpus.test.mjs` 里的一个固定用例（现在那六个用例就是 `@liustack/modlens`、`@michengai/dsh-codex-ui`、`@tt-a1i/archify-dsh` 这些真实包装出来的）——**同一条误报不会犯第二次**，这是这个插件唯一真正的进步方式。

**先说清楚不做的**（免得你提了我只能拒）：不自动改你的代码、不自动 bump 版本、不自动发 npm、不假装能在 CI 里跑完整门禁。`publish_gate_fix` 例外——它只做「这条规则只有一个正确答案」的那两类清单修复，而且默认 dry-run，见下面的设计取舍。

## 典型用法（写完插件后）

```
我写好了一个新插件 X，帮我发出去
→ agent 先调 publish_gate(X) 查所有静默坑（清单 + 产物 + 运行时三层）
→ 有 blocker 就修，修完再跑
→ 全绿后调 publish_gate_commands(X, {version}) 拿 GitHub/npm/市场三步的命令，照抄执行
→ 发完调 publish_gate_verify(X) 确认 registry 上那包的 shasum 和你本地这份一致
```

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add @bushizhanghan/dsh-publish-gate
```
重启 DSH 后生效。**只读**：除 `publish_gate_fix` 在你显式传 `apply: true` 时改 `package.json` 里那两类机械修复之外，这个插件从不写你的插件目录——不碰 `lib/`、不碰版本、不碰依赖。

## Agent 工具

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `publish_gate` | 全量门禁：清单 + 产物 + 运行时 + 浏览器半边 + 网络，返回 `safeToPublish`（`skipPack` / `skipTools` / `skipClient` / `skipNetwork` 可逐层跳过） |
| `publish_gate_tools` | 只跑运行时层：在子进程里 `apply(ctx)`，看注册了哪些工具、有没有缺 `execute`、重名、`presentCall` 抛错、`card` 用了宿主不认识的值 | 传 `call: ["工具名"]` 可以**真的调一次**（空参数）：注册永远不会执行 `execute`，所以「一调就抛 ReferenceError」这类 bug 只有这一条能看见。默认不调——有些工具会开程序或写文件，你点名才算同意。超时单独算 `tool-call-slow`（warn），不跟「真的抛了」混在一起：`of_env` 这种要起 WSL 的工具本来就慢。 |
| `publish_gate_client` | 只跑浏览器半边：在子进程里假造 `window.__ModuleLoader__`，看 bundle 会不会加载、`apply` 会不会抛、到底往哪个服务注册了东西、`inject` 有没有漏 |
| `publish_gate_verify` | 发后校验：`npm pack --dry-run` 的 shasum 和 registry 上的 `dist.shasum` 逐字节比，比版本号猜准 |
| `publish_gate_patch` | 只查 `cordis.patch.yml`——「插件装了但工具没出现」的第一个怀疑对象 |
| `publish_gate_market` | 校验市场条目 YAML（url/name/category/description 双语）；传 `dir` 则改查只有线上才能回答的三件事：这个仓库**已经在目录里**（再开 PR 就是重复条目）、另一个条目也在发同一个 npm 包、仓库还**不满 24 小时**（提交门禁会失败并自己重跑） |
| `publish_gate_next_version` | 当前版本、是否已被 registry 占用、建议 bump 到多少（本地比 npm 旧时从 npm 的 latest 往上加，不会推荐一个已被占用的版本） |
| `publish_gate_doctor` | 一次扫一个目录下的所有插件并按 blocker 排序（离线，不查 registry/GitHub），每行带真实打包体积 | 也认 pnpm/npm workspace：`pnpm-workspace.yaml` 的 `packages:` 与 `package.json` 的 `workspaces`，所以 monorepo 里的 `packages/*`、`plugins/*` 不会被当成空目录 |
| `publish_gate_link` | 本地开发链路：不联网、不调包管理器，只读 profile 自己的 `node_modules` / `.modules.yaml` / `cordis.patch.yml`，回答「宿主现在跑的到底是不是我刚改的这份代码」——链接的形态与目标、pnpm store 的 major、patch 行挂不挂载，一次报全。传 `profile` 可看别的 profile（默认 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`） |
| `publish_gate_smoke` | **装之前最接近真装的一次检查**：把 registry 上那个 tarball 下下来，解到 **profile 自己的 node_modules 里**（所以它的裸 import 会照真实依赖解析，而不是在系统临时目录里报 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND）、import 入口、`apply(ctx)` 一遍，报注册了什么、有没有抛。跑完自己清干净 |
| `publish_gate_ci` | 生成 `.github/workflows/publish-gate.yml`：CI 能真做的两件事——跑测试、以及校验 tarball 里到底有没有解析出来的入口文件和 `cordis.patch.yml`。**不假装**能在 runner 上跑完整门禁（那里没有 profile、没有宿主、也进不去你的 npm scope） |
| `publish_gate_update` | **装之前先回答该不该装**。市场里的更新插件都是装完起不来才回滚；这个先把 registry 上那个版本真的下载下来、解包到临时目录，跑同一套产物层与运行时层：入口能不能 import、`apply()` 能不能注册、tarball 里有没有代码、参数传错会不会抛。只在 checkout 里才有意义的规则（git / 市场 / 测试 / 链接）会被过滤掉，结论只关于代码。传 `dir` 或 `name` 都行（只给包名时从已装副本读当前版本） |
| `publish_gate_fix` | 只做「规则只有一个正确答案」的那两类机械修复：scoped 包缺 `publishConfig.access: "public"`（npm 会按私有发，报错既不说 scope 也不说这个字段）、`files` 里少了入口目录或挂载 patch（于是发出去一个装得上但永不加载的包）。**默认 dry-run**，只说改哪几处、为什么；`apply: true` 才写回 `package.json`。代码、版本、依赖一律不碰 |
| `publish_gate_commands` | 按顺序列出发布命令，并标出这台机器已经走到哪一步。命令是**这台机器上真能跑的形式**：Windows 下 `npm publish` 走 `cmd /c`（PowerShell 的 `npm.ps1` 常被执行策略拦掉），`npm publish` 后面紧跟一条 `publish_gate_verify`；版本是预发版时命令自带 `--tag next`；最后一步是给发出去的 commit 打 tag |

## 检查清单

### 会真的挡住发布的（error）

> 缺 `description` / `license` / `repository` / `author` 只给 warn：它们不影响安装和加载，只是出事时没人可找。0.25.1 之前这四个也报 error，29 个真实插件里 19 个因此被判「不能发」——那是把元数据当成了缺陷。
| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `utf8-bom` | BOM 让 JSON.parse 抛「Unexpected token」，错误信息里没有 BOM 三个字 |
| `json-parse` | package.json 语法错误 |
| `missing-field` | `name` / `version` / `main` / `type` 缺失——这四项决定消费者能不能加载它 |
| `invalid-name` / `invalid-version` | npm 拒绝的形状 |
| `files-omits-lib` | 发出去是空包——**npm 不警告** |
| `files-omits-patch` | `dsh.bundle.patch` 指的文件不在 files 里，装上不挂载 |
| `no-exports` | 缺 `exports["."]`，宿主解析不到入口 |
| `private-field-set` | 还留着脚手架模板的 `"private": true`，npm 直接 EPRIVATE 拒发 |
| `client-without-export` | 声明了 client 平台却没导出 `./client`，宿主半边在、侧栏永不出现 |
| `client-without-platform` | 反过来：导出了 `./client` 却没写 `dsh.client.platform`。文件发出去了，宿主不知道要加载它——装上后一个字节都不执行，而且没有任何报错 |
| `not-esm` | 没 `"type": "module"`，`import` 在加载时炸 |
| `no-insert-row` | patch 里只有 override，永远不挂载（页面报的仍然是这条——顶层 `- id:` 是 patch 不是挂载） |
| `bundle-patch-not-declared` | 有 `cordis.patch.yml` 但清单里没有 `dsh.bundle.patch`——patch 是死的，装了不挂载 |
| `entry-path-missing` | `main` / `exports["."]` / `exports["./client"]` 指的文件不存在，宿主解析到空 |
| `exports-target-missing` | 某个子路径导出（`"./engine"` 之类，不是 `"."` 也不是 `"./client"`）指向的文件根本不存在。谁写 `import x from "<包>/engine"` 谁就在运行时拿到解析错误 |
| `bin-target-missing` | `bin` 里某个命令指向的文件不存在。npm 会给它建软链，装完这条命令能出现在 PATH 上、一跑就报 not found |
| `entry-missing` | 清单里没有任何一个存在的入口文件——连 `import` 的机会都没有 |
| `inject-missing-*` | 用了 `ctx.tools` / `ctx.web` / `ctx.webServer` / `ctx.setInterval` 却没在 `inject` 里声明，cordis 永远不激活 |
| `patch-not-mount` | info：这些顶层 `- id:` 是在覆盖已有条目，合法，但**不是**挂载 |
| `insert-missing-name` / `insert-name-mismatch` | 挂载名缺失或与 package.json 不一致 |
| `no-patch-file` | 声明了 `dsh`（即自称是插件包）却既没有 `cordis.patch.yml` 也没有别的 bundle 补丁——装上了，宿主不会挂载它。没有 `dsh` 字段的纯库不在此列（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write`、`dsh-tui` 这类从来没有被谁挂载，要求它们交补丁是门禁自己发明规则） |
| `no-name-export` / `no-apply-export` | 入口协议不完整 |
| `bin-no-shebang` | `bin` 指向的文件没有 `#!` 行。Windows 上照样能跑，unix 上 shell 会自己执行它，报的是 shell 语法错，看不出真正原因 |
| `require-in-esm` | ESM 里 `require()` → `ERR_AMBIGUOUS_MODULE_SYNTAX`，报错不带行号 |
| `no-license` | 缺 LICENSE |
| `version-taken` | 这个版本已经在 registry 上，再发是 403 |
| `version-behind-latest` | 本地版本比 registry 上的 `latest` **旧**。npm 会照收，但 `latest` 继续指向新版本——包上传了，按名字装的人永远拿不到，且没有任何报错 |
| `publish-tag-not-latest` | 版本已经在 registry 上了，但 `dist-tags.latest` 还指着旧的。`--tag next` 发出去的版本就是这样：看着发出去了，按名字装的人拿到的还是旧的 |
| `prerelease-published-as-latest` | 版本是 `-beta` / `-rc`，却没写 `publishConfig.tag`。npm 不看后缀，照样发到 `latest`——所有人 `npm i` 装到的都是没做完的构建 |
| `registry-unreachable` | registry 回了 500/429 —— 版本检查**没跑**，所以别把它当干净 |
| `npm-not-logged-in` | 这台机器上 npm 没有可用登录（`npm whoami` 报 ENEEDAUTH）。`npm publish` 会在 tarball 打好之后才失败 |
| `readme-wrong-package` | README 的安装命令写的是**另一个包名**（从别的插件抄过来没改）。照着装的人装到别的插件上，而且不会报错——那个包真的存在 |

### 值得在发布前知道的（warn / info）
`npm-scope-mismatch`（登录的账号不是包 scope 的所有者，PUT 会 403，而错误里既不说 token 也不说 scope——我为一个 403 花了一小时）、`unscoped-name`（granular token 的 403）、`repo-missing`、`patch-name-unresolvable`（junction 放错层级）、`inject-unused-service`（`inject` 里写了个拼错的服务名，cordis 一直等它，插件静默不激活）、`no-publish-config-access`（scoped 包没写 `publishConfig.access`，只是提醒，因为命令里本来就带 `--access public`）、`publish-config-registry`（`publishConfig.registry` 指到内网 registry，版本发到别人装不到的地方）、`no-readme` / `readme-no-install` / `readme-no-profile`、`license-mismatch`、`no-tests` / `no-test-files` / `no-test-script`、`no-engines`、`bad-repo-url`、`no-git` / `no-gitignore`、`readme-path-missing`（README 里点名的仓库内文件路径已经不存在了，照着敲就是 ENOENT）、`readme-tool-undocumented`（README 没提这个工具）/ `readme-test-count`（README 写的测试数和真实数不一致）、`changelog-missing-version`（要发的这个版本号在 CHANGELOG 里没有对应标题，npm 照样发，发布说明就永远落后一版）、`changelog-no-versions`（CHANGELOG 里没有版本标题，读者对不上自己装的那版）、`no-changelog`（只是提醒）、`changelog-not-shipped`（CHANGELOG 在本地但没进 tarball——npm 只强制带 README 和 LICENSE，你一直更新的那份文件在 registry 页面上看不见），以及市场条目的 `market-*` 全系列。

### 产物层：npm 到底会发出什么

清单层只看 `files` 字段，而 npm 有它自己的规矩（`main` / `exports` 指向的文件强制入包、README/LICENSE/package.json 强制入包）。所以这一层真的跑一遍 `npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts`，读它返回的文件清单和体积。

| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `pack-omits-lib` | tarball 里没有 `lib/`——发出去是空包，**npm 不警告** |
| `pack-omits-patch` | `dsh.bundle.patch` 指的文件没进 tarball，装上不挂载 |
| `pack-omits-client` | `exports["./client"]` 指的文件没进 tarball。npm **不会**因为它在 `exports` 里就强制入包（只强制 `main`），所以 `files` 里没写它就会静默丢掉——本地能跑、装了没侧栏 |
| `pack-omits-export` | 子路径指向的文件在仓库里有，但 `files` 没让它进 tarball。和上一条的区别：代码没问题，**发出去的那个包**少了文件，装完 `import "<包>/engine"` 解析到空 |
| `pack-omits-readme` / `pack-omits-license` | README / LICENSE 没进包 |
| `pack-oversize` | 解包 >5 MB 是 error、>1 MB 是 warn，并点名最大的三个文件。测试 fixture 是常见元凶——我的一个插件曾把 20 MB 的算例目录发上去，装了它的人每次都要下 20 MB |
| `pack-ships-secret` | tarball 里有 `.env` / `.npmrc` / `*.pem` / `*.key` / `id_rsa`。没写 `files` 字段时 npm 会把 `.gitignore` 没排除的一切都打包，而包一发布就是公开的、npm 不会帮你撤回 |
| `pack-unexpected-dir` | `fixtures` / `test` / `tests` / `src` 被打进包里 |
| `pack-ships-junk` | 包里带上了 `.bak-20261026` 这类备份或编辑器残留。`files: ["lib"]` 会把 `lib/` 里所有东西都打进去——包括你自己源码的上一版，而且发上去就永久公开 |
| `pack-script-build` | 有 `prepack` / `prepare`：dry run 用了 `--ignore-scripts`，这次清单**不代表**真正发布时的产物 |
| `pack-unavailable` | npm 跑不起来（warn）——产物层没跑，别把它当干净 |

### 运行时层：`apply` 之后到底注册了什么

前两层都是读文件，读不出「装上能不能用」。这一层在独立子进程里 `import()` 入口、用假 ctx 调一次 `apply(ctx)`，把 `ctx.tools.register` 收到的每一条拿回来检查。20 秒超时，你的插件代码不在宿主进程里跑。

入口按 `exports["."]` → `main` → `lib/index.js` 的顺序解析。**早先写死 `lib/index.js`，拿三十一个真实已装插件一测，二十个报"入口抛异常"——其中两个的入口是 `index.mjs`，根本没有 `lib/`。**误报比漏报更贵：一个满屏假错误的门禁，第二次就没人跑了。

| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `entry-import-failed` | `import()` 入口就抛——装上必定不加载 |
| `entry-import-unresolved` | 入口 import 了一个没装在旁边的包（`@deepseek-ai/*` 这类宿主提供的 peer）——**warn**，不是缺陷 |
| `apply-threw` | `apply(ctx)` 抛 |
| `tool-none-registered` | 入口能加载，但一个工具都没注册 |
| `tool-missing-execute` / `tool-missing-output-schema` | 注册项缺 `execute` / `output.schema`（宿主用 schema 校验返回值，缺了等于没校验） |
| `tool-duplicate-name` | 两个工具同名，后者静默覆盖前者 |
| `tool-present-call-throws` | `presentCall` 抛——调用记录渲染时炸 |
| `tool-bad-card-kind` | `card: 'generic'` 的 `kind` 不在宿主认识的那一组里（`other` / `execute` / `search` / `read` / `edit` / `delete` / `fetch`）。注册不报错，卡片渲染坏掉——我五个插件一起踩过 |
| `tool-bad-parameter-type` | `parameters` 里某个 `type` 写错（`"strin"`）。宿主把 `parameters` 渲染进 prompt、但**从不校验**调用值，所以这个 typo 只是悄悄把类型提示弄丢 |
| `tool-no-description` | 工具没有 description。模型是靠 name + description + parameters 挑工具的，没有描述就只剩名字——工具发出去了，但基本选不中 |
| `tool-description-thin` | description 少于 30 字符，或者就是把工具名重复一遍。等于没写 |
| `tool-no-parameters` | execute 读 `args.x`，但整个 `parameters` 都没有。模型拿不到参数清单，不知道该传什么 |
| `tool-undeclared-param` | `execute` 读了 `args.x`，但 `parameters.properties` 里没有 `x`。模型只能传 schema 声明过的参数，所以这个值在真实调用里永远是 `undefined`——代码在，永远不跑，也不报错。`args.x`、`args['x']`、`const { x } = args` 三种写法都认 |
| `tool-output-invalid` | 工具返回的东西**自己的 output schema 不收**。宿主每个结果都拿 schema 校验，不匹配就抛 `ToolOutputError`——工具从第一次调用起就不可用，而报错只给一个 JSON 路径，不给是哪行代码返回的。只有点名 `call` 真的调了才检查。这个插件自己踩过：schema 收紧成 `additionalProperties: false`，但有一条错误分支还在返回 `{ ok, error }` |
| `tool-input-throws` | 把每个声明过的参数**塞一个错类型的值**去调，工具直接抛 `TypeError` 而不是回答。宿主从不拿 `parameters` 校验入参，所以这个值真的会到你的代码里——调用方拿到的是 `The "path" argument must be of type string`，插件日志里没有一行说是哪个工具。这条规则是在自己的工作区里跑出 **12 个真实崩溃** 之后才加的（`session`/`profile`/`casePath`/`workspace` 各一个入口），现在九个插件全绿。默认关：它会把每个工具都调一遍，用 `skip` 点名排除那些会开程序、写文件的 |

### 浏览器半边：侧栏面板到底会不会出现

清单层只检查「声明了 client 平台就得有 `exports["./client"]`」，可这一步过了之后还能坏很多次。而且它坏得很安静：宿主半边照样跑、工具照样能用，只是侧栏里什么都没有——看起来像 UI bug，其实是打包/注册 bug。

所以这一层真的把那个 bundle 在一个子进程里跑一遍：造一个假的 `window.__ModuleLoader__`、假的 `require('react')`，再给一个 `ctx`——`effect` / `inject` 会立刻执行回调，其余服务（`sidebarRightTabs`、`slots`…）每被调用一次就记一条。

| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `client-file-missing` | `exports["./client"]` 指的文件不存在 |
| `client-no-module-loader` | bundle 里没有 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load`——宿主根本不会执行它 |
| `client-load-not-called` | 文件能解析，但跑完没调用 `load`（常见：包在 `if (typeof window !== 'undefined')` 里，判断写错了） |
| `client-factory-throws` | `factory(require)` 抛 |
| `client-no-apply` | `factory` 返回的对象里没有 `apply` |
| `client-apply-throws` | `apply(ctx)` 抛 |
| `client-no-registration` | `apply` 跑完一次服务都没调用——面板不会出现 |
| `client-inject-missing-<service>` | `apply` 用了 `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` 但 `inject` 数组里没写它。cordis 不会把没声明的服务给你，于是 `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` 是 `undefined`，`apply` 一碰就抛（或静默什么都没注册） |
| `client-double-load` | 同一个 bundle 被注入了两次（它自己的 patch 一次，注入 `dsh-client-modules` 的侧边栏插件再一次）。loader 按 id 建工厂，第二次注册直接抛错，整个 Web 启动被中断——不是这个面板没了，是所有面板都没了。用 `if (window.__xLoaded) return; window.__xLoaded = true` 挡一下 |
| `client-parse-failed` | 文件有语法错误。**单独判**：`SyntaxError` 说明 bundle 本身是坏的，别的报错说明是沙箱不够真，两者别混为一谈 |
| `client-unavailable` | 子进程没跑起来（warn）——这一层没跑，别把它当干净 |

### 市场层：提交之前就能知道会不会被打回

本地全绿之后，发布还会在提交门禁那儿停一次。停的原因通常只有三种，而且三种都能提前查：

| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `market-duplicate-entry` | 这个仓库**已经在目录里**。再提一个 PR 就是同一仓库的第二条条目，reviewer 会拒。版本升级根本不需要 PR——目录条目只存 `url` |
| `market-release-behind` | 最新 GitHub release 比 package.json 旧（或新）。目录里写着 1.2.7、release 资产还是 1.2.6 时，市场条目装的是旧代码，而描述是新版写的——维护者正是以「描述与 tarball 不符」驳回过一次提交 |
| `market-npm-name-collision` | 另一个条目也在发同一个 npm 包，安装路径会互相盖 |
| `market-repo-too-new` | 仓库创建不满 24 小时。门禁会报 `0.0 days old` 然后**自己重跑**，PR 不会丢，但在那之前什么都不会合 |
| `market-fork-of-listed` | 这个仓库是某个**已经在目录里**的仓库的 fork。两条条目装的代码抢同一批 id，两个都装就有一个被静默盖掉——而且 reviewer 会把"没写"当成"隐瞒 fork" |
| `market-fork-undisclosed` | 是 fork，但 README 和 package.json 里都没有上游的 `owner/repo` |
| `market-no-repo` | `package.json` 里没有 GitHub 地址，没东西可提交 |
| `market-unavailable` | 目录拉不到（warn）——这几条没跑，别把它当干净 |
| `github-unavailable` | GitHub API 读不到（403 限流 / 5xx / 断网）：仓库年龄、fork 两条、未披露 fork **三条检查全部没跑**，标题里直接写「three market checks did not run」 |
| `market-release-unverified` | `releases/latest` 读不到（info）。404 不算——那是「这个仓库真的没有 release」，是答案；其余状态码才是「不知道」 |

### 代码卫生

`lib-debugger`（error）、`lib-console-log`（**每个文件一条，带次数**；浏览器半边豁免——那里 `console.log` 是调试通道，不是宿主日志残渣）、`lib-hardcoded-path`（`C:\Users\...` 硬编码）、`lib-url-pathname`（`new URL(...).pathname` 在中文路径上会百分号编码，得用 `fileURLToPath`）、`node-too-old`（`engines.node` 写着 `>=18`，`lib/` 里却用了 `Object.groupBy`（21）或 `Promise.withResolvers`（22）。npm 对 `engines` 只是警告，照样装上，然后在 import 那一刻抛——用户看到的是「插件坏了」，不是版本不匹配）。字符串和注释里的同名文字不算。

### 依赖真实性：`lib/` 里 import 的东西，消费者那边真的会装上吗

`npm install` 装一个包时只装它的 `dependencies`，**永远不装 `devDependencies`**。所以在你自己仓库里 `import 'x'` 能跑（依赖树是完整的），到了用户那边 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`——插件装上了，然后加载失败，用户看到的是「这个插件坏了」。

| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `undeclared-import` | `lib/` 里 import 了某个包，`package.json` 三个依赖字段里都没有。它在你机器上能解析，只是因为别的包把它提升（hoist）到了 `node_modules` |
| `dep-in-dev-only` | 只在 `devDependencies` 里声明。这是最常见的一种：写代码时 `npm i -D` 装上了，测试也全绿 |
| `unused-dependency` | `dependencies` 里声明了，`lib/` 里从没 import。每个装你的人都白下一份（info，因为有些包是运行时动态加载的）。带浏览器半边的包**不查这条**：打包器已经把依赖内联进 bundle，代码就在里面，不是没用到 |

内置模块（`node:fs`、`fs/promises`）、相对路径、以及浏览器半边从宿主 `require` 拿到的 `react` 都不算。工具描述里那句 `require("react")` 是散文，也不是依赖——这条规则最早就是被它自己误报出来的。

### 构建产物：`src/` 和 `lib/` 谁更新

有 `src/` 的插件（TypeScript 源码 + 构建出来的 `lib/`）最容易在这件事上翻车，而且两种翻车的表现一模一样——**发出去的字节没人跑过**：

| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `stale-build` | `src/` 比 `lib/` 新：构建没跑就发布了，tarball 里是上一次的产物 |

只是 warn：有可能你就是要发手改的产物（我干过）。但发之前你得知道自己在发什么。

> 早先还有一条 `hand-edited-build`（`lib/` 比 `src/` 新就报），**已删除**：正常构建本来就是先读 `src` 再写 `lib`，所以它在我自己每一个健康构建之后都会响一次。如果一条规则分不清「健康构建」和「手改产物」，它只是在教人忽略告警。

### 可追溯性：一周后你还能指出线上那包是哪份代码吗

发布是字节唯一一次离开你机器的时刻。如果这些字节既不在任何 commit 里、也没有 tag，那么一周后——包括你自己在内——没人说得清 registry 上那包是从哪份源码来的。

这不是假想：我发过一版 `1.2.7` 到 npm，仓库的 GitHub release 还停在 `1.2.6`，市场条目指向旧 tarball，维护者直接打回。

| 规则 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|
| `git-uncommitted` | 会进 tarball 的文件有未提交改动。发出去的字节不在任何 commit 里，以后复现不出来、也没法 bisect |
| `git-tag-missing` | HEAD 上没有 `v<version>` tag。发完之后这些字节的唯一记录就是 registry，GitHub release、changelog、市场条目都没法指向一个从没打过 tag 的 commit |
| `git-tag-elsewhere` | tag 存在但不在 HEAD 上：tag 和 tarball 是两份不同的字节，从那个 tag 构建出来的东西不是你刚发的东西 |
| `git-tag-unverified` | 读不到 `origin`（断网、私有仓库、没配 remote）。这是 **info**，不是 warn：提交是用 GitHub API 推的时候本地 HEAD 不是发出去的那个 commit，本地 tag 列表证明不了任何事。断网那天我有六个插件被误报「没有 tag」，六个都打了 |

都是 warn：本地试发、私有包、发完再补 tag 都合理。但「发完之后指不出是哪份代码」这件事，事后补不回来。

## 本地开发：宿主跑的到底是不是你刚改的代码

发布之前总有一段时间，插件只在你自己机器上跑。这段路比发布更容易踩空：宿主只加载 `<profile>/node_modules` 下的包，所以你改的是 `E:\...\dsh-x`，跑的是 profile 里那个入口——它可能是一个 junction、一份早就不再同步的拷贝，或者根本没有。这三种情况在宿主那边长得一模一样：插件不出现，没有报错，日志里也没有一行。

`publish_gate_link` 只读 profile 自己的三个文件回答这件事，不联网、不调包管理器、不写任何东西。

| 规则 | 严重度 | 抓什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `link-not-installed` | info | profile 的 `node_modules` 里没有这个包。新插件第一次接进宿主之前，这是正常状态 |
| `link-target-missing` | error | 链接在、目标没了（或目标里没有能解析的 `package.json`）。死掉的 junction 让宿主把包解析成空，插件静默消失——这台机器的 Web UI 就这样坏过一次 |
| `link-stale-copy` | warn | profile 里是**一份拷贝**而不是链接，且版本和工作区不同：改 `lib/` 永远不会到那边，而你在这边跑测试全绿 |
| `pnpm-store-conflict` | warn | profile 的 pnpm store 是 v10、随包的 pnpm 是 v11（或反过来）。`dsh plugin add link:` 会在装任何东西之前以 `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` 失败，而那条错误既不说 profile、也不说要匹配哪个 major |
| `patch-entry-top-level` | error | 这个包在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里是一条顶层 `- id:` 行。顶层行覆盖树里已有的条目、不新增一条：装上了、加载了、永远不出现。这个坑藏了我两个插件两周 |

链接的三种形态是分开报的：Node 对 junction 和目录符号链接都只说 `isSymbolicLink() === true`，只有 `realpathSync(p) !== p` 才说明它是 junction；普通目录则是拷贝。`mklink /J` 建 junction 不需要管理员权限，符号链接需要。

工作流：

```
1. 改完 lib/，跑 publish_gate_link(dir)
2. link-not-installed        → 建 junction（finding 的 fix 里就是能直接粘的命令）
3. link-target-missing       → 删掉旧入口，重建 junction
   link-stale-copy           → 同上；拷贝不会跟着工作区变
4. patch-entry-top-level     → 把那一行挪进 "- insert:" 块
5. pnpm-store-conflict       → 别用 pnpm，用 mklink
```

`profile` 参数可以看别的 profile（默认 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`）。测试永远用临时 profile，不碰真的那个。

没有做的：它不替你建链接、不改 profile 的 patch——和门禁其余部分一样只读，每条 finding 都带 `fix` 文案，动手是你的决定。

## 更新之前：这个新版本装上会不会坏

市场里的更新插件（`dsh-market`、`dsh-update-checker`、`dsh-onekey-update`、`dsh-plugin-auto-update`、`dsh-plugin-steward` …）做得都很好，但它们回答的是**装完之后**的问题：装上了、起不来、回滚。回滚能救回来，代价是这一次更新白做，而且坏的那一下已经发生了。

`publish_gate_update` 把顺序倒过来：**下载 → 解包到临时目录 → 跑门禁的产物层和运行时层 → 再决定要不要装。**

```
publish_gate_update({ name: "@liustack/modlens" })
→ current 0.1.0, latest 3.27.3
→ tarball: 239840 bytes
→ [warn] client-double-load: ./dsh/client.js 二次求值会重复注册工厂
```

它跑的是门禁已有的那几层，所以答案是逐条可追的：

- 入口能不能 `import`（`entry-import-failed` / `entry-missing`）
- `apply()` 能不能注册工具（`tool-none-registered`、`tool-missing-execute`）
- tarball 里有没有代码（`files-omits-lib`）、补丁在不在（`files-omits-patch`）
- 参数传错会不会抛（`tool-input-throws`，加 `fuzz: true`）
- 浏览器半边会不会加载、会不会重复注册（`client-*`）

只在 checkout 里才成立的规则（git / 市场条目 / 测试目录 / 本地链接 / 打包体积）被过滤掉——解包出来的目录没有 `.git`、没有 `README` 契约、没有 `test/`，跑那些只会把真正的结论埋掉。

三条自己的规则：

| 规则 | 严重度 | 说什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `candidate-same-version` | info | 已经是最新版，不用下载 |
| `candidate-older` | warn | registry 的 `latest` **比装着的旧**。unpublish 或误用 `--tag latest` 都会让 dist-tags 往回走，跟过去等于拿旧构建换掉能跑的安装 |
| `candidate-unavailable` | warn | 没下载成、没解开、没读到版本号。**这不是干净的结论**，detail 里明写 |

它不替你装、不替你更新——和门禁其余部分一样只读。想知道该不该更新，然后自己去 `dsh plugin add`，或者交给已有的更新插件去做。

## 一个真实的例子

对一个刚从别人那儿接手、准备发布的插件跑 `publish_gate`：

```
✗ package.json starts with a UTF-8 BOM  [utf8-bom]
    A byte-order mark makes JSON.parse throw `Unexpected token` and npm publish
    fail with a parse error that never names the BOM.
✗ files does not include "lib"  [files-omits-lib]
    The published tarball will contain no code.
✗ cordis.patch.yml has no insert row  [no-insert-row]
    A patch with only overrides never mounts your plugin. This file has 1
    top-level `- id:` row — those patch entries that already exist in the tree,
    they do not add one.
✗ lib/index.js calls require() inside an ESM module  [require-in-esm]
4 blocker(s) — fix before publishing
```

这四条里有两条是发布四个插件时真实踩到的。

## 设计取舍

- **三层，按代价排序**：清单层最便宜、先跑；产物层要起一个 npm（约 1–2 秒）；运行时层要起一个 node 子进程。前一层没过的错误通常值得先修，但三层都会跑完——一次给全，比来回问好。
- **浏览器半边单独一层，不并进运行时层**：宿主半边的失败会抛错、会有日志；浏览器半边的失败是「什么都没发生」。两者的排查路径完全不同，所以各起一个子进程、各有一组规则、各自能单独跳过（`skipTools` / `skipClient`）。
- **产物层用 `npm pack --dry-run`，不用自己推 `files` 规则**：npm 的入包规则（`main` / `exports` 强制入包、README/LICENSE 强制入包、`.npmignore` 优先级）比自己实现的准。唯一的代价是它需要这台机器上有 npm，所以跑不起来时降级成 `pack-unavailable` 而不是报错。
- **运行时层真的执行插件代码**：这是唯一能回答「装上能不能用」的办法。代价是 `apply()` 会跑，所以：假 ctx 是 Proxy 不落盘、20 秒硬超时、`skipTools` 一键跳过。
- **`--ignore-scripts`**：dry run 不跑 `prepack`，否则检查会触发一次构建。代价是清单可能和真实产物不同，所以有 `pack-script-build` 把这件事说出来。
- **发完那几十秒不算失败**：npm 收下包会先回 202，然后六十秒到几分钟里这个版本在 registry 上根本不存在。这个插件自己的 0.8.1 实测是**四分钟**才出现。所以 `publish_gate_verify` 加了 `waitMs` 轮询；一轮等不到就返回 `pending: true`——那是「还没轮到」，不是「没发成功」。单次最多等 90 秒，因为宿主 120 秒就掐掉工具调用，剩下的只能再跑一次。
- **`publish_gate_verify` 比 shasum，不比版本号**：版本号相同而字节不同（发了又改、或本地根本没发）是最常见的自欺。`npm pack --dry-run` 的 shasum 和 registry 的 `dist.shasum` 是同一套算法，所以这个比较是精确的。
  两侧 shasum 只要缺一个就**不下结论**，改报 `publish-served-unverified`（warn）——「没证明」和「证明相符」是两件事，以前的版本会把它读成 match。
- **只读**：修不修由你定，每条 finding 都带 `fix` 文案。门禁的职责是把话说清楚，不是替你做决定——所以没有 `--fix`。
- **确定性**：全部规则是文件内容、子进程或 registry/GitHub API 检查，没有 LLM 调用——一条规则答错，你可以直接看规则。
- **自举**：这个插件的测试把九个已发布插件当 fixture，断言它们在门禁下零 blocker；规则如果有任何误报倾向，测试先炸。

## 开发

```sh
node --test                      # 160 个单测
node test/integration.test.mjs   # 32 条集成断言（9 个真实插件作 fixture）
```

## License

MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-workbench

对话留在中间，代码就在手边。
DeepSeek Harness 右侧的开发工作台，用来读源码、核对改动、调试程序和整理讲解。

中文 · English　|　安装 · 功能 · 演示 · 最新发布

![对话与开发工作台的概念插画](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chengyunlai/dsh-workbench/demo-assets/readme/2026-11-03-v1/cover.png) AI 改完代码后，先在右侧打开 diff，从改动行跳回源码，再沿定义读到实现。遇到需要弄懂的代码，可以把问题交给一个讲解会话，随后在工作台翻阅卡片。文件树、编辑器和底部工具窗口可以调整大小，当前对话始终留在旁边。 ## 快速开始 1. 在 DeepSeek Harness 的插件管理器选择「安装插件」，输入 `@yunlai/dsh-workbench`，启用「开发工作台」。 2. 打开一个已注册的 Git 项目对话，展开右侧工具区，在「开始」或「更多工具」中选择「开发工作台」。 3. 从文件树打开文件。在支持的源码中按 `F12` 跳定义，或从底部打开「变更」核对 diff。 在线安装用户可在插件详情检查版本并更新，随后重载或重启 Harness。当前发布包要求 Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` 或更新版本，运行环境要求 Node.js `22.14.0` 或更新版本。[下载 ZIP](https://github.com/Chengyunlai/dsh-workbench/releases/latest) · [升级说明](UPGRADING.md)

## 工作台能做什么 | 想做的事 | 在工作台里怎么做 | | --- | --- | | **读懂源码** | 用文件树和内容查找定位代码。标签保留各文件的阅读位置，支持语法高亮、折叠、同词高亮、定义跳转和前进／后退。右键标签可关闭当前、其他或全部文件。 | | **看清 Python 类关系** | 从文件树工具栏或 Python 源码右键菜单打开层级树或分栏图。查看继承、抽象类、显式 Protocol 基类及有源码依据的工厂返回关联，点击节点或方法跳回源码。类关系目前仅支持 Python，处于 Beta 阶段。 | | **阅读文档和图片** | 对话中的 Markdown 可进入工作台预览，也可切回源码。预览支持 YAML 标题、标签和字段、代码块高亮与文件链接。文件标签还可预览 PNG、SVG、ICNS 等图片和图标。 | | **核对 Git 改动** | 分组查看已暂存、工作区变更和未跟踪文件，阅读逐行 diff、提交图与提交详情。双击 diff 行可跳到当前源码。可把选中的 diff 行作为修改任务或讲解材料交给新会话。 | | **检查真实执行** | 启动调试或接入已有进程，设置断点、单步并切换栈帧。暂停时可悬浮查看变量、展开对象、查看行内值及求值，也可一次清理全部断点。 | | **运行项目命令** | 从底部打开终端，复用 Harness 终端服务在当前会话的工作区运行命令。切换到查找、变更、历史、记忆卡片或调试时，编辑区仍可见。 | Python 类图基于静态源码分析。定义跳转可打开语言服务返回的受支持库源码和声明文件，显示为只读库标签。[类关系说明](USAGE.md#python-类关系图) · [导航限制](USAGE.md#导航行为与限制) ## 讲给我听与记忆卡片 例如读到一个 `stream()` 方法，想知道 SSE 字节在哪里分帧、何时变成模型事件。右键文件选「讲给我听」，输入问题。新会话会尝试沿源码和具体输入讲清链路，把同一份完整解释保存成一张卡。卡片先概括问题，末尾用一道回忆题请你复述机制或预测边界情况。 底部「记忆卡片」按归档目录分组，可组合搜索标题、摘要、标签、来源与路径。卡片是项目中的 Markdown 文件，默认存放在 `.dsh/cards/`。关联文件的卡片按源码最近两级目录归档，未关联源码的归入 `general/`，已有卡片也可按来源在索引里归组。[卡片使用指南](USAGE.md#记忆卡片) ![记忆卡片的 YAML 元数据、问题概括、示例与回忆题](screenshots/readme-v1.4.1/memory-card-preview.png)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# GSAP Skills for DeepSeek Harness

**`@chonwai/dsh-gsap-skills`** packages the eight official [GSAP skills](https://github.com/greensock/gsap-skills)
as a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) bundle, with **four documented factual corrections**.
Each `SKILL.md` is registered as a runtime skill, so a session can load
`gsap-core`, `gsap-timeline`, `gsap-scrolltrigger`, `gsap-plugins`,
`gsap-utils`, `gsap-react`, `gsap-frameworks` and `gsap-performance` on demand.

An independent community integration: not affiliated with, sponsored by or
endorsed by GreenSock or the GSAP project. “GSAP” and “GreenSock” are trademarks
of GreenSock, Inc. The skill documentation is MIT-licensed; **the GSAP library
itself is not included and is not MIT** — you install GSAP in your project under
GreenSock's own terms.

**Scope rule (read this first):** this bundle registers in the host/global skill
layer. The Web app mounts `skill-filesystem` inside the agent preset's scope and
disables the host-level filesystem row, so a file-level copy of any of these
skills under `~/.agents/skills`, `$DSH_HOME/skills`, or a project
`.agents/skills` lives in the nearer preset layer and wins the name outright —
**the bundle cannot override it**. Move the file copies out of the skills root
to activate the bundle; see *Migrating from a file-level install* below. A
profile install does not mean the row is the winning catalog entry while such a
copy exists.

## Quick start

Install from **Plugins → Add plugin → Install a third-party plugin** with
`https://github.com/Chonwai/dsh-gsap-skills#v1.0.3`, accept **Enable now**, then
**restart DSH** and open a session; load `/gsap-core`. Other channels (release
tarball, agent/`plugin_manager`, future npm), verification, layer migration and
troubleshooting: [docs/DISTRIBUTION.md](docs/DISTRIBUTION.md).

## Demo

[`demo/`](demo/) is a self-contained interactive page built with the bundle's own
guidance: a hero entrance timeline, scroll-revealed skill cards, and a pinned,
scroll-scrubbed Timeline → ScrollTrigger → Plugins strip, with reduced-motion and
no-CDN fallbacks. Serve the repo with `python3 -m http.server 8000` and open
`/demo/`; it loads GSAP 3.15.1 from a pinned CDN, so it needs network.

![Interactive demo: dark hero, eight skill cards and a pinned scroll strip](assets/demo.png)

## What it provides

| Skill | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `gsap-core` | `gsap.to/from/fromTo`, easing, duration, stagger, defaults, `matchMedia` |
| `gsap-timeline` | sequencing, the position parameter, nesting, playback |
| `gsap-scrolltrigger` | scroll-linked animation, pinning, scrub, triggers |
| `gsap-plugins` | registration, Flip, Draggable, ScrollSmoother, SplitText, SVG, eases |
| `gsap-utils` | `clamp`, `mapRange`, `normalize`, `interpolate`, `random`, `snap`, `wrap`, `pipe` |
| `gsap-react` | `useGSAP`, refs, `gsap.context()`, cleanup |
| `gsap-frameworks` | Vue, Nuxt, Svelte, SvelteKit lifecycle and cleanup |
| `gsap-performance` | transforms, layout thrashing, `will-change`, batching |

Plus `skills/llms.txt` (upstream's skill index). The host half registers all
eight with `resourceBase` pointing at each skill's own directory. There is no
client half, no settings/Config schema, no prompt section, no telemetry, no
runtime dependency and no network/process/write access — the module only reads
its own files.

## What is corrected

Applied at vendor time by `tools/apply-corrections.mjs`; every replacement is
quoted with its upstream issue or source evidence in
[docs/KNOWN-UPSTREAM-ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN-UPSTREAM-ISSUES.md):

1. **`gsap-core` transform order** — the documented alias order
   `translation → scale → rotationX/Y → skew → rotation` is wrong; GSAP 3.15.1
   CSSPlugin composes `translation → rotation → rotationY → rotationX → skew →
   scale`.
2. **`gsap-timeline` position parameter** — removed the wrong “(default)”
   markers; omitting the parameter appends at the end of the timeline, while
   `">"` means “after the most recently added animation”.
3. **`gsap-scrolltrigger` refreshPriority** — direction was backwards; **higher
   numbers refresh first**, so the first section on the page gets a higher
   number.
4. **`gsap-frameworks` duplicate `type Plugins`** — the second declaration is
   renamed `type PluginName = keyof PluginMap`, with `PluginModule`,
   `PluginExport` and `lazyLoadPlugin` updated.

Documented but not patched: `easeReverse` (GSAP 3.15) is missing from the skills,
and the Nuxt example's cleanup runs in `onMounted` (issue #23) — the example is
not vendored. Both are recorded in the known-issues file. The fail-loud vendor
script stops if upstream fixes any expected string, so a correction cannot
silently rot.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.2-rc.1** (`engines.dsh: ">=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0"`).
- Node.js **>= 22** (inherited from the Harness).
- A managed DSH profile (the Desktop app's `desktop` profile, or a CLI-managed
  profile).
- **GSAP itself is not included.** The skills only document how to use it; each
  user's project installs `gsap` (and any plugins) from npm under GreenSock's
  license.

## Install

All three routes are in [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md):

1. **Plugins page** (recommended): Plugins → Add plugin → install a
   third-party plugin → paste this directory's absolute path.
2. **`plugin_manager` tool**:
   `plugin_manager(action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/to/dsh-gsap-skills")`.
3. **Manual copy** (advanced, only when Plugin Manager is unavailable): copy
   the checkout into the profile's `node_modules` and add it to the profile's
   dependency/bundle list by hand; INSTALL.md has the exact steps and the
   rollback.

**Restart DSH after installing or toggling.** Profile bundle rows are composed
when the DSH host boots; a new session or a page reload does not re-compose
them, and `plugin_manager` showing installed/enabled is profile state, not proof
that the running host mounted the row.

## Usage

In a session, load a skill with the `skill` tool or its `/` gesture:

- `/gsap-core` — “how do I animate this element with GSAP?”
- `/gsap-timeline` — “sequence these steps, and what does `"<"` do?”
- `/gsap-scrolltrigger` — “pin this section and scrub the animation”
- `/gsap-plugins` — “register SplitText and lazy-load Draggable”
- `/gsap-react` — “clean up this animation in React”
- `/gsap-frameworks` — “Vue/Nuxt/Svelte lifecycle cleanup”
- `/gsap-performance` — “this list animation janks; why?”
- `/gsap-utils` — “clamp and snap values with gsap.utils”

Natural language works too: “use the GSAP timeline skill and review this
sequence”. The skill body is the upstream documentation; it does not install
packages or execute animation code.

## Migrating from a file-level install (required for the bundle to take effect)

Three facts from the DSH source decide which copy wins:

1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app/presets/standard.patch.yml` mounts
   `skill-filesystem` **inside the agent preset's scope**.
2. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app/cordis.patch.yml` **disables the host-level
   `skill-filesystem` row** ("presets own local discovery").
3. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill` merges the global layer with the viewing scope's
   chain: **the nearest layer's entry wins a duplicate name outright**, and rank
   only orders duplicates inside one layer.

This bundle is a host row, so it registers in the **global** layer. Any
file-level copy of these skills under `~/.agents/skills`, `$DSH_HOME/skills`, or
a project `.agents/skills` is discovered by the preset's provider and lives in
the **nearer scoped layer**, which wins unconditionally; the bundle cannot
override it. Preflight:

```bash
for d in ~/.agents/skills "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills"; do
  for s in gsap-core gsap-timeline gsap-scrolltrigger gsap-plugins gsap-utils gsap-react gsap-frameworks gsap-performance; do
    test -d "$d/$s" && echo "WARNING: file-level copy will shadow the bundle: $d/$s"
  done
done
```

Move the copies out (this package never does it for you):

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.dsh-backup
for s in gsap-core gsap-timeline gsap-scrolltrigger gsap-plugins gsap-utils gsap-react gsap-frameworks gsap-performance; do
  test -d ~/.agents/skills/$s && mv ~/.agents/skills/$s ~/.dsh-backup/$s-$(date +%F)
  test -d "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/$s" && mv "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/$s" ~/.dsh-backup/$s-dsh-$(date +%F)
done
```

Project-local `<repo>/.agents/skills/gsap-*` copies must be moved too. The
filesystem watcher picks the removal up at the next pre-step (no restart needed
for the removal); installing or toggling the bundle itself needs a DSH restart.

## Verified vs unverified

Every claim below is executable from the package directory. **Verified** on
macOS 27.2 (arm64), Node 22.21.1, on 2026-11-09:

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Offline gate | `bash tests/offline-check.sh` | `RESULT: PASS (90 checks)` |
| Host smoke | `node tests/host-smoke.mjs` | `11/11 passed` |
| Registry smoke (optional) | `node tests/registry-smoke.mjs` with `DSH_ASAR_MODULES` pointing at an extracted `app.asar`’s `@deepseek-ai` | `3/3 passed` |
| Corrections | `node tools/apply-corrections.mjs --check` | `corrections: 10/10 verified` |
| JS syntax | `node --check lib/index.js` | exit 0 |
| Vendor idempotency | re-run `tools/vendor-upstream.sh --from-dir /tmp/gsap-skills --ref aed9cfd3… --no-tests` | byte-identical `skills/`, `checksums.txt`, `provenance.json` |

The optional registry test prints `SKIP` and exits 0 when no extracted DSH
package tree is present; **SKIP is not verification, only a real `PASS` counts.**

**Unverified:**

- **Live activation on other machines.** The maintainer's machine has the
  bundle installed and live: `skill("gsap-core")` loads from the installed
  package on v1.0.2/1.0.3 (after the required DSH restart). Verify the same on
  yours — the loaded `Base directory` must point into the package, not
  `~/.agents`.
- **Plugins page rendering** of the localized title/description and the icon.
- **GSAP runtime behaviour.** The corrections were verified against GSAP 3.15.1
  source (and the upstream issues), not by running each animation in a browser;
  no GSAP library is bundled.
- **Upstream fixes.** Issues #20/#21/#23 were open on 2026-11-09; the vendored
  corrections are this bundle's, not upstream's.
- **Non-macOS hosts** and DSH versions other than 0.2.2-rc.1.
- **No npm release:** installed from a checkout only (`private: true`).

## Known upstream issues

Full quotes, source evidence and issue links:
[docs/KNOWN-UPSTREAM-ISSUES.md](docs/KNOWN-UPSTREAM-ISSUES.md).
Series conventions: [docs/SERIES.md](docs/SERIES.md).

## Development

```bash
npm test                  # offline gate; prints RESULT: PASS
npm run check             # node --check lib/, tests/, tools/
npm run smoke             # host + optional registry smoke
npm run corrections-check # verify the four corrections in the vendored tree
```

Re-vendoring (deterministic, idempotent):

```bash
bash tools/vendor-upstream.sh aed9cfd3277740755f6bfc1155c7aa645403b760 \
  --repo /path/to/gsap-skills
# or from an existing checkout:
bash tools/vendor-upstream.sh --from-dir /path/to/gsap-skills \
  --ref aed9cfd3277740755f6bfc1155c7aa645403b760
```

It copies the eight `SKILL.md` files and `llms.txt`, applies the corrections
(failing if an expected original string is gone), rewrites `checksums.txt` and
`provenance.json`, and runs the gates. Update the `Source:` line in
[NOTICE](NOTICE) if the commit changes: the offline gate fails when `NOTICE` and
`provenance.json.ref` disagree. There is no build step.

## Repository layout

```
lib/index.js                 host half: read, parse, register, dispose
cordis.patch.yml             one insert row: id gsap -> @chonwai/dsh-gsap-skills
skills/gsap-*/SKILL.md       the eight vendored skills (four corrections applied)
```

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-py-codeact

A CodeAct agent loop for the DeepSeek Harness: the model's action space is a **persistent IPython session**, and harness tools are bridged into it as awaitables.

```python
# one cell
from __dsh__.tools import read, glob
import pandas as pd, io

paths = await glob(pattern="data/*.csv")
frames = [pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(await read(file_path=p))) for p in paths]
df = pd.concat(frames)

# a later cell — `df` is still bound, and so are `read`, `_`, `Out[1]`, everything
df.groupby("region").revenue.sum().nlargest(3)
```

`python` is the only tool the model can call directly. Everything else lives in `__dsh__.tools`, so the action space really is one tool — the CodeAct shape.

By default, cells run through `InteractiveShell.run_cell_async`, so magics, `transform_cell`, top-level `await`, execution history, and IPython's traceback formatter all come for free. The shell setup and the LLM-specific touches below follow [`CNSeniorious000/temporary-mcp-servers:ipython-mcp.py`](https://github.com/CNSeniorious000/temporary-mcp-servers/blob/main/ipython-mcp.py).

## How it differs from dsh's built-in Code Mode

Both offer programmatic tool calling. This plugin keeps IPython as the model’s action space.

| | Code Mode (`run_code`) | this plugin (`python`) |
|---|---|---|
| Language | TypeScript (or Python via a backend) | Python, in IPython |
| State between calls | runtime-dependent; persistent execution is supported | **persists** for the session |
| Layer | a `PtcRuntime` seam provider | an ordinary tool plugin |
| Tool surface | a generated `tools` global | the `__dsh__.tools` module |
| Exclusivity | `tools.mode: code`, enforced by the registry | `mode: code`, via prompt assembly + a guard |
| Result | program logs + return value | tagged stdout / return / traceback / note |

DSH 0.2.1 supports persistent PTC execution (`persistent-in-memory`). This plugin remains an ordinary tool because it provides an IPython-specific interaction model, including magics, history and introspection; persistence alone no longer requires a separate tool.

That tradeoff is real and inherited: the interpreter's live state cannot be reconstructed from a session replay. What IS in the log is every cell's source and every bridged tool call, which is enough to audit what happened.

## `__dsh__` — the seam

`__dsh__` is a real package in `sys.modules`, so every import form resolves:

```python
from __dsh__.tools import glob, grep  # the usual one
import __dsh__.tools as T  # T.read(...)
from __dsh__ import tools  # tools.read(...)
```

A dunder-named package reads as harness-owned, survives `%reset`, and leaves the obvious name `tools` free for the model's own variables.

**Each tool is a real `async def`.** dsh's description becomes its `__doc__` and its parameters become a keyword-only signature, so the REPL's own introspection does the explaining:

```
In [1]: read?
Signature: read(*, file_path: 'str', offset: 'int' = ..., limit: 'int' = ...) -> 'ReadOutput'
Docstring:
Read a file from the workspace. Results include line numbers…

Parameters:
    file_path: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.
    offset: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.
    limit: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.
```

The block renders the same picture: one parameter per line, its description as a trailing comment, the tool's own as a docstring — so what a model reads in the prompt and what it gets from `?` are the same text, from the same source. Annotations are rendered host-side by dsh's own exported renderers, so there is no second JSON-Schema mapper to drift.

The **return** type comes from the tool's own `output` schema, by way of `ctx.tools.sdkSchemas(scope)` — the projection that carries it. It is the one annotation the model cannot recover by reading harder: a wrong argument fails loudly at the call, while an unknown return shape is only discoverable by calling once and printing the result, which costs a whole turn per tool. A tool that declares no output schema still renders `Any`; claiming a type nobody declared would be worse than admitting ignorance.

Every object in that schema is declared as a named `TypedDict` above the signatures, and an output that is a choice of shapes becomes a union of named branches. For a bridged MCP tool the schema described here is the payload, not the transport wrapper — see below; `dict[str, Any]` would say a dict arrives without saying which keys, which is the one thing a return annotation exists to say.

```python
class BashOutput1(TypedDict):
    kind: Literal["background"]
    jobId: str

class BashOutput2Stdout(TypedDict):
    text: str
    truncated: bool

class BashOutput2(TypedDict):
    kind: Literal["foreground"]
    exitCode: int | None
    stdout: BashOutput2Stdout

async def bash(*, command: str, run_in_background: bool = ...) -> BashOutput1 | BashOutput2: ...
```

`jsonSchemaToPy` cannot do this and says so — it is context-free, and naming a `TypedDict` needs the render context `renderToolsSdkPy` supplies. With nowhere to hang a declaration it degrades every object to `dict[str, Any]`, which on a stock catalogue is the return type of every tool but one. `renderType`, the context-carrying core, is not exported, so the context is borrowed instead: `renderToolsSdkPy` is called with the parameters stripped — the one input it renders without allocating a class, which makes every class it emits an output class — and the block it returns is read back for the declarations and each tool's return text. The `Literal`s, the nested classes, the collision suffixes and the Unicode identifier rules are then dsh's own rather than a second mapper drifting alongside them. The binding set is resent with every cell, because restrictions and mid-conversation tool changes can move a tool in or out between calls.

### The MCP wrapper does not reach the cell

dsh's MCP client resolves a call to `{ content, structuredContent? }` — the protocol's block array plus the server's own payload — and declares exactly that as the tool's output. That wrapper is transport, not API: `content`'s text duplicates the payload, and an image inside it is re-attached to the conversation separately, so a cell can do nothing with it. Handed the wrapper, a model writes `r["structuredContent"]["result"]` — and spends a call discovering it has to.

So the bridge unwraps, and the signature describes what the cell actually receives:

```python
mcp.review.search(*, q: str) -> McpReviewSearchOutput   # the payload, not the wrapper
mcp.email.ping() -> str                                 # no declared payload: the text blocks, joined
```

A server that declares no output schema is the common case in the wild, and its result really is just text — one text block, in every one of the 4142 MCP results measured across six trials, which is why this is a `str` and not a `list[str]` that would cost an `r[0]` at every call site to preserve a boundary that never appears. A result carrying no text block at all resolves to the empty string: an image there is re-attached to the conversation and read on the next step, so there was never anything for the cell to receive. One divergence is possible and belongs to the server: a tool that declares an output schema but omits `structuredContent` on some call resolves to that call's text, where the signature promised the payload type.

Unwrapping keys off the tool's declared output schema, not off the value that comes back: a tool whose own payload happens to be `{content: [...]}` is not wrapping anything, and replacing its value with joined text would change what that tool returns with nothing to say so. This deliberately differs from Code Mode, which hands the whole envelope to `tools.name(args)`.

### MCP tools work, with nothing special

MCP servers register into the same `ctx.tools` registry as everything else, so they arrive in `__dsh__.tools` like any other binding and dispatch through the same pipeline. They are *presented* grouped, under one `mcp`:

```python
from __dsh__.tools import mcp

data = await mcp.gh.github_graphql(query="{ viewer { login } }")
```

dsh names them `mcp__<server>__<rawName>`, and with a hundred mounted that import line was most of the prompt block while every call site respelled its server. The flat names stay bound — `mcp` is how they are shown, not what they are — so a cell written before this still runs, `import *` still binds them, and only the listings drop them. A name the grouping cannot serve is still shown: dsh hashes a public name that needed normalising and the cut can land before the second `__`, and a raw name that is a true dunder is refused by `__getattr__`; either way the flat name is the only one that works. They are kept out of `dir(__dsh__.tools)` for the same reason the block stopped printing them; a name the grouping cannot reach (dsh hashes a public name that needed normalising, and the cut can land before the second `__`) stays listed, because `mcp` is not another way to say it. The block lists them one module per section — `# __dsh__.tools`, then `# __dsh__.tools.mcp.<server>` — because that is what they are. It used to declare `Protocol` stubs with `self`-taking methods, copied from dsh's own SDK renderer; that renderer describes a singleton object (`tools: Tools`), while this grouping is a real package, so the stub claimed a binding that never happens. `mcp.exa.web_search?` answers `(*, query: str) -> str`, and the block now says the same thing.

It is a real package, so a server can be imported as a module — which reads better than `mcp.` at every call site when a cell leans on one server:

```python
from __dsh__.tools.mcp.calendar import list_events, create_event
from __dsh__.tools.mcp import calendar          # or the server itself
```

The deep form is why each server gets a `sys.modules` entry of its own: `__getattr__` can serve `from __dsh__.tools.mcp import calendar`, but not `from __dsh__.tools.mcp.calendar import list_events` — the import machinery looks that one up as a module. No meta path finder is needed; registration is enough.

`mcp` and its server modules are live views of the catalogue, not snapshots of the cell they were imported in: a restriction or a reconnecting server moves tools in and out between calls, and unlike a single tool the model has no reason to ever import the namespace twice. (A name pulled OUT with `from ... import` is a snapshot, as it is for any Python import.) The name is reserved — a native tool called `mcp` is not bound, nor is one called `ToolCallError`, nor any whose name starts with `_`. The prompt block mirrors all three, because a block that imports a name the kernel never binds is an `ImportError` on the first line the model copies.

dsh's MCP client is explicitly aware of this route — its canonical value "retains the complete JSON MCP blocks and optional structured content for programmatic and Code Mode callers" — and the sub-call logs a `SUBTOOL` row like any other.

Worth contrasting: Anthropic's server-side [programmatic tool calling](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling) is *not* compatible with MCP tools. Owning the bridge host-side is what buys this.

A raw MCP name is a routine place to find a hyphen — dsh normalises over `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, so `-` survives, and `-` is legal in no Python identifier. Such a tool is bound under BOTH spellings: its own, and the `-`→`_` fold that the listings show and the block spells. `mcp.notion.API_patch_block_children(...)` dispatches to `mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children`, and an existing `getattr(mcp.notion, "API-patch-block-children")` keeps working. The fold never displaces a real tool: a server exposing both `a-b` and `a_b` keeps `a_b` meaning `a_b`, and both stay listed.

Measured before adding it: on a 20-task benchmark run, 676 of 17030 dispatches (4.0%) went to twelve hyphenated tools, all from one server, and `API-patch-block-children` was the single most-dispatched tool of the whole catalogue — each call site paying for a `getattr`, with no signature in the block to go with it, because an unspellable name was excluded from the listing entirely. Across the 208 distinct tool names those runs dispatched, no fold collided with another fold or shadowed an existing name.

(Folding fixes only what a substitution can reach. A keyword (`class`) or a digit-leading name (`123tool`) is unspellable for reasons no rewrite fixes, and those keep the `getattr` route — `getattr(__dsh__.tools, "class")` — which the block still points at when there is one.)

## Exclusive mode

`mode: code` (the default) makes `python` the only directly callable tool:

- a `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall listener filters `assembly.tools` down to `python`, so the other schemas never enter the request;
- a `ctx.tools.guard()` denies a model-direct call to anything else and names the route back (`from __dsh__.tools import <name>`) — presentation alone is not enforcement, and a bare rejection reads as a broken deployment. Sub-dispatches carry a `parent` token and are exempt.

`ctx.tools.restrict()` cannot do the first job: it masks *global* tools only, and in a preset composition the tools are scope-local — "scoped registrations remain visible". The assemble waterfall is the layer that owns the model-facing list.

The rule ships as its own prompt section at order 99, ahead of the 100–199 tool-guidance band, for the reason Code Mode orders its own code-only rule there: the model should read which tools it may call before it reads what each one is for. (Measured: moving it out of the band took it from character 4129 to 170.)

Set `mode: both` to keep the native schemas alongside — useful while debugging a composition, not the CodeAct shape.

## The `CodeAct` card

The browser half registers `tool.call.toolview` under `key: 'python'`, giving the call its own card:

```
CodeAct · count the markdown files at the root
┌ python                                  copy ┐
│ from __dsh__.tools import glob                │
│ print(len(await glob(pattern="*.md")))        │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   Glob · *.md          ← native SUBTOOL row, untouched
```

The code body is the shipped `CodeBlock` primitive with `lang: "python"`, so the highlighting, the language label, and the copy button are dsh's own.

**A client half is required, because nothing host-side can affect this row.** `toolRowModel` ignores the `presentCall` view entirely and derives everything from the tool NAME plus raw args:

```js
title   = TOOL_TITLES[toolName] ?? VARIANT_TITLES[classifyTool(toolName)]  // unknown → "Tool call"
summary = variant === 'others' ? `${toolName} · ${base}` : base
body    = deriveBody(variant, argsRaw)                                     // unknown → raw args JSON
```

and `classifyTool` reads a hardcoded map in which `run_code: 'code'` is the only entry that reaches the syntax-highlighted branch (with `lang: "typescript"` also hardcoded). `run_code` is a reserved name a plugin may not take. Upstream fix proposed in [discussion #4724](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/4724): let the call view carry `kind: 'execute'` plus a language.

**SUBTOOL nesting survives by construction.** `ToolCallBranch` renders `block.subCalls` as *siblings* of the slot occupant:

```js
children: [renderSlot('tool.call.toolview', owner, { entryKey: toolName, fallback }), children]
```

so a registered toolview replaces the card body only. The slot contract says the same: "registering is additive for your own tool".

The card is hand-written in the client module system's factory form (a classic script registering a CJS factory) rather than bundled — this package has no build step, and the card needs only React plus one shipped primitive.

The key is the literal name `python`; a custom `toolName` falls back to the generic row.

## SUBTOOL rows come free

Each bridged call appends the same two session events Code Mode uses:

```js
session.append('tool/code-dispatch-start', { rootCallId, parentCallId, subCallId, name, arguments })
session.append('tool/code-dispatch',       { ...same, isError, content })
```

They pair by `subCallId` (`<parent>:py:<n>`), and the settle event carries `tool/result`'s own vocabulary (`content` + `isError`) — so the trajectory UI renders them through the exact code path it uses for native calls, as `SUBTOOL` rows under the `python` call. No client change.

Both events have to land inside one open turn: the v3/v4 read path rejects a `tool/ptc-dispatch` found outside one and refuses to load the session at all. So nothing is left in flight when a cell ends. The cell owns an `AbortController` — the signal every sub-call of it runs under — and `execute` aborts that and then waits for whatever is still outstanding before it releases the shell's slot. A call parked on an approval is answered `cancelled` rather than performed hours later inside no turn, and its settle is still logged, in the same turn as its `-start`. Code Mode's `run_code` holds its run open the same way, which is what makes this contract hold there too.

Both types are in `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`, so reusing them is supported. Note that an out-of-repo plugin cannot invent a *new* event type: the persistence read path refuses a log containing a type outside that set unless the event is marked `ignorable`, and a registration surface for downstream events is explicitly deferred upstream.

Sub-dispatches carry the outer execution's `parent` token, so they re-enter the complete `pre-execute → guards → execute → post-execute → result` pipeline. The sandbox and approval stack still gate every tool call made from inside a cell. Settled sub-calls also use the public `tools/ptc-dispatch-log` waterfall and preserve result metadata and structured errors.

## What the model gets

- **Magics.** `%whos` to recall what it has bound, `%timeit`, `%run script.py`, `%%writefile`, `obj?` / `obj??`, `%cd`. Cheap self-orientation in a session it has partly forgotten.
- **History.** `store_history=True`, so `_`, `__`, `_i3`, `Out[n]` all work.
- **Redundant-import hints.** When an `import` rebinds a name to the object it already held, the result carries `` `json` is already imported in this session — no need to re-import it. `` A model driving a persistent REPL re-imports constantly; telling it is cheaper than letting it burn a line every cell. (Implemented with a `dict` subclass that watches top-level `STORE_NAME` and checks the preceding opcode was `IMPORT_NAME`/`IMPORT_FROM`, so `x = x` does not trip it.)
- **Readable reprs.** `objprint` + IPython's `pretty` for objects whose own `__repr__` is `object.__repr__` — an agent reading values needs structure, not `<Foo object at 0x…>`.
- **Tagged observations.** `<stdout>`, `<stderr>`, `<return>`, `<traceback>`, `<note>` — with four things possibly present at once, the model needs to know which is which. A plain successful value stays bare.
- **Introspection over prompt text.** `read?` for one tool's full description, `dir(__dsh__.tools)` for the list — `mcp` rather than the hundred flat names under it, matching what the block printed — then `dir(mcp)` and `dir(mcp.<server>)` for those, and `%whos` for its own bindings. `__all__` is left alone: it is what `import *` binds, not what the model is shown — so it carries every flat name the listings drop, and `ToolCallError`, which no listing shows because it is not a tool but which `except ToolCallError` needs after an `import *`. What it introspects matches what the block showed it: the listing carries `mcp` rather than the hundred flat names under it, and an optional parameter renders `= ...` there as it does here — `inspect.signature` uses `repr`, and `repr(...)` is `Ellipsis`, which is what `read?` used to say.

## Streaming execution

In DSH Web's **Plugins** page, open **dsh-py-codeact** and enable **Streaming execution** to execute stable Python statements while the model generates its tool arguments. Both modes use the same CodeAct preset and `python` tool. The switch applies from the next model step without restarting the Python namespace; an active cell keeps its execution mode. Streaming requires DSH 0.2.2 or later, `mode: code`, and session persistence. It is off by default.

Leave `streaming` unset on the preset's plugin row to follow this profile preference. An explicit `true` or `false` overrides it for that preset:

```yaml
- name: dsh-py-codeact
  config:
    streaming: true
```

The live preference belongs to the profile's `py-codeact-settings` entry, installed by the [bundle patch](cordis.patch.yml). The execution row retains ordinary configuration lifecycle rules; editing its explicit override can remount the plugin and discard interpreter state.

The plugin reads the same `agent/assistant-stream` events as the WebUI. [partial-python](https://github.com/promplate/partial-python) executes each stable statement once in the existing namespace; the final tool invocation joins that execution. Streaming execution uses the host's public plugin APIs. Source admission passes through the normal tool policy pipeline and is persisted before execution; bridged tools retain the step's tool set, sandbox policy, and approval checks. Streaming admission authorizes code that is still arriving, so retain whole-cell mode when approval must inspect the complete program.

Early admission uses the internal `<toolName>_stream` capability (`python_stream` by default). Tool-name policies must cover this capability as well as the final `python` call; approving the final call cannot undo earlier effects. Durable context notices record admission and its accepted outcome, so a restart can report effects even when no complete assistant tool call was committed.

Streaming uses raw Python with top-level `await`. Use `print(...)` for output and `help(...)` for introspection; IPython magics, shell escapes, history updates, and automatic final-expression echo are unavailable. Stable statements inside `if`, `with`, and `async with` may run before the block closes. Loops, `try`, function definitions, and other unsupported compound kinds wait for their complete statement. Open contexts span source generation: time spent waiting for tokens counts toward `asyncio.timeout()`, and locks or transactions may stay open longer.

Truncation, malformed arguments, disconnects, and cancellation abort pending source and unwind open contexts before the step settles. Earlier effects remain; the plugin never reruns the source to recover or automatically retries a model attempt after execution starts. CPU-bound code still uses the kernel's interrupt escalation. A restored admission with no conclusive result is reported to the model as an unknown outcome, not as proof that nothing ran; interpreter memory is not restored.

One streamed Python call is supported per response. Other direct tools remain unavailable in exclusive CodeAct mode. The generated tool description and SDK instructions explain these rules to the model. A configured `python` or `command` interpreter must supply [`partial-python~=0.1.0`](https://github.com/promplate/partial-python) as well as IPython and objprint; the default `uv` setup installs them from the worker's PEP 723 metadata.

## Cancellation

An aborted turn sends an in-band `interrupt` frame, cancelling the running cell at any `await` point. `run_cell_async` catches the `CancelledError` itself, so the model is told plainly (`InterruptedError: the harness cancelled this cell. State is intact; the cell did not finish.`) rather than handed a raw traceback it might read as a bug in its own code. The session and every binding survive.

A pure CPU loop (`while True: pass`) never reaches an await point. After `hardInterruptMs` (default 5s) the interpreter is SIGKILLed and the next call respawns it; that observation is prefixed with `[the interpreter was restarted; every earlier binding is gone]` so the model does not keep referring to variables that no longer exist.

## Known limitations

- **Native writes are not captured.** stdout/stderr are captured at the Python level, so `print` is captured but a subprocess writing to fd 1 is not. Use `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)`, or `%run`. (Anything that does reach fd 1/2 — including IPython's own colored traceback, deliberately routed there — is retained only for the crash message.)
- **Scope is not optional.** The visible tool set comes from `ctx.tools.sdkSchemas(scope)` — the scope being the agent. Omitting it yields the *global* view, which in a preset composition holds only host-registered tools; the preset's own `read`/`bash`/`edit` live in the agent scope and vanish. The prompt section reads `assembly.scope`, and the kernel's name list is resent with every cell (restrictions and mid-conversation tool changes can move a tool in or out between calls).
- **Pick a `toolName` nothing else answers to.** With an MCP IPython server also mounted, a model told to "use the python tool" reaches for `mcp__py__ipython_execute_code` — which has no `tools` binding — and then reports that your tool does not exist.
- **A shape Python cannot name stays vague.** A field whose key is not a valid identifier degrades its own class back to `dict[str, Any]` rather than emitting a body that will not parse — the tool stays callable and only that one annotation goes quiet. A parameter named `self` is now just a parameter: every tool renders as a module-level function, so no enclosing signature has spent that name. A tool name Python refuses gets a class under one it accepts (`123tool` → `Tool123toolOutput`), rather than the `class 123toolOutput` that would be a SyntaxError taking the whole block with it; that tool has no `async def` line, but it is still bound, and `123tool?` names the same class. A schema with no declared properties still renders `Any`; claiming a type nobody declared would be worse.
- **Cold start.** The PEP 723 environment is resolved on first use (`uv python find --script`). Warm afterwards; pass `python` to skip it.

  The interpreter is then spawned **directly**, never behind `uv run --script`. A wrapper stays in the process tree as the interpreter's parent: when it exits first, the interpreter is reparented to init, the handle the host holds reports an exit, and a perfectly live kernel looks dead — so the next cell respawns and the session's state vanishes with an `[the interpreter was restarted]` notice nothing actually caused. `alive` is likewise tracked from the exit event rather than read off `proc.killed`, which Node sets on any `kill()` call, including a signal the process survived.
- **Containment, not a security boundary.** A separate process with a curated environment, but model code can `import os`. Treat a session on this preset as shell access.
- **One shell per agent.** Under `danger-full-access`, a subagent can reuse its parent's process — sharing its event loop, `sys.modules`, installed packages and `__dsh__.shared` — while keeping its own globals and tool catalogue. Confined sessions use separate interpreters.
- **`__dsh__.shared`** is the one deliberate crack in that isolation: a module every agent in the process can read and write, for handing live objects across a fan-out with no serialization and no tokens.
- Shells close with their session; the process goes when the last agent pointing at it does.

## Environment

By default the kernel gets an allowlist — `PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TERM` — not the empty environment the worker-thread runtime uses. CPython running IPython needs a profile dir and a `PATH` for shell escapes; the point is excluding ambient credentials, which an allowlist does just as well. `inheritEnv: true` passes the whole harness environment.

Execution requires DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 or later with `sandboxPolicy` and `subprocess` services. The Python interpreter runs through the host’s managed subprocess provider, including descendant termination, and resolves the session’s `sandboxPolicy` and uses `ctx.sandbox.confine` in `read-only` and `workspace-write` modes. Only an explicit `danger-full-access` policy skips confinement. A missing policy/provider fails closed. Interpreter provisioning is host setup; model cells run inside the confined process. The initial cwd comes from the working-directory service when available; the immutable session cwd still defines the sandbox boundary.

Changing a session’s sandbox mode or effective working directory retires its existing kernel, so variables and open handles are lost. Pending bridged calls are cancelled and drained before a replacement starts. Confined kernels are not shared across session identities. Unrestricted parent/child sessions with the same working directory may still share one process.

`COLUMNS`/`LINES` are pinned inside the kernel: with no TTY, `get_terminal_size()` falls back to 80×24 and wraps tracebacks and pretty output far narrower than the harness renders at.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-py-codeact
```

On DSH 0.2.2 and other hosts with the split tool-executor API, the Python SDK renderer is **required**. Install it alongside the plugin, using the exact version of your DSH host (for example, `0.2.2-rc.1`):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-py-codeact @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-executor-ptc@<dsh-version>
```

The renderer peer is optional in package metadata only to preserve legacy hosts, which export the renderer from `dsh-tools` and cannot satisfy the new executor's host peers. Split-API hosts must provide it; a missing renderer produces an explicit installation error. Other import failures retain their original diagnostic.

On DSH 0.2.2, add the row from `example/agent.cordis.yml` to an owned `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration's `config.plugins` through a profile bundle patch. Inspect the existing composition first and retain its realms, tools, sandbox, and approv

# dsh-openai-live

**Full-duplex voice for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): a Gemini
Live adapter and the original GPT-Live-1 adapter, behind one capability seam.**

> **Status: pre-release.** The GPT-Live-1 path is verified against the live API. The Gemini Live path is
> verified offline — keyless replay, the shared conformance suite, and a bundle composed through the real
> Loader — and its wire path has been **run against Google's Live API** (text and audio sessions, 2026-11-09: setup,
> tool call, tool response, spoken reply, and both transcription directions observed). The full
> browser-to-responder path has not;
> what remains is [docs/gemini-live-build.md](docs/gemini-live-build.md) §5. 1,169 tests, a per-file 100% coverage gate
> that is enforced rather than reported, and a built-artifact smoke that runs the published output under
> plain `node`. Not yet published to npm.

**A fork of [Travizm/dsh-openai-live](https://github.com/Travizm/dsh-openai-live).** That project
carries the GPT-Live-1 path and its measured wire record; this one adds the Gemini Live adapter, its
keyless replay, and the composition that mounts it. Both adapters live behind the same seam, and the
composition you get by default is Gemini's — see [docs/gemini-live-build.md](docs/gemini-live-build.md).

Two compositions ship, and they are deliberately **not** one patch: the two protocols need different
opening instructions on the shared agent row.

| Composition | Patch | Provider | Credential |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gemini Live** — what `dsh.bundle.patch` names | `cordis.gemini.patch.yml` | `gemini-live` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` |
| GPT-Live-1 | `cordis.patch.yml` | `openai-live` | `OPENAI_LIVE_API_KEY` |

## Why this exists


DeepSeek Harness ships no full-duplex speech subsystem at all, and no plugin in the ecosystem
implements `gpt-live-1` — the only live, non-sunsetting full-duplex voice model. The nearest existing
plugin targets the retiring `gpt-realtime` family at a different endpoint with a different event
vocabulary. This is that port.

The interesting part is not the audio. It is that the model can **delegate**: mid-conversation it
raises a task for the host agent and waits to be answered, without stopping the conversation. Getting
that envelope right — and failing closed when it cannot be answered — is the domain of this project.

## The seam, not a monolith

Four packages, mirroring how DSH itself models `ctx.llm`:

| Package | Role |
|---|---|
| **`dsh-realtime`** | The **seam**. Registers the `realtime` service; owns providers, routes, and session lifecycle. Deliberately refuses to own turn-taking, endpointing, or any auto-answer path for a delegation. |
| **`dsh-realtime-gemini`** | The **Gemini Live adapter**. `BidiGenerateContent` over WebSocket, in-band function calling (`ask_coding_agent`), and a 24 kHz → 16 kHz resampler, so the browser's capture reaches the model at the rate it expects. |
| **`dsh-realtime-openai`** | The **GPT-Live-1 adapter**. Wire types, transport, translation, and the session — four separable layers, with the translation layer pure and tested against recorded frames. |
| **`dsh-realtime-replay`** | The **keyless backend**. Plays a recorded session through the *real* adapter and session, so conformance runs in CI with no credential, no network, and no spend. |

A fifth package, **`dsh-openai-live`** (this repo's root), is a bundle: it carries both compositions —
`cordis.gemini.patch.yml` (what `dsh.bundle.patch` names) and `cordis.patch.yml` — and depends on all four.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-openai-live      # once published
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config                   # composes?
dsh --profile <name> web
```

Then supply the credential **from the environment** — it is a validated config field, never a file
this code reads:

```bash
export GEMINI_API_KEY=…      # or GOOGLE_API_KEY; the Gemini composition reads either
# The GPT-Live-1 composition instead reads:
# export OPENAI_LIVE_API_KEY=…
```

A profile composes fine *without* one. The route registers, and opening a session fails with
`MISSING_CREDENTIAL` — an error that **names the setting and never the value**. That is deliberate: an
unconfigured machine should boot and then say precisely what is missing, rather than break the harness
at startup.

**On the Gemini composition**, the model is handed an `ask_coding_agent(task)` tool in its setup frame;
a call arrives as a delegation carrying the task as a structured payload, the responder runs it against a
real DSH session, and the answer returns as the tool's result for the model to summarise out loud. Set
`sessionId` on the responder row to the session you want the voice conversation to steer — it has no
default because a responder attached to the wrong session would speak another conversation's reply.
The full build record, including what a live-key run still has to prove, is
[docs/gemini-live-build.md](docs/gemini-live-build.md).

## Properties held to, and tested

1. **Fail-closed delegation.** An unresolvable or erroring delegation never auto-approves.
2. **The provider owns the turn boundary.** There is no hand-rolled VAD, and the seam refuses
   end-of-utterance calls outright — `session.input_audio.commit` *does not exist* in the API, which
   the server itself confirmed by enumerating its vocabulary.
3. **Credentials are a tested invariant, not a convention.** The credential error names the setting.
   No value reaches a log, a fixture, a commit, or a published tarball.
4. **Keyless replay.** The full conversation path is exercised with no API key present.
5. **Drift canary.** A scheduled check fails loudly when the provider changes shape, so the first
   signal is a red build rather than a user bug report.
6. **Appends resolve on the provider's acknowledgement**, correlated on the echoed `client_event_id`
   with a **FIFO fallback** — an undocumented echo must degrade to ordering, never to a hung promise.
7. **Usage is cumulative**, so a consumer replaces its figure rather than adding to it. The same value
   legitimately arrives twice, on `session.usage.updated` and again on `session.closed`.
8. **Every registry proves disposal** — a contribution is made from a child fiber, that fiber is
   disposed, and the contribution is observed gone.

## Verified against the live API

The `docs/` directory is the primary record. Everything in it was measured, and the traps each cost a
run:

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md) | GPT-Live-1 over WebSocket: the full client and server vocabulary, the delegation envelope, audio formats, and the traps |
| [docs/gemini-live-build.md](docs/gemini-live-build.md) | Gemini Live: the build record, the tool bridge, and **what a first live-key run still has to prove** |
| [docs/voices.html](docs/voices.html) | the 30 prebuilt voices, one click each — `pnpm voice-samples` re-renders them |
| [docs/second-provider-spike.md](docs/second-provider-spike.md) | the provider comparison, with ✅ observed and ❓ documented kept apart |
| [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) | architecture, scope, session lifecycle |
| [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md) | ADRs — why client delegation, why a seam, why this repo is non-governed |
| [docs/w1-entitlement-probe.md](docs/w1-entitlement-probe.md) | entitlement, and why a zero balance is not an entitlement failure |
| [docs/w1-delegation-envelope.md](docs/w1-delegation-envelope.md) | the two delegation modes, measured |

## Working on it

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm gate      # build → typecheck (src AND tests) → coverage gate → built-artifact smoke
pnpm canary    # live drift check; self-skips without OPENAI_LIVE_API_KEY
```

The gate enforces **per-file 100% statements, branches, functions and lines**. That is enforced with
`perFile: true`, and the enforcement was proven to bite: one injected uncovered branch exits 1 naming
the file and each axis. Beyond unit tests there are two tiers a change cannot skip — a real
**composition** test that boots a `cordis.yml` through the actual Loader, and a **built-artifact**
smoke that runs the published `lib/` under plain `node`.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Security

No credential is stored in this repository. `.gitignore` was committed **before** the first tracked
file, and the full history is secret-scanned in CI — a secret removed in a later commit is still
published. Report a vulnerability per [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Licence

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# dsh-dafeiyu-pro 🐋🎙️

**给「大肥鱼」桌宠加上语音能力** —— 基于 [QCYTSN/dsh-dafeiyu](https://github.com/QCYTSN/dsh-dafeiyu) 的二次开发。

> ⚠️ **这是一个 fork，不是原创项目。**
> 原项目 `dsh-dafeiyu` 由 [@QCYTSN](https://github.com/QCYTSN) 开发，MIT 协议。
> 本仓库在其基础上增加语音交互能力，遵循同样的 MIT 协议。

---

## 目录

- [这是什么](#这是什么)
- [与上游的关系](#与上游的关系)
- [当前进度](#当前进度)
- [规划中的功能](#规划中的功能)
- [技术选型](#技术选型)
- [开发环境](#开发环境)
- [许可与致谢](#许可与致谢)

---

## 这是什么

[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的桌面伴侣插件。

原版 `dsh-dafeiyu` 会显示 Agent 的实时状态（思考、改文件、等确认、出错），它有一个透明置顶的原生窗口，还能看余额。

**本项目要做的，是让它能听、能说：**

```
你叫「大肥鱼」
    ↓
它回「我在」
    ↓
你说话 → 流式识别 → 意图分流
    ↓
    ├─ 闲聊 → 直连 LLM → 1~2 秒回话
    ├─ 查数据 → 调天气/搜索 API
    └─ 长任务 → 派给 DSH agent，先垫一句「好的，我看看」
    ↓
流式合成，边收边播，可以中途打断
```

---

## 与上游的关系

### 来源

| 项目 | 地址 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| **上游** | [QCYTSN/dsh-dafeiyu](https://github.com/QCYTSN/dsh-dafeiyu) | 原作者，MIT |
| **本仓库** | [cooleye/dsh-dafeiyu-pro](https://github.com/cooleye/dsh-dafeiyu-pro) | 二次开发 |

### 我们改了什么

| 领域 | 上游 | 本项目 |
|---|---|---|
| 语音唤醒 | ❌ | 🔨 开发中 |
| 语音识别 | ❌ | 🔨 开发中 |
| 语音合成 | ❌ | 🔨 开发中 |
| 意图分流 | ❌ | 📋 规划中 |
| 长期记忆 | ❌ | 📋 规划中 |
| 状态显示 | ✅ 完整 | ✅ 保持不变 |
| 桌宠动画 | ✅ 完整 | ✅ 保持不变 |

### 我们没改什么

- **动画素材**：仍然来自上游，原始出处是 [PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet)（MIT）
- **图标、光标、音效**：保持不变
- **状态机核心**：`companion-reducer.js` 的逻辑保持上游实现

---

## 当前进度

| 阶段 | 内容 | 状态 |
|---|---|---|
| — | Fork 上游代码 | ✅ 完成 |
| Phase 0 | 唤醒词 PoC | ✅ **完成**（实测 3/3 命中） |
| Phase 1 | 音频栈 + 本地出声 | ✅ **完成**（唤醒→回应已跑通） |
| Phase 2 | 云端流式 ASR | ✅ **完成**（连续多段已修好） |
| Phase 3 | 对话闭环（LLM + TTS） | ✅ **完成**（能真聊了） |
| Phase 4 | 分级路由（闲聊/查询/干活） | ✅ **完成**（8/8 测试通过） |
| Phase 5 | 长期记忆 | ⬜ 未开始 |

### 已跑通的完整链路

```
说「大肥鱼」
    ↓
本地 KWS 命中（零云端调用）
    ↓
回「我在」
    ↓
进入听写态，VAD 断句
    ↓
阿里云 paraformer 流式转写
    ↓
💬 你说：今天天气怎么样？
    ↓
🧭 意图分流
    ├─ chat → 直连 LLM 0.5~1s
    ├─ data → LLM + 搜索工具，1~2s
    └─ task → DSH agent，先垫一句「好的，我看看」
    ↓
按句切分 → qwen3-tts 合成 → 逐句播放
```

**实测数据**：

| 项目 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 唤醒 | 3/3 命中 |
| ASR 准确度 | 「今天天气怎么样？给我讲个故事呗。」全对，带标点 |
| ASR 速度 | 2.89 秒音频 → 0.97 秒转完（3× 实时） |
| LLM 首字 | 0.25~0.33 秒 |
| **工具调用** | 问天气自动触发搜索，1.34 秒出结果 |
| TTS 合成 | 6.64 秒音频 / 1.5 秒合成（4.4× 实时） |
| **端到端开口** | **约 2 秒**（闲聊）/ 1.3 秒（带搜索） |
| DSH agent | 简单任务 4.3 秒，长任务有两级垫场 |
| 连续多段识别 | 6 段全部正确，会话不串 |
| 自动化测试 | 17 个用例全过（不联网、不用麦克风） |

> ⚠️ **Windows 音频独占**：MME / DirectSound / WASAPI 都可能被别的程序
> （比如 DSH 自己的语音输入）独占，只有 **WDM-KS** 能稳定打开。
> 本项目已做自动降级。

> ⚠️ **模型可用性**：这个 key 上 `qwen-turbo` 长期 429，
> `qwen-flash` / `qwen-plus` / `qwen-max` 可用。默认用 `qwen-flash`。

### 三级路由的意义

| 路径 | 触发 | 延迟 | 谁在干活 |
|---|---|---|---|
| chat | 寒暄、情绪、玩笑 | 0.5~1s | 直连 LLM |
| data | 天气、新闻、实时信息 | 1~2s | LLM + 搜索工具 |
| task | 写文档、改代码、做开发 | 垫场即时 | DSH agent |

**为什么不统一走 agent**：DSH agent 能干活但一次几十秒，
说「你好」等半分钟体验会崩。分流之后快的地方快，慢的地方有垫场。

详细设计见 [docs/VOICE-DESIGN.md](docs/VOICE-DESIGN.md)，
怎么测试见 [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md)。

---

## 规划中的功能

### 语音唤醒（本地，零云端调用）

- 唤醒词可配置，默认「大肥鱼」
- 用 [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx) 的 KWS 模型
- 待命态不烧钱：超出唤醒词长度窗口的音频直接丢弃

### 语音识别（云端流式）

- 阿里云 paraformer-realtime-v2
- 边说边出字，支持打断
- 多级降噪门控（能量迟滞 / 过零率 / 有声帧占比）

### 语音合成（云端流式）

- 阿里云 Qwen-TTS / MiniMax
- 边收边播，支持中途打断
- 云端失败时回落到本地 TTS

### 意图分流

三条路，各走各的：

| 路径 | 触发 | 响应 | 走的通道 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 闲聊 | 「你好呀」「今天怎么样」 | 1~2s | 直连 LLM |
| 查数据 | 「今天天气」「有什么新闻」 | 1~2s | LLM + 天气/搜索 API |
| 长任务 | 「帮我写个文档」 | 先垫话，后异步 | DSH agent |

### 长期记忆

- 事实库（关键词 × 类别 × 重要度 × 新鲜度打分）
- 每条事实带用户原话作为依据，防模型凭空记忆
- 闲聊记忆和任务记忆分开存

---

## 技术选型

| 层面 | 选型 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| 桌面壳 | PySide6 (Qt6) | 沿用上游 |
| 插件层 | Cordis (DSH) | 沿用上游 |
| 唤醒词 | sherpa-onnx KWS | 本地、低功耗、零成本 |
| 语音识别 | 阿里云 paraformer-realtime-v2 | 流式效果好，实测中文 CER 2.1% |
| 语音合成 | 阿里云 Qwen-TTS | 支持情感语气，首包几百毫秒 |
| 音频采集 | sounddevice (PortAudio) | Qt 打包里没有 QtMultimedia |
| 意图分类 | 规则 + 小模型兜底 | 快、可解释 |

### 参考实现

语音链路参考了 [desk-ai](https://github.com/) 的实测参数（私有项目），包括：

- VAD 参数（起说话 0.03 / 收尾 0.012 / 对话态静音切段 1050ms）
- 打断阈值与 1 秒重喂机制
- ASR 幻觉短语过滤词表
- 阿里云 WebSocket 的 `"streaming": "duplex"` 坑

---

## 开发环境

### 前置

- Node.js ≥ 22.19
- Python ≥ 3.10（用于 helper）
- pnpm

### 本地开发

```bash
# 克隆
git clone https://github.com/cooleye/dsh-dafeiyu-pro.git
cd dsh-dafeiyu-pro

# 安装依赖
pnpm install

# 跑测试
npm test
npm run test:python

# 直接跑 helper（开发期推荐，不用每次打包）
npm run helper:headless     # 验证协议，不开窗口
npm run helper:visual       # 开窗口
```

### 装到 DSH 里

```bash
# 用 link 模式，改代码实时生效
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<本仓库绝对路径>
```

### 打包

```bash
npm run build:helper:windows   # Windows exe
npm run build:helper:linux     # Linux
npm run build:helper:darwin    # macOS
```

---

## 目录结构

```
dsh-dafeiyu-pro/
├── src/                    Node 侧（插件逻辑）
│   ├── plugin.js           配置 Schema、事件订阅
│   ├── companion-reducer.js 状态机
```
