evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-llm-manage

A persistent [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that
manages the model inventory of a configured LLM route: pins and favorites, a per-model
reason why each model is unusable, gateway directory reconciliation, and automatic
fallback when one model's quota runs out.

**No screenshots are committed, on purpose.** `screenshot.mjs` captures a *running* harness,
so the images show whatever routes and model inventory that harness has — the maintainer's own
deployment. A route name rendered into a PNG cannot be found by a text scan, which is how a
set of them was published once. Run the script against your own harness (see
[Looking at the panel without restarting](#looking-at-the-panel-without-restarting)) and you
get your own routes, which is the only version of that picture that means anything to you.

## Why

A route that aggregates many providers behind one gateway exposes its whole catalogue as
one flat list. Five things then go wrong at once, and none of them is the gateway's fault:

| Pain | What this plugin does |
|---|---|
| A long list, favorites buried | Pin and favorite models; the picker lifts them into their own sections at the top, and the panel sorts pinned → favorite → recent → rest |
| No sense of which models you actually rely on | A local ledger levels each model by how often you use it and ranks the rest by 14-day heat, shown as a **Most used** card in the panel and a ranked section in the picker |
| Retired models still listed; selecting one errors | Reconciles the route's `models:` list against the gateway's own `GET {baseURL}/models` directory and flags anything missing as retired |
| Quota exhausted, manual switching | Watches `agent/request-error`, moves the session to the next usable model on a model-scoped failure, and reports the switch only once the model that answered confirms it |
| The same model served by several providers | Marks each row with how many other routes also serve it, instead of hiding the copies |
| Models that cannot be called at all | Probes with a minimal request and labels the incompatibility honestly |

Nothing here is hard-coded to one gateway or one model id.

## Install

From the npm registry (the packaged release, no toolchain needed):

```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-llm-manage
```

`dsh plugin` forwards the arguments after `--profile <name>` to pnpm inside that profile's
directory, so anything pnpm accepts works here (`add`, `remove`, `why`, …). The profile maps
`node_modules/dsh-llm-manage` to the package from the registry.

### Development installs

Prefer the npm package for a normal installation. Two alternatives are useful while working
on the plugin itself:

- Install from a **path** to link the directory, so local edits show up without reinstalling:
  ```
  dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-llm-manage
  ```
  This symlinks the working copy — ideal when you are the author. Every edit is live, which
  is why "Applying a change" below is written for it.
- Install from the **git URL** to get a fixed copy of the latest source rather than the npm
  release:
  ```
  dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/PhilYue/dsh-llm-manage.git
  ```

The package installs as a bundle: its `dsh.bundle.patch` row inserts one Host plugin, and
its `dsh.client` declaration makes the web shell load the browser half. The Host half
needs a **full harness restart**; the browser half is picked up by the client HMR watcher,
so a page refresh is enough. See "Applying a change" below.

## Configuration

Every value lives in the plugin row's `config`, so your own patch layer keeps overrides
across upgrades. Defaults:

```yaml
- id: llm-manage
  name: 'dsh-llm-manage'
  config:
    selector:
      mode: managed     # our picker owns the seat; 'native' hands it back to the shipped one
    probe:
      intervalMs: 1200  # delay between deep probes
      timeoutMs: 30000
      batch: 40         # probes accepted per request
    directory:
      ttlMs: 1800000    # how long a gateway directory read is trusted
    fallback:
      enabled: true
      chain: []         # 'route/model' entries, tried first
    usage:
      enabled: true     # local proficiency/heat counters
      seed: true        # one pass over existing session logs at startup
      flushMs: 5000     # counters are batched to disk on this interval
```

The fallback chain order is: `fallback.chain`, then pinned models, then favorites, then the
remaining models on the same route, then other routes. Models already known to be retired,
protocol-incompatible, hidden, or inside their quota cooldown are skipped. At most three
automatic switches happen per turn.

### Which failures switch, and which never do

The rule is **scope**, not severity:

| Failure | Scope | Switches? | Recorded against the model? |
|---|---|---|---|
| model not found / retired | one model | yes | yes |
| wrong protocol for this route | one model | yes | yes |
| per-model quota exhausted | one model | yes | yes |
| other per-model failures | one model | yes | yes |
| no adapter registered for this route | the whole route | yes | **no** |
| account-wide rate limit | the whole API key | **never** | no |
| account-wide quota | the whole API key | **never** | no |

A model-scoped failure moves to another model, because a different model can serve the
turn. An account-scoped failure never moves: every model shares that key, so switching
would only hide the real problem and burn another request.

A switch cannot rescue the turn that just failed. DSH freezes the provider, model and
reasoning effort at step preparation, re-validates them when the request is built, and
replays the same frozen selection on a retry — so the plugin commits the switch with
`agent.model.select()`, the one path the SDK documents, and the **next** message runs on
the new model. The failed turn reports its real error instead of a request-time mismatch.
If the Session still holds the broken selection when the next message is claimed — a
refused controller call, or a level the session did not drop — the repair is finished
there, synchronously, before the step reads its selection.

A **route with no adapter** is its own scope. Switching models *on that route* cannot
help — every model there fails the same way — but switching to another provider can, so
it still switches. What it must not do is land in the model's health record: `error` is
in the set of reasons that make the fallback chain skip a model, and unlike `quota` that
verdict has no staleness escape, so a single route misconfiguration would have removed
an innocent model from every future chain permanently.

### A probe is not a routing event

"Unusable" and "move the conversation" are two different conclusions, and only a **failed
request** reaches the second one:

- A **failed request** (`agent/request-error`) is the live conversation hitting a wall. If
  the failure is model-scoped, the turn is retried on the next usable model and a banner
  names the model it moved for.
- A **failed probe** is an answer to a question you asked about a model. It records that
  model's health — so the *next* real switch skips it — but it does **not** touch whichever
  session happens to be using it. Moving a live conversation because of a diagnostic you
  ran would be switching models behind your back, which is the thing this design forbids.

Concretely, with `model-gamma` selected and its quota exhausted:

| Event | Selected model afterwards |
|---|---|
| you deep-probe `model-gamma`, and the probe fails | still `model-gamma` |
| a real request on `model-gamma` fails with per-model quota | `model-beta` (next usable), banner shown |
| a real request fails with an account-wide key limit (2008) | still `model-gamma` |

At most three automatic switches happen per turn, and if the chain finds nothing usable the
failure is passed through untouched rather than retried in a way that cannot succeed.

### The switch happens, and the banner proves it

Two mechanisms move a model, and the difference matters:

- **The session's own selection** (`sessionController.selectModel`) is what makes the
  change real. It validates the target against a registered adapter and appends a durable
  `model/selection` event, so the model the conversation uses actually changes and every
  surface agrees. The saved **default model is put back** afterwards: an automatic
  recovery has no business permanently changing which model new sessions start on.
- **A per-request override**, bound to the exact turn and step it was decided for, is what
  recovers the turn already in flight. It is needed because the harness applies the
  session selection during prompt assembly, which happens once per step — before the retry
  loop — so the session change alone would only take effect on the *next* turn.

The banner then reports what was **proven**, not what was decided. A switch is recorded as
pending, and only promoted to something you are shown once a committed assistant message
names the model that actually produced the response:

| What the answering model was | What the banner says |
|---|---|
| the model we switched to | *Model switched*, with **Switch back** |
| a different model | *Switch did not take effect*, naming the model that actually ran |
| no message — the turn ended | *Switch attempted, turn not recovered* |

The earlier version wrote the banner when the switch was decided, so a retry that failed,
was aborted, or ran on a third route produced the same "switched automatically" text. It
also hardcoded "exhausted quota" as the cause for every failure, including failures that
were not about quota at all. Each reason now has its own wording, and the provider's raw
message is one clamped line with the full text on hover — inlined in full it was up to 400
characters, which made the banner taller than the conversation around it.

The banner carries the way forward, not just the news. **Continue** appears once a switch
was confirmed: the platform froze the model for the step that already failed, so the only
continuation is the next message — and that message stays yours. The button fills an
editable prompt ("continue from where the previous answer stopped") into the draft and
persists it; it never sends on your behalf. **Switch back** is offered under the same
condition, since it moves the session's model back. **Stop switching** suppresses automatic
switching for that session until the harness restarts. **Dismiss** hides the report for
that switch only.

Some gateways report a *model's* quota exhaustion as HTTP 429, which the harness's own
classifier maps to a retryable `RATE_LIMIT` — indistinguishable from an account-wide rate
limit. The two need opposite handling, so this plugin reads the gateway's numeric business
code out of the error body instead of trusting the mapped code. The code table is at the
top of `index.js`; adjust it there if your gateway numbers things differently.

## Why probing is manual

`GET /v1/models` is free but is only a directory, not a callability list: a model can be
advertised and still fail on first use (wrong protocol, no capacity, image-only). Probing
each model deeply is therefore the only way to learn whether it works — and deep probes
spend the gateway's **per-key** rate budget, so a sweep large enough to be useful is also
large enough to rate-limit the user out of their own gateway.

Health is learned cheapest-first instead:

1. the free directory set,
2. real request failures as they happen (passive, zero extra traffic),
3. explicit probes the user starts, throttled at `probe.intervalMs` and capped at `probe.batch`.

Each row's status is the strongest evidence available, in this order:

| Status | Means | Shown when |
|---|---|---|
| `retired` | the gateway no longer lists the model | the directory read succeeded and the model is absent from it |
| the recorded health | a probe or a real request produced a verdict | any health record exists for that route+model |
| `ok` | the gateway lists it, and no failure is known | the directory read succeeded and there is no health record |
| `unknown` | nothing is known | the route exposes no `baseURL`, so there is no directory to compare against |

`ok` therefore means "listed and not known to be broken", which is weaker than "verified
working" — a model can be advertised and still fail on first use. The panel keeps the
distinction visible by showing the source alongside the status, so a row reads
**usable · deep probe** once it has actually answered and **usable · never checked** while it
has not. Neither is hidden: the second is the honest label for the majority of a large
catalogue, because verifying all of it at once is what would rate-limit you out.

## Verifying it

Five suites, all runnable without any particular deployment:

```
node verify.mjs          # Host half: registry, gateway, classification, fallback
node verify-client.mjs   # Browser half: renders the panel in jsdom and clicks it
node verify-browser.mjs  # Control geometry in a real engine (headless Chrome)
node verify-parity.mjs   # Did the shipped seats we take keep their capabilities?
node verify-live.mjs     # The whole thing against a RUNNING harness (opt-in)
```

`verify-parity.mjs` needs the harness **source** (`DSH_CHECKOUT`) and fails without
it, because its whole job is comparing this plugin against the shipped one. See
[docs/upstream-parity.md](docs/upstream-parity.md).

Each suite picks a mode automatically:

- **`real`** — this machine has a profile whose first provider route resolves, plus that
  route's credential. The settings under test are then the deployed ones, and the gateway
  directory is read live. This is the mode that catches a fixture agreeing with a wrong
  assumption.
- **`synthetic`** — otherwise. A local stub serves a synthetic catalogue, so every code
  path still runs: offline, deterministically, with no credential and no internal endpoint.

```
LLMM_VERIFY_MODE=synthetic node verify.mjs    # force a mode
DSH_CHECKOUT=/path/to/deepseek-harness node verify.mjs
```

`DSH_CHECKOUT` points at the harness checkout, which supplies the real Tool registry,
React and jsdom. It is not vendored here; the suites try a few conventional locations and
then tell you what to set.

`verify.mjs` also gates the **publish surface**: where the maintainer's
company-information scanner is present it fails if the runtime files (`index.js`,
`client.js`, `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `icon.svg`) contain anything identifying
a particular employer or internal service; in this published package the scanner is
absent, and the gate says so rather than reporting a pass it did not perform. The scanner
is not shipped because its own rule patterns have to quote the identifiers they look for.

Some checks exist because the live harness caught bugs a shallower suite passed:

- **The suites execute the registered tool**, not just register it. A definition can
  register cleanly and throw on its first call.
- **The fixture context enforces Cordis's inject guard**, so reading `ctx.llm` from
  `apply`'s own context fails exactly as it does live.
- **Never test one half alone.** The two halves can agree on every type and still disagree
  on a field name: the panel once folded `data.snapshot` while the Host returned the same
  state under `value`, so pin/favorite/hide updated nothing until the user reloaded by
  hand. A Host-only suite passed it, and so did a client suite whose other half was a mock
  returning whatever field the client asked for.
- **`verify-browser.mjs`** exists because jsdom has no layout: every
  `getBoundingClientRect()` returns zeros, so a tooltip's position and a button's width
  cannot be measured in-process. It loads the real panel into headless Chrome and asserts
  the geometry the design depends on, then skips with exit 0 when no Chrome-family binary
  is present (`CHROME_PATH` overrides).
- **`verify-live.mjs`** exists because every other suite builds its own page and hands the
  plugin a context it controls — so none of them can catch a contract they do not enforce.
  The plugin declared `slots`, `modelDirectories` and `sessions` at the top level, then
  called `modelDirectories.directoryFor()`, which internally reaches
  `this.ctx.remote.session`. Cordis checks the **consumer's** inject list, so in the live app
  that read threw `cannot get property "remote.session" without inject`, the picker's slot
  entry crashed, and because `Style` renders inside that same subtree the composer's model
  control lost **every rule in its stylesheet**. All three suites were green: the hand-built
  contexts were plain objects that enforced nothing.

  It opens the URL `dsh web` prints — in a real engine, against the real profile, real
  catalogue and real composer — and skips with exit 0 when no live harness answers:

  ```
  DSH_LIVE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=...' node verify-live.mjs
  DSH_LIVE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3080/ DSH_LIVE_COOKIE='dsh-auth-...=...' node verify-live.mjs
  ```

### Two more contract mistakes the suites had to learn

Both of these shipped, both were green in every suite, and both were found by looking at
the running app. They are worth stating because each one changed what the suites assert.

**The theme cannot be supplied by the thing being tested.** The card was painted with
`--dsw-alias-bg-overlay`, which the plugin token contract labels *"Overlay and popover
background"* — a reasonable reading of the docs. Measured in the app it is `#e9ecf2`, a mid
grey, darker than the white composer it drops out of; DSH's own popovers paint the
translucent `--dsw-specific-menu` on a child layer with a backdrop blur instead. The suites
could not catch it because they defined that token themselves: `verify-browser.mjs` had
`--dsw-alias-bg-overlay:#fff`, and the deleted `preview.mjs` invented the same white. The
suites now carry the values the app actually resolves, and `verify-browser.mjs` fails if the
stylesheet reads any token its theme block does not define — 27 are read. `verify-live.mjs`
asserts the painted surface against the token's real value.

**A stylesheet in a template literal can truncate without a syntax error.** A backtick or
`${` inside a CSS comment ends the literal early. The pieces often still re-parse as
JavaScript, so `node --check` passes, and the failure that reaches you is a browser refusing
the import — the whole client half silently absent. `verify-client.mjs` extracts the literal
and asserts it is intact, which catches the case that parses but is wrong.

  The lesson generalizes past this bug: **a suite that supplies the context cannot verify
  the context.** An inject declaration is a contract with the runtime, and only the runtime
  can check it.

### Looking at the panel without restarting

```
DSH_LIVE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=…' node screenshot.mjs
```

Captures the panel and the model picker out of the running harness, light and dark, into
`docs/` — which is gitignored, so the images stay on your machine. It is the preview of record
because it supplies nothing: it opens the URL `dsh web` printed and photographs what is there.

The images are not committed because a capture of a real harness is a picture of the routes
and model inventory that harness is configured with. That is the maintainer's deployment, and
it is also the one kind of content a text scan cannot inspect: a route name rendered into a
PNG reads as PNG bytes, matches no rule, and passes. Four such screenshots were published
before anyone noticed. `build-public.mjs` now refuses to stage any binary asset, and
`scan-company-info.mjs` reports files it cannot read as unscannable rather than counting them
as clean — the whitelist that decided which extensions to open was the whole defect.

This replaced a `preview.mjs` that rendered the plugin into a hand-written page with a
hand-written theme. That page defined `--dsw-alias-bg-overlay:#fff` — a value the token never
has in the app, where it is `#e9ecf2` — and defined only the 14 tokens the plugin contract
documents while the stylesheet reads 27. The mock showed a white card; the app painted a grey
one. A preview that supplies its own theme cannot show you the theme, and an approved mock is
worse than no mock: it is the reason the grey card shipped.

The replacement supplies nothing of its own and skips with exit 0 when no harness answers, so
it never reports a picture it did not take. To reach the panel it sends the `settings.open`
chord — `primary+alt+Comma` on web, not the plain `primary+Comma` the desktop runtime uses —
then clicks through the settings nav until the panel appears, matching no label because the
labels are localised. A development aid, not a test.

## Where it appears

- **Settings → Models → the provider card**: the management panel.
- **The composer model picker**: this plugin's picker in the shipped picker's seat — one
  entry, one panel, with the shipped capabilities (search, provider grouping, keyboard
  roaming, a trigger that names the current model and level) plus levels, probes, the
  manager and the usage figures. `selector.mode: native` hands the seat back to the shipped
  picker and leaves only the health dot, level chip and listing badge on its rows.
- **Above the composer**: a banner when this session's model was switched.

### Decorating the shipped picker

As of DSH 0.2.2 the shipped picker carries its own reasoning levels, its own badges and the
provider-default effort, so this plugin stopped shadowing it: the seat belongs to the owner
and we contribute the marks the owner cannot know — the health verdict, the proficiency
level use has earned, and the listing badge.

That is a slot contribution (`conversation.input.model.label`), and two of its rules decided
the implementation:

- A contribution **replaces** the owner's fallback, so the model name is ours to draw. A
  label that returned nothing would blank the composer control — the failure is invisible in
  a picker screenshot, so `verify-client.mjs` asserts the name is rendered.
- The label mounts once per catalogue row, so the plugin's stylesheet is mounted once into
  `<head>` (re-found by attribute) rather than per instance: a sheet per row would multiply
  20 KB by the size of the catalogue. A second mount is asserted to reuse it.

The level only appears once use has earned it (level 2 and up) and only where there is room:
the collapsed trigger keeps the health dot alone, because the owner budgeted its width.

### The composer controller

Inside the composer card, on the row the submit button lives on, sits a control cluster that
changes shape with the session instead of holding a fixed row of buttons:

- **idle** — the manager button and a dimmed `⌘K`; nothing else. The reasoning level is
  deliberately absent: the model trigger a few pixels away already names it and opens the
  panel that owns it, and one fact with two controls reads like two facts.
- **typing** — adds `Draft 42 chars`, plus attachment and queue counts when they exist.
- **a submit in flight** — the phase it is in: reading command, command claimed, running
  command, sending.
- **a running turn** — `Running 1:07` with a status dot.
- **waiting on you** — the same line, followed by `waiting for you`.

It is deliberately **additive**. `conversation.composer.bar` owns the editor — IME
composition, paste, slash adjudication, @-mentions, attachment drops, local echo, the hero
variant — and replacing it would mean reimplementing all of that while losing every shipped
`conversation.input.*` seat that renders inside it. The cluster lives in
`conversation.input.right` — the list the shipped editor already reads for "compact controls
before the submit action" — so it sits in the card instead of floating above it, and reads
the same live input state the editor publishes: it reacts without owning a keystroke.

Taking the model seat means inheriting its obligations, not only its space: the shipped
menu rendered `conversation.input.model.options` there, which is where the agent-team toggle
registers. The picker renders that slot with the same props (`locked`, `dismiss`,
`reportFailure`), so switching a team on still happens where it always did — a capability
that vanished because a replacement did not know the slot existed would be worse than not
replacing the menu at all.

`⌘K` (or `⌘J`) opens the command palette: a session console, not a chat box. Its rows are
grouped — **This session**, **Model**, **Diagnostics**, **Manage** — because a flat list of
eleven rows with eight of them being reasoning stops is a list nobody reads.

- **Search** filters as you type. Matching is by subsequence over label, hint and alias, so
  `th` finds 探活 and `mdl` finds the dialog row; every row carries English and Chinese
  aliases, which makes typing one word faster than reading a list. A word that matches
  nothing says so instead of drawing an empty card.
- **Levels are one row** naming the stop actually in force (`Level · High`), and that row
  opens a second page: the stops plus **Auto**, with exactly one of them marked as current.
  `‹` or `Esc` goes back. The stops used to sit in the root, where six of them outnumbered
  every other command and pushed the useful rows below the fold.
- **A command in flight says so.** The running row carries a spinner, every other row is
  disabled, and the answer — or the failure — lands on the row that was asked. Previously the
  palette tracked a `busy` flag in state and then never read it while rendering, so a probe
  that took a round trip looked like a dead row you could click again.
- **Diagnostics got the rows only it can offer**: refresh the gateway catalogue (a snapshot
  that bypasses the Host's cached directory), probe every model on this route (batch probe,
  capped at 40 upstream, submitted and then reported in the probe log rather than blocking
  the panel for a minute), plus **Recent failovers** and **Probe log**, which open the
  manager on that tab.
- **Escape peels one layer at a time**: clear the search word, then leave a sub-page, then
  close.

Rows are the only things in the palette that are not the search box, and a row that names a
tab lands on that tab — opening the dialog on the catalogue and making the reader click
again answers a different question than the row promised. Entry points that name no tab
(the ⚙ button, `⌘⇧M`, the picker footer) land on the catalogue even if the last visit sat
elsewhere.

Every row runs a real action through the seats the owner already provides
(`inputActions.submit`, `inputActions.setDraft`, `directory.select`, the plugin's own Host
route), so the palette never renders a command it cannot execute. `Enter` runs the
highlighted row and stops the event there, so it cannot also submit the draft behind it. The
palette is a fixed surface: the composer card clips its own children, so a popover born
inside it would be cut at the card's edge.

The palette is drawn from the same material as the model picker card — the theme's menu fill
on a `::before` layer behind the content, the elevation stroke, `border-l1` for the rule under
the header. An earlier version filled it with `--dsw-alias-bg-overlay`, which is the scrim
colour *behind* a dialog rather than a surface colour, so a 560px panel painted with it read
as a different product pasted over this one.

### The composer model picker


![The model picker, rendered from a synthetic catalogue](docs/picker.png)

The picture is a synthetic render, not a photograph of anyone's harness: `preview.mjs`
renders the real plugin code against an invented catalogue — fake models on fake routes —
so the screenshot cannot contain a route you do not already have in front of you in the
source. To see it against *your* catalogue instead, run `screenshot.mjs` against your own
harness: it drives the real settings UI — sending the `settings.open` chord and finding the
Models section — so what you get is your own catalogue in your own theme.

The panel, from the same renderer:

![The models panel, rendered from the same synthetic catalogue](docs/panel.png)

The picker opens on **Pinned**, then **Favorites**, then **Most used**, then one section per
route. Pins and favorites are lifted *out* of their route and shown once, at the top, so a
favorite is one click away no matter how many routes the profile has or how many models sit
ahead of it alphabetically. Below the sections, each route still lists everything else, minus
the rows already lifted — every listed model is offered exactly once. Hidden models are not
selectable, but they are not discarded either: they collect in a **Hidden** section at the
bottom, which is the only place the menu can offer them back.

A model that is both pinned and favorited appears under **Pinned** only, matching the
fallback chain's own precedence, where a pin outranks a favorite.

**Most used** is earned rather than declared: it holds the five models this profile reaches
for most, ranked by heat, so the models you actually work with rise to the top without being
pinned by hand. It is capped, because it is a shortcut to the top of the list rather than a
second copy of the catalogue, and it never repeats a pin or a favorite.

Because a lifted row is no longer under its route's heading, a section that spans more than
one route prints the route beside each model. The same model id on two routes is two
different selections, and the row has to say which one it means. A section that stays on
one route prints nothing, since the label would be noise on every row.

Rows keep their health dot and reason chip, so an unusable model is visibly unusable here
too — but it is still *selectable*. The plugin's view of a model can be stale, and hiding a
model from the picker is the one thing this design refuses to do silently. Search filters
across the lifted sections as well as the route groups.

A model that has been used c

decision.reason: Held for versioned DSH compatibility. MIT and exact npm gitHead are present. Native host/client entries persist model overlays, inspect credentials and send model-directory/probe requests; UI RPC uses connection.fetch. README discusses DSH 0.2.2 behavior but does not state a supported version contract, and the manifest declares no DSH peers/engines. Probe requests may incur provider usage and were not sent. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-chat-embed 在 **DeepSeek Harness（dsh）桌面版**里开一个**多标签 AI 聊天面板**。 左侧导航有「聊天」入口，点开后**中央主面板就是聊天页**：顶部一排标签 —— DeepSeek、豆包、ChatGPT、MiniMax、Kimi、Gemini、Grok —— 每个标签是一个真实的桌面 webview，**各自独立登录**；切标签不重载页面。同一个聊天页也能放到**右栏**（会话头「⧉」按钮 / 右栏启动器），两处互斥，**哪边点哪边接管**。 ![左栏「聊天」入口，中央主面板里是 DeepSeek 聊天页](assets/screenshots/01-deepseek-left-panel.png) --- ## 项目名称与组成 | 名称 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | `dsh-chat-embed` | 本插件的包名，也是 dsh 插件管理器里的条目名 | | `index.js` | **Host 半侧**（Node）：当前是空壳，只为满足 bundle 的 loader 行；后续若需 Host 配置从这扩展 | | `client.js` | **Client 半侧**（浏览器）：多标签、租约握手、内联席位、全部 UI。手写产物，无构建 | | `locale/{en,zh}.json` | 插件管理器里显示的标题与简介 | | `cordis.patch.yml` | 组合补丁：向 profile 插入 `id: chat-embed` 的 loader 行 | | `scripts/verify-bundle.mjs` | 门禁：语法 / 清单 / loader 契约 / 服务注册表 / 显示资源 | | `test/` | 纯 Node 契约测试（伪造 DOM + 伪造桌面桥），57 项 | | `docs/architecture.md` | 内嵌契约、席位架构、壳补丁、升级复验清单（**接到项目先读这份**） | | `tools/shell-patch/` | 可选的桌面壳补丁：持久分区（跨重启免登录）+ 关闭磁盘缓存 | | `清理聊天缓存.cmd` / `restore-shell-patch.cmd` | 缓存回收 / 还原原版壳 | **没有第三方运行时依赖**：`client.js` 直接由 dsh 的模块加载器执行，React 用壳共享的那一份。 ### 文档入口 | 想了解 | 读哪里 | | --- | --- | | 怎么装、怎么用 | 本文件（README） | | 为什么这样实现、内嵌契约、升级外壳时的复验清单 | `docs/architecture.md` | | 壳补丁（持久分区 / 关缓存）与回滚 | `tools/shell-patch/` + `restore-shell-patch.cmd` | | 门禁与测试覆盖了什么 | `scripts/verify-bundle.mjs`、`test/client.test.mjs` | --- ## 软件定位与功能 **定位**：给 dsh 桌面版补上一个"多服务 AI 聊天"的常驻界面。不代理请求、不保存聊天内容，只是把各站点装进独立登录态的桌面 webview。 | 能力 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | 左栏「聊天」→ 中央主面板直接是聊天页 | 顶部多标签切换，每个服务独立 webview、独立分区 | | 右栏聊天 tab（`keepMounted`）+ 会话头「⧉」 | 切标签不卸载，页面状态保留 | | 哪边点哪边接管 | 左栏入口 / 右栏 tab 谁被点开谁承载；互斥，切换重建一次并回到上次会话 | | 7 个内置服务 | DeepSeek、豆包、ChatGPT、MiniMax、Kimi、Gemini、Grok；改 `PROVIDERS` 一行即可扩展 | | 标签常驻 | 切标签只切 `data-active`（`display:none`），草稿与滚动位置保留 | | 失败隔离 | 单个标签失败不影响其它；「重新加载」只换该标签的租约 | | 拖动排序 | 按住标签横向拖动（>6px 才算拖动），顺序写 `localStorage`；溢出时滚轮横向滚动 | | ⚙ 设置 | 逐个启用/禁用服务，至少保留一个，状态持久化 | | 诊断（⚙ 菜单） | URL / 分区 / 阶段 / 右栏注册 / 席位 / 自检，一键复制 | | 调试日志（⚙ 菜单） | 默认关闭；开启后控制台输出插件事件，菜单里可「复制日志」 | | 原生布局跟随 | 聊天页放在席位布局盒里，宽高由 CSS 决定；拖分隔条零 JS、零重渲染 | | Google 登录死路 / 非桌面环境 | 自动退回入口并给出说明卡片；Web GUI 下显示说明 + 外开链接 | --- ## 截图 | 左栏：中央面板多标签 | 右栏：聊天 tab | | --- | --- | | ![ChatGPT 标签](assets/screenshots/02-chatgpt-left-panel.png) | ![右栏标签里的 DeepSeek](assets/screenshots/05-deepseek-right-tab.png) | | ![Gemini 标签](assets/screenshots/03-gemini-left-panel.png) | ![右栏标签里的 Gemini](assets/screenshots/06-gemini-right-tab.png) | ## 快速开始 ### 环境要求 | 项 | 要求 | | --- | --- | | 桌面端 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop 0.2.2-rc.1`（实测；Windows 10/11） | | Node.js | `>= 22`（仅开发/测试需要，插件运行时不依赖 Node） | | 浏览器/壳 | Electron（`webviewTag` 开启）—— Web GUI 只能用降级卡片 | ### 安装（5 行） > 仅桌面版可用（需要 Electron 的 `` 和 `window.dshDesktop.browser`）。 > 当前实测版本：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop 0.2.2-rc.1`；包声明了 `engines.dsh`，版本不符时插件管理器会拒绝安装。 **方式一：npm（发布之后）** ```jsonc // 在 dsh 会话里交给插件管理器执行 plugin_manager { "action": "install_bundle", "target": "dsh-chat-embed" } // 然后刷新页面；左侧栏出现气泡图标即安装成功 ``` ```powershell # 命令行等价写法 dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-chat-embed ``` **方式二：git 仓库或本地 tarball** ```powershell # 从 Releases 下载 dsh-chat-embed-<版本>.tgz 后： dsh plugin --profile desktop add .\dsh-chat-embed-0.5.0.tgz # 或直接从公开仓库安装 dsh plugin --profile desktop add git+https://github.com/poluce/dsh-chat-embed.git ``` **方式三：在本仓库开发（link 方式，改完即生效）** ```powershell dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<本仓库克隆路径> ``` > 卸载：`dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-chat-embed`（或 `plugin_manager { "action": "remove_bundle", "target": "dsh-chat-embed" }`）。 ### 启动与打开 1. 打开 dsh 桌面版，左侧栏点「聊天」图标 → 中央主面板加载聊天页； 2. 或在任意会话的标题栏点「⧉」→ 右栏打开聊天 tab； 3. 标签切换 / 拖动排序 / 右上角工具行（重新加载、外开、设置）即可使用；诊断与调试日志在「⚙」菜单里。 --- ## 简要使用说明 | 场景 | 操作 | | --- | --- | | 打开聊天 | 左栏「聊天」图标（中央）或会话头「⧉」/ 右栏启动器（右栏） | | 切换服务 | 点标签；标签会记住上次激活项（`localStorage`） | | 拖动排序 | 按住标签横向拖到目标位置松手；溢出时用滚轮横向滚动 | | 隐藏某个服务 | 工具行「⚙」→ 关闭对应开关（至少保留一个） | | 页面卡住/白屏 | 工具行「重新加载」（换新租约）或「外开」到系统浏览器 | | 排查问题 | 工具行「⚙」→「标签页诊断…」→ 看地址 / 分区 / 状态 / 席位 / 自检，点「复制诊断信息」发给维护者 | | 打开调试日志 | 工具行「⚙」→「调试日志」开关（默认关闭）；开启后控制台输出插件事件，「复制日志」导出最近 200 条 | | 查看跨重启登录 | 工具行「⚙」→「跨重启保持登录」一行显示 已开启（persist: 分区）/ 未开启（内存分区）/ 尚未检测；未开启时可点「复制补丁说明」 | | 换到另一处显示 | 直接点另一处的入口（左栏图标或右栏 tab），聊天会接管过去并回到上次会话 | **登录**：每个服务在自己的 webview 里用站点自己的方式登录（验证码/扫码/邮箱）。登录态在同一次运行内有效；跨重启需要打桌面壳补丁（见 [已知限制](#已知限制)）。 --- ## 配置 ### 增删服务 服务清单只有一处：`client.js` 的 `PROVIDERS`。追加一条即可： ```js { id: 'gemini', label: 'Gemini', url: 'https://gemini.google.com/', origin: 'https://gemini.google.com', workspace: 'dsh-chat-embed:gemini:v1' }, ``` | 字段 | 作用 | 约束 | | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | 标签 id，也参与分区命名 | 小写、唯一 | | `label` | 标签文字 | 非空 | | `url` | 首次打开导航到哪里 | `https://` | | `origin` | 站点基址（诊断/策略用） | `url` 的前缀 | | `workspace` | 壳的存储身份 = 分区键 | 唯一；**发布后不可改**（改了就退出登录） | 改完执行 `npm run check` → 重装插件 → 刷新页面。门禁会校验 https、workspace 唯一、无未声明站点。 ### 运行时开关 - `⚙` 设置的启用状态存在 `localStorage['dsh-chat-embed:enabled']`； - 标签顺序存在 `localStorage['dsh-chat-embed:tab-order']`； - 上次激活标签存在 `localStorage['dsh-chat-embed:active-tab']`； - 调试日志开关存在 `localStorage['dsh-chat-embed:log']`（`1` 开 / `0` 关，默认关）； - 最近一次检测到的持久化状态存在 `localStorage['dsh-chat-embed:persist']`，重启后无需等 guest 挂载即可显示。 ### 桌面壳补丁（可选，跨重启免登录） ```powershell node tools/shell-patch/patch-asar.cjs build # 自动探测安装目录并生成 app.asar.new node tools/shell-patch/patch-asar.cjs build --resources "D:\DeepSeek Harness\resources" node tools/shell-patch/patch-asar.cjs --help # 查看参数 # 关闭 DSH 后由 watchdog 自动替换，或手动替换 resources\app.asar ``` > 通过 npm 安装时脚本位于 `/node_modules/<包名>/tools/shell-patch/`；也可以在「⚙ → 跨重启保持登录」里点「复制补丁说明」拿到步骤。 补丁做两件事：`persist:` 固定分区（登录落盘）+ `cache:false`（不落 Chromium 缓存）。 没有补丁也能用，只是每次重启要重新登录。细节与风险见 [已知限制](#已知限制)。 --- ## 目录结构 ```text dsh-chat-embed/ ├── package.json # 包名/版本、dsh.bundle.patch、dsh.client、exports/files ├── cordis.patch.yml # 组合补丁：插入 id=chat-embed 的 loader 行 ├── index.js # Host 半侧（空壳，扩展点） ├── client.js # Client 半侧（约 3545 行，手写产物） ├── locale/{en,zh}.json # 插件管理器显示用 meta ├── icon.svg # 插件图标（插件管理器显示） ├── assets/ │ ├── icon-180.png # 商店卡片图标（180×180 位图） │ └── screenshots/ # 商店截图（6 张，1600×1027） ├── screenshots.json # 商店截图清单（插件市场读取） ├── scripts/ │ ├── verify-bundle.mjs # 门禁脚本 │ └── pack-dist.mjs # 产出 dist/*.tgz（维护者） ├── test/ │ ├── fake-env.mjs # 伪造 DOM / 伪造桌面桥 │ └── client.test.mjs # 62 项契约测试 ├── docs/ │ ├── architecture.md # 架构与内嵌契约（先读这份） │ └── publishing.md # 维护者：发版、分发与列表投稿 ├── tools/shell-patch/ # 随 npm 包发布 │ ├── patch-asar.cjs # 壳补丁（持久分区 + 关缓存） │ ├── watchdog.ps1 # 退出时替换 asar │ └── clean-cache.ps1 # 只删缓存、保留登录 ├── 清理聊天缓存.cmd ├── restore-shell-patch.cmd ├── LICENSE (MIT) └── README.md ``` --- ## 工作原理（简要） 1. **五处 slot**：`main`（中央聊天页）、`sidebar.panellist`（左栏图标）、`sidebar.right.pane.tab`（右栏 tab body）、`sidebar.right.pane.tab.title`（右栏 chip 标题）、`conversation.session.header.utilities`（会话头「⧉」）。 2. **租约握手**：点标签 → `window.dshDesktop.browser.acquire(workspace)` → 拿到一次性 `lease` 与 `partition` → 建 ``。三个属性必须完全一致，否则壳在 `will-attach-webview` 拒绝。 3. **导航**：只能从 guest 文档内部导航（`executeJavaScript('location.href = …')`），`loadURL()` / 改 `src` 无效。 4. **内联席位**：聊天页渲染在席位布局盒里（`width/height:100%`），拖分隔条由浏览器布局，零 JS 测量；切标签只切 `display:none`，元素不移动。 5. **席位接管**：席位挂载即认领 guest；另一席位若仍挂载则显示移交卡片。宿主变化时丢弃旧 guest 并重建（Electron 无法搬移 webview），再用 `startUrlFor()` 回到上次会话地址。 6. **隔离**：每服务一个 workspace、一个分区、一个 guest、一条租约；一个标签失败不影响其它。 > 想看证据、契约细节与升级检查清单：**[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)**。 --- ## 开发 ```powershell # 获取最新代码（当前仓库未配置远程地址，按你实际的 remote 替换） git clone dsh-chat-embed cd dsh-chat-embed # 无需安装依赖；直接跑门禁与测试 npm run check # 语法 + 清单 + 显示资源 + 服务注册表 + 62 项测试 npm test # 只跑测试 ``` **没有构建步骤**：`client.js` 就是最终产物。改完后重装一次让浏览器拿到新 generation： ```jsonc plugin_manager { "action": "remove_bundle", "target": "dsh-chat-embed" } plugin_manager { "action": "install_bundle", "target": "<本仓库克隆路径>" } ``` 提交前约定：门禁必须绿；代码注释/提交信息英文，文档中文；同时改 `package.json` 的 `version` 与 `client.js` 的 `BUILD`。 ### 发布与分发 维护者发版、打包、GitHub Release、npm 发布与插件列表投稿：见 **[docs/publishing.md](docs/publishing.md)**。 --- ## 已知限制 1. **跨重启登录需要壳补丁**：壳默认给内存分区（`dsh-sidebar-browser-`，无 `persist:`，每次启动随机），登录态不落盘。`tools/shell-patch/` 可修；客户端升级会覆盖 `app.asar`，需要重打。 2. **左右互斥**：右栏聊天依赖会话视图；中央打开聊天面板时右栏不可用。同一时刻只有一处显示聊天页，切换会重建一次（自动回到上次会话，不用重新登录）。 3. **中心面板会被切走**：选另一个主面板时中央聊天页随 DOM 卸载，回来要重建；右栏 tab 带 `keepMounted`，切标签/切会话不卸载。 4. **内存**：每点亮一个标签 = 一个渲染进程；7 个全开会明显吃内存。 5. **Google / Apple 登录无法在内嵌面板完成**：GSI 依赖 `window.opener` 交回凭据，面板无弹窗上下文；插件识别死路后自动退回入口并提示用邮箱登录。 6. **人机校验**：ChatGPT 首次打开可能要求过一次。 7. **仅 Electron**：无 Tauri / 第三方壳适配；Web GUI 降级为说明卡片。 8. 聊天页宽度依赖席位布局盒（`.dce-inline` 100%）；若 dsh 改掉主面板 / tab body 结构需复核。 --- ## 常见问题 | 现象 | 处理 | | --- | --- | | 侧栏没有「聊天」图标 | 插件未启用 / 未加载：看 **设置 → 插件**，或重装一次 | | 左栏入口打开是空白/卡片 | 确认右栏聊天是否开着（互斥）；看「⚙ → 标签页诊断… → 席位 / 自检」一行 | | 标签变红（`data-failed`） | 该标签租约或导航失败：点它看状态行 `detail`，再「重新加载」 | | 显示「已连接」但页面空白 | 网络或站点风控；「重新加载」或「外开」 | | 出现「使用环境异常」 | UA 归一化失效（壳升级后 UA 结构变了），查 `normalizedUserAgent` | | 重启后要重新登录 | 未打壳补丁，或补丁被客户端升级覆盖：重跑 `patch-asar.cjs build` | | 磁盘占用变大 | 执行 `清理聊天缓存.cmd`（只删缓存，保留登录）；或确认补丁含 `cache:false` | | 标签文字/顺序要改 | 只改 `PROVIDERS`，`npm run check` + 重装 | --- ## 版本历史 | 版本 | 变化 | | --- | --- | | `0.5.0` | 可发布化：`engines.dsh`、`publishConfig`、`files` 纳入 `tools/`、壳补丁脚本自动探测安装路径、README 增加三条安装路径与发布清单 | | `0.4.28`–`0.4.31` | 调试日志：默认关闭，⚙ 菜单一键开关，环形缓冲 + 诊断卡片复制；新增 `log` 探针；工具行精简为「重新加载 / 外开 / 设置」 | | `0.4.32`–`0.4.33` | 设置里显示「跨重启保持登录」状态（按 `persist:` 分区判定并记忆）；未开启时提供「复制打补丁命令」 | | `0.4.27` | 文档重写并与实现对齐（README / architecture / 注释）；新增 `layout` 诊断探针 | | `0.4.25` | 删除旧的浮层/测量实现（`client.js` 3947 → 3243 行），行为不变 | | `0.4.15`–`0.4.22` | 诊断探针（`dom` / `prefer` / `openRight`）、`preferSeat` 席位偏好、"哪边点哪边接管" | | `0.4.13` | 左栏入口直接挂载聊天页（不再渲染入口页） | | `0.4.0` | 内联宿主：聊天页渲染在席位布局盒里，几何交给 CSS | | `0.3.0` | 多标签、每服务独立分区与租约、拖动排序、⚙ 设置、ⓘ 诊断 | > 完整改动见 `git log`。 --- ## 路线图 1. **多壳适配**：Tauri / `window.__DSH_CHAT_EMBED__` 自定义原生视窗协议。 2. **标签管理**：可关闭标签（释放租约）、可配置服务列表（走 Host `Config`）。 3. **内存策略**：LRU 回收久未使用的标签，切回时重建。 --- ## 反馈与贡献 - **Bug / 功能请求**：在仓库 issue 里描述现象 + 「⚙ → 标签页诊断… → 复制诊断信息」得到的报告（含 `build`、地址、分区、席位、自检），能大幅缩短定位时间。 - **补丁**：改 `client.js`（或 `index.js` / `tools`）→ `npm run check` 全绿 → 提交 PR。提交信息英文、文档中文。 - **本地开发**：无需依赖安装，见 [开发](#开发)。 - 联系方式：`fishsummer@126.com`。⚠️ 当前仓库**未配置远程地址**，issue/PR 入口需在配置 remote 后补充。 - 目前**没有邮件列表 / 聊天群组 / 官方网站**；相关通知以仓库提交记录与邮件为准。 --- ## 作者 poluce — `fishsummer@126.com`（维护者，GitHub 账号同 `poluce`；完整提交历史见 `git log`）。 --- ## 许可证与法律声明 - **许可证**：[MIT](LICENSE)。Copyright (c) 2026 dsh-chat-embed contributors。 - **无隶属**：与 DeepSeek、字节跳动（豆包）、OpenAI（ChatGPT）、MiniMax、月之暗面（Kimi）、Google（Gemini）、X（Grok）均无关联，相关商标归各自所有。 - **使用风险**：插件只是把各站点装进桌面 webview，登录的是**你的真实账号**，请遵守各站点的服务条款与当地法律；因使用第三方服务产生的账号、数据、风控问题由使用者自行承担。 - **免责**：软件按"现状"提供，不附带任何明示或暗示担保；作者不对因使用本软件造成的任何损失负责。

decision.reason: Held for package or companion artifact mapping. MIT, public Git-source install, a versioned DSH engine and committed client/host modules are present. Runtime relies on Electron lease/webview behavior; persistent login and layout instructions additionally patch the installed desktop shell. The exact companion shell build and those modifications are not mapped to this source snapshot. Browser account sessions and external provider pages were not opened. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# billion-context

English | 中文 | 日本語

Context-compression plugin — billion-context is all you need.

small context windows (100K is enough) · 5× fewer tokens · month-long single sessions (billions of tokens) · high compression quality

npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local

                                           

--- > **Cache health at a glance:** a healthy session keeps a **95–97%** prefix-cache hit rate — compression itself costs ≤2%. Sustained lower? Check attribution with `/acp` or `/acp-cache` (see [FAQ](#faq)); usual causes, in order: upstream cache TTL expiry · model switch · a bili bug (please report) · other/unknown. ## Community QQ Group: 1056132097 (full) 1108730198 (full) 1129868472 (open) --- ## 📄 Paper / Preprint - **[Model-Driven Incremental Hierarchical Compression: Training-Free Multi-Generational Context Management for Long-Lived Coding Agents](./paper/model-driven-incremental-hierarchical-compression-training-free-multi-generational-context-management-for-long-lived-coding-agents.md)** (English, v0.2) > 📝 **The paper itself is open-sourced under the MIT License as part of the codebase (`paper/`). It is a living document — anyone may edit it; improvements are welcome via pull request.** A production-scale longitudinal study: 4.5 months, three hosts, 174,327 model calls, 18.76B cumulative input tokens (~24.7B across all hosts), zero window violations on 204,800-token models, marathon sessions of 8,584–12,049 calls. ### 📊 Independent Third-Party Benchmarks - **[1,500-Item Cross-Benchmark Evaluation (`LongMemEval-S` · `ContextBench` · `MemoryAgentBench`)](./benchmarks/third-party-1500/README.md)** ([中文版](./benchmarks/third-party-1500/README.zh-CN.md)) — head-to-head comparison of `billion-context` (`v0.1.202`) against `full` context and 3 RAG arms (`bm25`, `embedding`, `embedding-rerank`) with `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash`, `Qwen3-Embedding-8B`, `Qwen3-Reranker-4B`, and `Pi Agent`: **#1 on ContextBench** (`0.3097` Utilized F1, `-58.3%` cost vs `full`), **+16.6% over best RAG on LongMemEval-S** (`79.20%` vs `62.60%`, `-71.1%` independent-session cost vs `full`), and **100% survival on 1.48M-token MemoryAgentBench TTL** (`30×` steady-state compression where `full` fails `199/199`). --- `billion-context` sits between **any** agent and its model API, rewriting Anthropic/OpenAI streams with [acp-kernel](https://github.com/ranxianglei/acp-kernel) compression. The model decides **when** and **what** to compress into high-fidelity summaries — not a hard truncation limit. ## Why Long coding sessions blow up context. Each provider charges per token, and once you pass the context window the session degrades or dies. `billion-context` compresses consumed conversation into layered summaries so you can run a single session for days — billions of tokens through one context window. Unlike a host's built-in summarizer, compression here is **incremental, reversible, and prefix-cache friendly**: summaries are written in small ranges, can be decompressed on demand, and the cache prefix stays intact. ## How it works ![How it works](docs/how-it-works.en.svg) ### Context-management tools The proxy injects four context-management tools into the conversation; the model calls them itself as context grows, and the proxy executes `compress` server-side so folded ranges stay summarized in history until restored: - **`compress`** — fold a message range into a detailed summary. - **`decompress`** — restore a compressed range when exact details are needed again. - **`search_context`** — keyword search over compressed summaries and visible messages. - **`acp_status`** — context-usage overview plus which ranges are still compressible. ## Which do I need? Pick by your client: | Client | Use | |---|---| | **pi** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili pi` (launcher) or `bili plugin install pi` (native); standalone [`billion-context-pi`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context-pi) remains usable — details: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md#pi-pidev-coding-agent) | | **opencode** (1.x / 2.x) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili opencode` (launcher) or `bili plugin install opencode` (native); standalone [`opencode-acp`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/opencode-acp) remains usable on 1.x — full guide: [OpenCode](docs/clients.md#opencode) | | **omp** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili omp` (built-in plugin) or `bili plugin install omp` (self-spawning native plugin, no launcher) | | **dsh** | `bili dsh` (launcher — full native plugin via `--patch`) or `bili plugin install dsh` ≡ `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` (one unified lane) — details: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md) | | **kimi** | `bili plugin install kimi` (self-spawning native, Kimi Code ≥ 2.0.0) or `bili kimi` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — details: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md) | | **hermes** | `bili plugin install hermes` (self-spawning native, Python plugin #958) or `bili hermes` (cert-MITM) | | **zcode** (Z.ai / bigmodel coding plan) | `bili plugin install zcode` (self-spawning native, #1145) or cert-MITM via the GUI's Settings → Network or `/bili/` prefix — details: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md) | | **claude** | `bili claude` (launcher) or `bili plugin install claude` (native posture, #964 — managed settings block + session-owned proxy; see the notes below) | | **codex** | `bili codex` (launcher — the full zero-config posture) or `bili plugin install codex` (MCP-shell tools companion: **start bili first** — the shell never spawns a proxy and never routes codex's own traffic) — details: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md#codex-openai-codex-cli) | | **jcode** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili jcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (compiled Rust binary, no plugin seam, [#962](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/962)) | | **gemini** (Gemini CLI) | `bili gemini` (launcher, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix — launcher-only (no in-loop tool seam, #1043) | | **iflow** (iFlow CLI) | `bili iflow` (launcher, `IFLOW_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix | | **qwen** (Qwen Code) | `bili qwen` (launcher, cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix | | **antigravity** (Antigravity CLI / agy, Google) | `bili antigravity` (launcher, `CLOUD_CODE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite of daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com — Antigravity's real default upstream, #3129) or `/bili/` prefix — no plugin seam (closed Go language_server; its user-plugin surface is additive-only, #2115) — details: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md) | | **mcode** (MiniMax Code) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili mcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (event hooks only, no model-request seam, [#1050](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1050)) | | **aider** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili aider` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (shell-command-only hooks, no tool-injection seam, [#1048](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1048)) | | **copilot** (GitHub Copilot CLI) | `bili copilot` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **amp** (Amp CLI) | `bili amp` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **kiro** (Kiro CLI, AWS) | `bili kiro` (launcher, cert-MITM) — Rust shell + Node agent server, no plugin seam; model traffic is the Responses wire on `runtime..kiro.dev`, gateway quirks handled built-in — details: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md#kiro-cli-aws) | | **crush** (Charm Crush) | `bili crush` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Go binary, no plugin seam; built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `base_url`s auto-discovered from crush.json (#2340) | | **zed** (Zed editor) | `bili zed` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Rust editor, no plugin seam; reqwest honors HTTPS_PROXY, CA via SSL_CERT_FILE (Linux env probing); built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `api_url`s auto-discovered from settings.json; loopback providers (ollama/lmstudio) stay direct via NO_PROXY (#2340) | | **goose** (Goose CLI) | `bili goose` (launcher) — rustls trusts no CA file, so no cert-MITM: openai/anthropic legs via `OPENAI_HOST`/`ANTHROPIC_HOST`, custom providers via a regenerated `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT` overlay (#1049) | | **everything else** (no context hook) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili ` (launcher, preferred) or `/bili/` prefix | **Native mode vs standalone extensions.** The host-native plugins (`bili plugin install …`) and the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) are **mutually exclusive** — both active means double compression. The installer makes the switch: it replaces the legacy entries (bare name, `npm:` alias, versioned, path form; array or object shape) and snapshots the original config to `.bili-bak` once; a **project-local** install is not touched — remove that one by hand. As a runtime safety net for manual installs, the native entries set `BILLION_CONTEXT_NATIVE=` synchronously at load so a standalone extension can stand down at action time. On the pi side the marker needs `billion-context-pi` **0.1.72+**, and the pi-native entry scans both pi settings files once its proxy is up and warns loudly when it spots a co-resident legacy entry the installer never saw — that warning is the only visible signal while an old `billion-context-pi` silently double-compresses. ## Install Linux / macOS — install with a user-level prefix (no `sudo`, no npm config changes, and `bili`'s self-update never hits permission errors): ```bash npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local ``` The `bili` command lands in `~/.local/bin` — already on PATH in most distros; if not, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. On nvm or Homebrew Node the default prefix is already user-owned — a plain `npm install -g billion-context` works as-is. On Windows the default prefix (`%APPDATA%\npm`) is also user-writable — plain `npm install -g billion-context`. This installs the `bili` command (`bili-proxy` is kept as an alias). Hitting `EACCES` with an old root-owned prefix? Reinstall with `--prefix=~/.local` (pass the flag again on any future npm reinstall of `bili`) — that is the permanent fix; avoid `sudo`. Prefer containers? A `Dockerfile` ships at the repository root — see [Running in Docker](#running-in-docker) below. ## Quickstart Three ways to use it — pick one: - **Native plugin (most native):** `bili plugin install ` — bili becomes a plugin inside the client; start the client as usual. - **Launcher (config-free):** one `bili ` command brings up the proxy and the client together — no real config file is ever touched. - **URL change (most universal):** prefix your client's baseURL with the proxy origin + `/bili/`. Mechanism details behind these three options (plugin lifecycle, runtime-info protocol, injection priority) live in [docs/technical-notes.md](docs/technical-notes.md). Ports, briefly (#1660): `bili start` (manual) owns `8787`. Everything a lane spawns for you (native hooks, launcher lanes) lives in a separate self-managed zone starting at `18787` — collisions hop +1 and each lane remembers its drift, so zero-config installs never fight you for a port, and a deliberate `bili start` daemon is attached by default. Attach is lane-aware (#2905): a hook rides its own lane's instance first, NEVER another declared lane's — except lanes you list in `native.attachLanePriority` — and the 8787 user-zone daemon stays the LAST-resort fallback. An upgrade-restart that finds the previous build still draining on the lane's port waits for it to release (up to 5s) and rebinds the SAME port instead of drifting (#1723); only a genuinely occupied port hops +1 — and that hop is now logged loudly. ### Option 1 — Native plugin (`bili plugin install pi` / `omp` / `opencode` / `dsh` / `kimi` / `hermes` / `zcode`) The proxy lives inside the client: install once, then start the client exactly as you always do — no launcher command, no env vars, no fixed port, no URL edits. Supported today for **pi**, **omp**, **opencode** (1.x and 2.x), **dsh**, **kimi**, **hermes** and **zcode**: ```bash bili plugin install pi # registers a "billion-context" entry in pi's settings (npm form when bili itself was npm-installed) bili plugin install omp # registers an extensions entry in omp's config.yml (~/.omp/agent/config.yml) bili plugin install opencode # registers the plugin in opencode's real config + disables native auto-compaction bili plugin install dsh # runs 'dsh plugin --profile add billion-context' for every existing profile bili plugin install kimi # writes $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/billion-context/kimi.plugin.json (+ installed.json record); per-session routing block lands in config.toml on first start (Kimi Code >= 2.0.0) bili plugin install hermes # copies the Python plugin into ~/.hermes/plugins/billion-context/ (+ machine-owned bili.json sidecar) and enables it via `hermes plugins enable billion-context` bili plugin install zcode # writes hooks.enabled + a SessionStart hook + mcp.servers.bili into ~/.zcode/cli/config.json; per-session routing lands in the bigmodel provider store on first start bili plugin remove # undo (dsh removes through the same channel; config snapshots go to .bili-bak) ``` Where a client has its own plugin channel you can also install natively, skipping bili commands entirely: - **dsh:** `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` is the very command `bili plugin install dsh` drives per profile (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry — pasting a GitHub address installs source without `dist/` and the bundle never loads) — same end state either way (pnpm into the profile, bundled patch layer mounted by dsh itself); remove through the same channel. See the dsh section below. - **opencode:** easiest is `bili plugin install opencode` (it picks the right entry form for your host version). Hand-install without bili (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry): - **OpenCode 1.x** — add the bare npm name to your real config's plugin list: `"plugin": ["billion-context"]`. The package publishes `exports["./server"]` → `dist/agent/opencode-native.js`, so opencode loads it through its own Npm.add machinery and the plugin self-spawns exactly like the bili-installed form. - **OpenCode 2.x** — the bare name does NOT work: 2.x resolves it through the package `main` field (`dist/index.js`, the CLI — no plugin definition), so the module load fails (#3976). Instead, put a one-line re-export in a directory and point the config's `plugins` list at that directory: ```js // /index.js export { default } from "/dist/agent/opencode-native.js"; ``` ```json { "plugins": [""] } ``` Either generation: do the two things the bili installer would have done for you too — set `"compaction": { "auto": false }` in the same config (otherwise OpenCode's native auto-compaction double-compresses) and keep a manual backup of the file first. - **claude:** this repository doubles as a Claude Code plugin marketplace — `/plugin marketplace add ranxianglei/billion-context`, then `/plugin install billion-context@billion-context`, then run `/billion-context:bili-setup` (it drives `bili plugin install claude` for you and tells you to restart). Same end state as the bili installer; the plugin ships no hooks or MCP entries of its own, so nothing double-registers. For pi / omp / kimi / claude there is no client-side channel — `bili plugin install ` writes their config entries for you (kimi's declarative `kimi.plugin.json` + registry record, claude's managed settings block, …). Notes: - Native mode is **mutually exclusive** with the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) — the installer swaps the entries and snapshots the original config (`.bili-bak`). - **pi:** native installs wire in built-in subagents by default (`acp_delegate` / `acp_delegate_wait` / `acp_delegate_cancel`) — how to disable them while keeping context compression: [Pi built-in subagents](#pi-built-in-subagents). - OpenCode legacy sessions, V1/V2 shapes and caveats: [OpenCode](docs/clients.md#opencode). - `kimi` reports runtime-info at bootstrap only (static headers can't carry per-request window/model values); subagent tool calls are routed by the proxy's outbound tool-use witness ring (#1685) — no model-visible conversation id. - `hermes`'s native plugin is Python: it points hermes' httpx stack at the proxy via env vars after a health check and stamps per-request headers through an `llm_request` middleware. - `codex` is the one client a plugin install cannot make self-sufficient: codex routes model traffic via env only (no config-file routing seam for the default ChatGPT-login provider — a managed `model_providers` block would force API-key auth and drop subscription login), and an MCP server cannot inject env into its parent. `bili plugin install codex` writes a single `[mcp_servers.bili]` block into `~/.codex/config.toml` (command = node, args = dist/mcp.js) exposing the four ACP tools; at session start the shell resolves a proxy — env `BILI_MCP_PROXY` > the live-instance record (any lane's proxy or a `bili start` daemon) > the 8787 user-zone default (#1660 removed the install-time origin bake, #403) — nothing reachable → `tools/list` fails with -32003. So: start bili first (`bili start` or any client's lane proxy), export HTTPS_PROXY yourself if you also want compression, or use `bili codex` for the zero-config full posture. Mechanics: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md#codex-openai-codex-cli). - `claude` has a native posture (#964): managed settings block + `SessionStart` hook + MCP shell; the hook rides the self-managed port zone (#1660) and re-pins the managed URL to the live origin each session, so port drift self-heals. Since #1821 the MCP shell also watches the proxy mid-session (30 s tick × 3 failures) and respawns a dead lane proxy itself, so model requests recover within ~90 s instead of a new session (same semantics as the zcode lane). Opt out with `BILI_NATIVE_CLAUDE=0` (passthrough). Mechanics: [docs/technical-notes.md](docs/technical-notes.md). **Known limitation (#2290):** the Claude Desktop app's Code tab (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=claude-desktop`) sets its own `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on its embedded Claude Code, overriding the managed one — desktop sessions bypass the proxy entirely while the managed block's `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1` still applies, so they get neither bili compression nor native auto-compaction. The hook warns loudly at session start (and records it for `bili doctor`, which also flags machines where Claude Desktop is installed alongside the native lane); terminal sessions are unaffected. **Field-tested 2026-10-06 (#2290):** putting `HTTPS_PROXY` in the settings `env` block produced zero CONNECT traffic to a live MITM-enabled proxy on Claude Desktop 2.19675.1 / embedded CC 2.1.288 (Windows 11) — the variable reaches no network stack there, matching the CLI behavior of that era — note that newer builds (CC 2.1.301+) DO honour `HTTPS_PROXY` on the CLI, which is why `bili claude` routes via the `/bili/` base-URL rewrite — the launcher gives this lane no proxy and no CA at all, and a child that brings a proxy of its own gets the loopback hosts merged into `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` so that leg stays direct regardless of its proxy behavior (#3446). As of that version there is no usable routing seam on the desktop Code tab; the lane stays tracked in [#2290](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/2290) in case upstream changes behavior. **Account-bound features (#4693):** because the lane routes via a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, Claude Code treats the session as third-party/API-key and disables features bound to your Anthropic account/Cloud — **Remote Control** (`/remote-control`, driving a local session from mobile/desktop/web) disappears from the command list while bili routes traffic. Compression is unaffected; run plain `claude` without bili (or `bili plugin remove claude`) for sessions that need those features. This is inherent to the base-URL routing seam — no alternative interception point survives CC's undici stack (#2290) — not a config deletion. Desktop-only users can restore native auto-compact with `bili plugin remove claude`. Since #5095 the managed block also installs a `SubagentStart` hook (`node /dist/claude-subagent-hook.js`) that mints a per-dispatch lane token into each subagent's context: subagents that ride the parent's session id with no agent-id headers (the VS Code extension build, #4352) key onto their own `|sub:…:t:` compression lanes, so parallel same-type dispatches stop merging (and the token disappears from later requests once the first message folds — those fall back to the fingerprint lane). Uninstall removes the hook with the managed block. - `zcode` has a native posture (#1145): managed `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` block + per-session provider `baseURL` rewrite. Full mechanics: [docs/clients.md](docs/clients.md). - `jcode` and `aider` have no native mode (no plugin/MCP/tool-injection seam: #962, #1048) — use `bili jcode` / `bili aider`. - `copilot`, `amp` and `goose` are launcher-only (#1049); goose cannot be cert-MITMed (rustls trusts no CA file) and rides plain-HTTP base-URL redirects instead. ### Option 2 — Launcher (`bili pi` / `bili codex` / `bili claude` / `bili omp` / `bili opencode` / `bili hermes` / `bili dsh` / `bili codebuddy` / `bili qoder` / `bili trae` / `bili jcode` / `bili kimi` / `bili gemini` / `bili iflow` / `bili qwen` / `bili antigravity` / `bili mcode` / `bili aider` / `bili copilot` / `bili amp` / `bili goose` / `bili kiro`) The launcher wraps a client in one command: it starts a proxy on an independent port (a fresh instance is always spawned — a port is never reused), then points the client at it — **certificate-based MITM** where the client honors proxy/CA env vars, or an isolated **`/bili/` config rewrite** where it doesn't. No real config file is ever edited; the client's own config is READ to discover which HTTPS upstream hosts it talks to, and those hosts are whitelisted for MITM so the proxy can TLS-terminate exactly them and blind-tunnel everything else. ```bash bili pi # launch pi through the proxy — file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider, real ~/.pi untouched bili codex # launch codex through the proxy bili claude # launch claude through the proxy bili omp # pi-style, file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider + compaction cancel, real ~/.omp untouched bili opencode # OpenCode (1.x & 2.x): full guide in the [OpenCode](docs/clients.md#opencode) section below bili hermes # file-free (#535): hermes proxy env (HTTPS_PROXY + combined CA bundle via SSL_CERT_FILE) — https via CONNECT MITM, http via absolute-form forward proxy; real ~/.hermes untouched bili dsh # deepseek-harness: full native plugin injected via --patch (#941) — real dsh tools, session-bound /acp + /acp-cache (plugin mode); non-loopback upstreams ride proxy envs, loopback keeps the overlay DSH_HOME rewrite (#535); dsh auto-compaction off everywhere — host plane via the bundle patch, web-profile presets at load time (#1772/#2474/#3354) bili codebuddy # Tencent CodeBuddy Code CLI: CODEBUDDY_BASE_URL /bili/ rewrite (OpenAI chat completions wire), budget aligned via CODEBUDDY_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW; real ~/.codebuddy untouched bili qoder # qoder CLI (`qoder`/`qodercli`): model endpoint is hardcoded https (no /bili/ rewrite possible) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, default model hosts whitelisted (#653). Qoder Desktop is a separate BYOK/custom channel that speaks plaintext OpenAI over a `/bili/` prefix — point it at bili as a normal custom provider (not this MITM lane); its official-subscription traffic is encrypted and out of scope (#764) bili trae # Trae CLI (ByteDance, closed Go binary, no base-URL override) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE, model host from TRAE_CLI_API_HOST or the default enterprise gateway (#655) bili jcode

# DSH 输入助手

简体中文 | [English](README.en.md)

[![CI](https://github.com/Somnus678/dsh-input-assistant/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Somnus678/dsh-input-assistant/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Somnus678/dsh-input-assistant)](https://github.com/Somnus678/dsh-input-assistant/releases)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)
[![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.1--rc.2-purple)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-203%20passed-brightgreen)](docs/validation.md)

[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的输入框增强插件：**提示词优化**、**下一句预测**、**输入续写**、**草稿暂存**。

当前源码版本为 **0.1.4**，包含预测详略度、预设、独立预测按钮、预览采纳、手动重试、草稿复制及辅助模型选择。可从当前源码构建并安装本地 `dist/dsh-input-assistant-0.1.4.tgz`；公开发布情况请参见 [Releases](https://github.com/Somnus678/dsh-input-assistant/releases)。

![优化界面](docs/images/optimize.png)

截图来自本地浏览器夹具，使用正式组件、宿主主题及模拟模型输出。

## 功能

| 功能 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **提示词优化** | 把草稿或选中文字改写成更准确、可发送的表达。三档强度（轻/标准/深度），先预览差异，采纳后写入，可还原。 |
| **下一句预测** | 回复完成后预测你接下来可能说的话，以灰字提示，Tab 采纳，不发送。 |
| **输入续写** | 根据当前草稿预测后续内容，停顿时间与最小间隔可调。 |
| **手动建议与重试** | 点击独立「预测」按钮生成一次；自动建议关闭时仍可使用，失败后可明确重试。 |
| **详略度与预设** | 简明、标准、详尽三档；详尽允许多行，始终遵守长度上限。三种预设经保存后生效。 |
| **草稿暂存** | 当前会话最多保留 3 份草稿，点击“暂存并清空”先保存再清空，显式恢复；删除后 10 秒内可撤销。 |

深色与浅色主题均已适配：

| 浅色 | 深色 |
|---|---|
| ![浅色](docs/images/light.png) | ![深色](docs/images/dark.png) |

### 保护机制

改写时会识别并锁定以下内容：

- 代码块（``` 和 ~~~）与行内代码
- URL（含平衡括号）与盘符绝对路径（`C:\...`）
- 正斜线或反斜线相对路径与常见文件名（`src/core/generation.ts`、`src\index.ts`、`package.json`、`.env`、`.gitignore`）
- 你显式锁定的片段

占位符被模型篡改、丢失或重复时，插件拒绝该结果并保留你的原稿。

带空格的 Windows 路径支持引号边界，未加引号时会按文件名、标点或行尾识别。目录名和后续自然语言存在歧义时，请用引号、反引号或手动锁定，避免依赖自动识别。片段完整不等于语义不变，采纳前仍需审阅。

中文紧贴普通文件名时会切出文件本身，例如“请修改package.json中的scripts”。未引用的纯中文文件名与紧贴的中文说明仍可能存在歧义；混合中英文名称请使用引号、反引号或手动锁定。

### 失败不丢稿

优化、续写、预测在超时、取消、网络失败、模型空输出时都保留原稿，只给出提示。一次瞬时状态轮询失败不会中断正在进行的手动优化。

## 安装

需要 **Node.js >= 22.19** 和 **DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` 或 `0.2.1-rc.3`**。安装预构建 `.tgz` 不需要在本地编译 TypeScript。

构建本版后，将以下路径指向本地包并安装到 Web profile：

```powershell
dsh --version                                  # 确认 0.2.1-rc.2 或 rc.3
dsh plugin --profile web add (Resolve-Path './dist/dsh-input-assistant-0.1.4.tgz').Path
dsh --profile web --dump-config                # 应看到 dsh-input-assistant 层
dsh --profile web
```

已发布的 GitHub 安装包可从 [Releases](https://github.com/Somnus678/dsh-input-assistant/releases) 下载，请核对版本号和文件来源。

官方桌面端使用自己的 `desktop` profile（默认 Windows 安装位置）：

```powershell
$dsh = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd'
& $dsh --version
& $dsh plugin --profile desktop add (Resolve-Path './dist/dsh-input-assistant-0.1.4.tgz').Path
```

安装或升级后**完全退出并重新打开 DSH**，插件才会加载。

如果曾安装其他内容的同名 0.1.4 包，请先核对安装包的来源与 SHA256，并在重启后核对实际加载的插件文件。同版本缓存可能复用旧文件；仅看到版本号相同不能证明已更新。

### 卸载

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-input-assistant
```

同样需要重启对应实例。卸载**不会**清除插件保存的草稿与设置（存在宿主私有 storage 中）。

### 从源码构建

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Somnus678/dsh-input-assistant.git
cd dsh-input-assistant
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm pack --pack-destination dist
```

## 快速上手

1. 安装后重启 DSH，输入框右侧出现**「优化」「预测」按钮**和快捷菜单。
2. 在输入框写入草稿，点「优化」，查看差异后决定**采纳优化**或**保留原文**；等待期间可取消。
3. 左下角账号菜单 → **设置 → 输入助手**，可分别开关四个模块、调整强度与高级参数。

> **默认会调用模型。** `下一句预测` 和 `输入续写` 默认开启，会在你输入时自动发起请求。若只想手动使用优化功能或控制成本，请先在设置中关闭这两项。

## 设置项

| 设置 | 默认 | 范围 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 提示词优化 | 开 | — | 是否启用优化 |
| 草稿暂存 | 开 | — | 是否启用“暂存并清空”与恢复 |
| 下一句预测 | 开 | — | 回复后是否预测下一句 |
| 输入续写 | 开 | — | 输入时是否预测后续内容 |
| 优化强度 | 标准 | 轻/标准/深度 | 改写幅度 |
| 预测详略度 | 标准 | 简明/标准/详尽 | 不会自动提高长度上限；详尽使用可滚动的候选面板 |
| 显示方式 | ghost | ghost/panel | 灰字或面板 |
| 下一句长度上限 | 120 | 20–1000 | Unicode 字符上限 |
| 续写长度上限 | 80 | 10–500 | Unicode 字符上限 |
| 续写停顿 `debounceMs` | 600 | 200–5000 | 停止输入多久后触发 |
| 最小间隔 `minIntervalMs` | 2000 | 500–30000 | 两次续写请求的最小间隔 |
| 固定辅助模型 | 跟随输入框 | — | 可从宿主目录选择；高级选项支持手填 provider/model；留空跟随输入框模型 |

### 各功能怎么用

**优化整稿或选区**：输入草稿后点「优化」。原稿保持不变，结果以差异视图展示；点「采纳优化」才写入输入框，点「保留原文」或按 `Esc` 放弃预览。采纳后可在菜单点「还原」，或按一次 `Ctrl+Z` 恢复原文。

**下一句预测与输入续写**：预测结果以**灰字**或候选面板显示。详尽模式统一使用可滚动的面板，完整展示多行候选。按 `Tab` 采纳，按 `Esc` 或继续输入忽略。采纳**不会**发送消息。

**手动生成与重试**：点击「预测」或菜单中的「生成建议」，空稿时预测下一句，有草稿时续写。自动功能关闭时仍可使用，失败或正常弃权后可明确重试。输入框需为无附件、无引用的空闲纯文本，光标位于末尾。手动请求仍遵守宿主最小间隔；限流时最多延后重试一次，不会循环调用。页面隐藏会停止自动建议，重新可见后再判断是否触发。

**暂存长草稿**：在菜单点击「暂存并清空」，保存成功后才清空输入（最多 3 份）。可显式追加或替换恢复；切换会话、切换模型、断线重连后暂存仍在该会话下。删除或清空暂存后，可在 10 秒内撤销；撤销不会覆盖其他窗口新保存的草稿，容量不足时会提示先释放空间再重试。

保存期间可点「取消清空」保留输入，已开始的保存仍会完成。保存中编辑草稿、切换模型或修改设置，也只保存原快照并保留当前输入。该按钮不用于取消删除或撤销等存储操作。

**预设档位**：「敏捷模式」「标准平衡」「节流省流」只修改设置表单，点击「保存设置」后才全局生效，不会立即生成。滑块用于快速调整，数值框支持范围内的精确整数，如 601 毫秒。

最近一次删除的 10 秒撤销期限不会因切走会话再返回而改变。撤销失败的目标单独保留在当前插件运行内，后续删除不会覆盖该目标；可重试、复制或主动放弃。两批备份均恢复失败时，会先要求处理一批，避免继续删除覆盖备份。插件卸载或连接切换会释放这些内存备份。草稿卡和待恢复备份都支持复制，复制不受当前输入附件或引用限制。

功能开关、显示方式、辅助模型和高级参数集中在 **设置 → 输入助手**，均为全局设置。快捷菜单只保留常用操作，并明确标注优化强度的全局作用范围。

辅助模型选择只保存插件自己的路由，不切换主会话模型；目录部分失败或不支持目录接口时，可刷新或使用高级手动填写，已有选择会保留。输入、优化和暂存的字数预算均按 Unicode 码点统计。

## 兼容性

| 项目 | 支持范围 |
|---|---|
| DSH | 声明 `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`；本轮测试依赖以 `0.2.1-rc.3` 为基准，完整宿主组合尚未验证 |
| Node.js | `>= 22.19` |
| 操作系统 | Windows x64（已验证）；macOS/Linux 未验证 |
| 浏览器测试 | Microsoft Edge |

## 已知边界

**这个插件没有完成完整的效果评测。** 请据此判断是否适合你的场景：

- 60 条固定合成质量集尚未跑完真实模型评测，也没有独立人工语义标注，状态为 `not_evaluated`。
- 6 次真实模型小样本对照只能说明链路可用（2,807 tokens），**不能证明效果优于同类工具**。
- 中文 IME 候选组合、附件/引用组合、完整官方 Web 组合、其他插件组合、非 Windows x64 平台均未验证。
- 声明允许 `0.2.1-rc.2` 至 `<0.3.0-0`；本版未对声明范围内每个宿主版本完成实机验证。

详见 [验收记录](docs/validation.md) 与 [低用量真实模型试验](docs/smoke-comparison.md)。

## 数据与隐私

- 不收集遥测，不上传使用数据。
- 草稿与设置存在宿主 DSH 的私有 storage。
- 模型调用走宿主已配置的提供商；插件不持有或记录 API key。
- 优化/预测/续写会把当前草稿与相关上下文发给模型提供商 —— 这是功能必需，请按你所用提供商的数据政策评估。

详见 [安全策略](SECURITY.md)。

## 开发

```powershell
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck     # 类型检查
pnpm test          # 全量工程回归（含 Edge）
pnpm build         # 构建 lib/
pnpm pack --pack-destination dist # 先生成当前版本归档
pnpm test:package  # 校验打包产物（需先 pack）
pnpm test:web      # 真实 Edge 回归
pnpm test:package:web # 直接加载实际 .tgz 的 client/core 做 Edge 回归
```

贡献前请阅读 [贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING.md)。技术细节见 [0.1.2 修正记录](docs/CHANGELOG-0.1.2.md)。

### 持续集成

每次 push 和 PR 都会在 GitHub Actions 上自动运行 [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml)：

| Job | 环境 | 内容 |
|---|---|---|
| `test-windows` | `windows-latest` | 全量工程测试 + 源码与实际安装包的 Edge 回归 + 构建可复现性校验 |
| `test-linux` | `ubuntu-latest` | Node 22.19 与 24.19 矩阵，排除 Edge 专属渲染测试，验证核心/宿主/控制器及包消费者 |
| `package` | `ubuntu-latest` | 打包内容审计：必需文件齐全，且不含研究资料、缓存或测试夹具 |

`test-windows` 是权威结果：主题测试、`scripts/smoke-web.mjs` 和 `scripts/smoke-package.mjs` 使用
`chromium.launch({ channel: 'msedge' })` 驱动真实 Microsoft Edge 渲染已发布的 DSH 主题，
浏览器检查在无 Edge 的 Linux 上无法运行，因此覆盖由 Windows job 提供。

本地想复现 Linux job：

```powershell
pnpm vitest run --exclude 'tests/browser-theme.test.ts'
```

发布流程复用完整 CI，全部任务通过后才下载并发布其中已验证的同一份 `.tgz`，同时校验 tag 与包版本一致。

推送 `v*` 标签会触发 npm 发布工作流，需要仓库配置 `NPM_TOKEN`；该工作流不会自动创建 GitHub Release。如需在 GitHub 提供下载，需在 CI 成功后另行创建 Release 并附上已验证的归档。发布前应确认版本号、标签和归档一致，且该版本尚未发布。

# dsh-lynn-sticker-mcp Optional, configuration-only DeepSeek Harness bundle that connects the Harness to the local Lynn-chan sticker MCP server. ## Prerequisites Start the local server (serves both the REST API and `POST /mcp`): ```bash npm run stickers:api # lynn-sticker api listening on http://127.0.0.1:4319 ``` ## Install From the repository root: ```bash # Plugin Manager -> Add local bundle -> /absolute/path/to/packages/dsh-sticker-mcp-bundle ``` The bundle inserts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` with `serverName: lynn_sticker` and exposes tools named `mcp__lynn_sticker__search_stickers`, `mcp__lynn_sticker__get_sticker`, `mcp__lynn_sticker__random_sticker` and `mcp__lynn_sticker__list_sticker_tags`. ## Why this is optional Every discovered MCP tool definition enters the model's tool list on every request. The direct `dsh-lynn-sticker` bundle exposes one compact `send_sticker` tool and renders the sticker inline, which is the context-efficient path for DeepSeek Harness. Use this MCP bundle only when you want a shared MCP namespace (for example, several agents or a non-DSH client). ## Not installed by default Nothing in this repository installs this bundle automatically. Installing both bundles is allowed but adds the MCP tool schemas to every request. # Lynn-chan Stickers
## 使用 Sticker ### Telegram ![2025-12-03 00.53.53.png](https://s2.loli.net/2025/12/03/RnpxzAsYZw6FqDP.png) [在 Telegram 中添加 Lynn-chan Sticker Pack](https://t.me/addstickers/lynnchan) 动态贴纸（2026-11-06 发布，共 181 张）： - [Lynn Sticker @stvlynn 1 · 120 张](https://t.me/addstickers/lynn_sticker_stvlynn_1_by_lynn_ai_bot) - [Lynn Sticker @stvlynn 2 · 61 张](https://t.me/addstickers/lynn_sticker_stvlynn_2_by_lynn_ai_bot) 网站支持“静态／动态”标签切换、当前类型内搜索，以及动态贴纸 WebM 原文件下载。动态贴纸仅在可见区域静音循环播放，开启系统“减少动态效果”后显示静态预览。 ### 微信 ![sticker.weixin.qq.com_cgi-bin_mmemoticonwebnode-bin_pages_stickerPage_setting_stikerid_stiker_176451914991ba5a1d2bd4a81f.png](https://s2.loli.net/2025/12/03/5uGkTNDiHsfF8MQ.png) [在微信中使用 Lynn-chan Sticker](https://w.url.cn/s/AhlJ5Bk) --- ## 关于 Lynn 酱 | | | |---|---| | Lynn 酱是由 [Steven Lynn](https://x.com/Stv_Lynn) 设计的 OC，经过多次迭代最终形成现在的样子。

最新一版的 OC 来自于 [YAYOI の 夢](https://x.com/Yayoi_no_yume)，从此转为了白毛的形象～ | ![Lynn OC](./oc.png) | ## 如何贡献 欢迎向 Lynn-chan Sticker 库贡献你的创意作品！ ### 提交步骤 1. Fork 本仓库 2. 在 `public/stickers/` 文件夹内添加你的 PNG 图片 3. 提交 PR ### 设计建议 推荐使用 **gemini-3-pro-preview** 生成 Sticker。以下是推荐的 Prompt： ```text 将角色变形并设计一张 LINE 贴纸。姿势和文字排版要富有创意，变化丰富，设计独特。 对话应为简体中文，参考 sticker 示例。 使用文本"[YOUR_TEXT]"，动作是[YOUR_ACTION]。 图片整体使用浅灰色 RGB(240, 240, 240) 背景，文字和角色周围有白色描边。 ``` **示例：** ```text 将角色变形并设计一张 LINE 贴纸。姿势和文字排版要富有创意，变化丰富，设计独特。 对话应为简体中文，参考 sticker 示例。 使用文本"干饭"，动作是开心地吃饭。 图片整体使用浅灰色 RGB(240, 240, 240) 背景，文字和角色周围有白色描边。 ``` ## 请求新 Sticker 如果你有想要的 Sticker 创意，欢迎提交 Issue！ ### Issue 格式 ```markdown **Sticker 名称：** [中文名称] **描述：** [简要描述这个 sticker 的内容、场景、表情等] **文本建议：** [希望在 sticker 上显示的文本] **参考：** [可选：参考其他 sticker 或参考图片] ``` **示例：** ```markdown **Sticker 名称：** 加班中 **描述：** Lynn 酱疲惫地工作，眼神无神，咖啡杯在旁边 **文本建议：** 又是加班的一天 **参考：** 参考 "在忙.png" 的风格 ``` ## Agent 接入 贴纸库同时提供三种 agent 接入方式，详见 [docs/sticker-agent-stack.md](docs/sticker-agent-stack.md)： - **Catalog API**：`packages/sticker-catalog/catalog.json`，覆盖 80 张静态贴纸和 181 张动态贴纸。 - **REST / MCP**：`npm run stickers:api` 启动本地 API（含 `/mcp`），`npm run stickers:mcp` 启动 MCP stdio 服务。 - **DeepSeek Harness 插件**：安装 `packages/dsh-sticker` 后，agent 可以在合适的时候调用 `send_sticker`，贴纸直接显示在对话里；匹配时优先选择动态贴纸。模型会根据提示词中的适用时机主动选择；任务相关的 `tools/post-execute` hook 会在修改类工具结束后提示模型自行决定是否发一张贴纸。 插件本身只有约 70 KB，不打包任何贴纸图片/WebM； 图片和动态图按需从 `https://sticker.stv.pm` 加载。贴纸媒体和完整 catalog 都不会进入模型上下文。 ```bash npm run stickers:build # 生成 catalog、public/catalog.json、MCP 静帧和插件元数据 npm run stickers:api # REST API + MCP HTTP，默认 127.0.0.1:4319 npm run stickers:mcp # MCP stdio npm run stickers:verify # 端到端校验 npm run stickers:pack # 打包 dsh-lynn-sticker 插件 ``` 插件安装：在 Plugin Manager 中添加本地 bundle 目录 `/absolute/path/to/packages/dsh-sticker`， 或发布后安装 npm 包。`sticker.stv.pm` 已提供 `/catalog.json`，插件会按 TTL（默认 5 分钟） 在后台刷新贴纸元数据；贴纸图片和 WebM 也直接按需从站点加载。MCP 客户端配置示例和上下文开销 说明见 [docs/sticker-agent-stack.md](docs/sticker-agent-stack.md)。 ## 协议 本项目中的所有 Sticker 作品采用 **CC BY 4.0** 协议。 - ✅ 可以自由使用、修改和分享 - ✅ 必须署名原作者 - ❌ **禁止商用** 详见 [CC BY 4.0 协议](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) ## 技术栈 - **框架：** Next.js 14 + React 18 - **样式：** Tailwind CSS - **动画：** Framer Motion - **图标：** Lucide React ## 本地开发 ```bash # 安装依赖 npm install # 启动开发服务器 npm run dev # 访问 http://localhost:3000 ``` ### 同步已发布的动态贴纸 资源及来源、顺序和 SHA-256 记录分别保存在 `public/stickers/animated/` 与 `src/data/animated-stickers.json`，运行网站无需 OpenSticker 项目。需要从发布工作目录重新同步时： ```bash node scripts/sync-animated-stickers.mjs ~/code/OpenSticker/.workspace/lynn-telegram ``` 脚本只导入 `pack-plan.json` 中已发布的条目，并核对 `published.json` 的数量和每个 WebM 的 SHA-256。 --- Made with ❤️ by [Steven Lynn](https://x.com/Stv_Lynn)

decision.reason: The fixed manifest is an optional composition that configures the official MCP client to connect to the local sticker MCP server, not its own native implementation. The separate packages/dsh-sticker host/client implementation is the repository representative.
