evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-lynn-sticker A DeepSeek Harness bundle that lets an agent send a Lynn-chan sticker inline in the conversation when the moment fits — without putting the sticker catalog or any image into model context. - One compact model tool: `send_sticker({ mood, id? })`; when several stickers fit, the matcher prefers an animated one (with a small score bonus) and the prompt asks the model to do the same. - One short system-prompt hint, about 55 words. - One-line tool results (`Sent sticker "摸鱼".`), no images or base64 in model context. - The sticker is rendered at the **end of the completed turn** through `conversation.chat.turnTail`, so it is visible in normal conversation flow without expanding the collapsed tool-call group. The browser loads the media on demand from **https://sticker.stv.pm**; animated stickers play the site's WebM and fall back to the poster under reduced motion. - The npm package bundles **no sticker media** — only the compact matching metadata (`lib/catalog.json`, ~120 KB) and the host/client code. The published tarball is ~70 KB. - A soft limit of one sticker per assistant turn. - Task lifecycle hook: after a substantive tool result (`edit`, `write`, `apply_patch`, `bash`, terminal), the host appends one short context note asking the model to decide whether this is a natural sticker moment. The model chooses; the host does not hardcode intent rules or pick a sticker. The expanded tool description and prompt hint spell out the moments where a sticker is appropriate (greeting, thanks, celebration, frustration, a funny failure, a break). ## Install The package is published to npm as `dsh-lynn-sticker`: ```text plugin_manager install_bundle target=dsh-lynn-sticker@1.2.0 ``` Or install the local bundle directory (from this checkout): ```text plugin_manager install_bundle target=/Users/steven/code/sticker/packages/dsh-sticker ``` The local directory install links the checkout, so the committed `lib/catalog.json` is used directly. No generated media is required. ## Use The agent calls: ```json { "mood": "今天终于上线了，开心" } ``` The tool resolves the best sticker server-side and returns one line to the model. The UI loads the sticker image/WebM from `sticker.stv.pm` and shows it inline. Passing `id` (for example `s-65`) selects an exact sticker from a previous result. Use it sparingly: it is for warmth and humor, never a substitute for a substantive answer. ## What enters model context | Item | Approximate cost | |---|---| | Tool schema + description | ~150 tokens | | Prompt hint | ~70 tokens | | One send result | ~15 tokens | | Sticker image / video | 0 tokens (never sent to the model) | | Catalog metadata | 0 tokens (not injected; used only for matching) | A second `send_sticker` call in the same turn returns `Sticker skipped: already sent a sticker this turn.` and renders nothing. ## Media loading and dynamic catalog The host half builds absolute media URLs from a configurable base URL (default `https://sticker.stv.pm`): - Static sticker: `https://sticker.stv.pm/stickers/.png` - Animated sticker: poster `…/stickers/animated/.png` plus WebM `…/stickers/animated/.webm` Set `LYNN_STICKER_BASE_URL` in the DSH environment to point at a different deployment. The host also fetches `${LYNN_STICKER_BASE_URL}/catalog.json` in the background and swaps in the refreshed metadata if it is valid. Refreshes are TTL-based: at activation and on a tool call when the cached list is older than **5 minutes** (override with `LYNN_STICKER_CATALOG_TTL_MS`). The bundled `lib/catalog.json` is the offline fallback, so stickers keep working if the site is unreachable. Updating the deployed `public/catalog.json` therefore makes **new or retagged stickers** available without republishing the npm package; updating sticker images on the site needs no package change at all. ## Build and package (repository development) ```bash npm run stickers:build # canonical catalog + public/catalog.json + MCP stills + lib/catalog.json npm run stickers:pack # dist/dsh-lynn-sticker-1.2.0.tgz ``` The packaging script fails if any sticker media is bundled or if the catalog references a non-site-relative path. The tarball contains the host/client halves, `lib/catalog.json`, the patch, locales, icon and LICENSE — no images. ## License and attribution Sticker artwork and the plugin icon are licensed under **CC BY 4.0** by Steven Lynn () and contributors; keep the attribution when redistributing. The plugin icon is derived from `public/stickers/mhy.png`. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). See also the repository root [README](../../README.md) and [LICENSE](../../LICENSE). # Lynn-chan Stickers
## 使用 Sticker ### Telegram ![2025-12-03 00.53.53.png](https://s2.loli.net/2025/12/03/RnpxzAsYZw6FqDP.png) [在 Telegram 中添加 Lynn-chan Sticker Pack](https://t.me/addstickers/lynnchan) 动态贴纸（2026-11-06 发布，共 181 张）： - [Lynn Sticker @stvlynn 1 · 120 张](https://t.me/addstickers/lynn_sticker_stvlynn_1_by_lynn_ai_bot) - [Lynn Sticker @stvlynn 2 · 61 张](https://t.me/addstickers/lynn_sticker_stvlynn_2_by_lynn_ai_bot) 网站支持“静态／动态”标签切换、当前类型内搜索，以及动态贴纸 WebM 原文件下载。动态贴纸仅在可见区域静音循环播放，开启系统“减少动态效果”后显示静态预览。 ### 微信 ![sticker.weixin.qq.com_cgi-bin_mmemoticonwebnode-bin_pages_stickerPage_setting_stikerid_stiker_176451914991ba5a1d2bd4a81f.png](https://s2.loli.net/2025/12/03/5uGkTNDiHsfF8MQ.png) [在微信中使用 Lynn-chan Sticker](https://w.url.cn/s/AhlJ5Bk) --- ## 关于 Lynn 酱 | | | |---|---| | Lynn 酱是由 [Steven Lynn](https://x.com/Stv_Lynn) 设计的 OC，经过多次迭代最终形成现在的样子。

最新一版的 OC 来自于 [YAYOI の 夢](https://x.com/Yayoi_no_yume)，从此转为了白毛的形象～ | ![Lynn OC](./oc.png) | ## 如何贡献 欢迎向 Lynn-chan Sticker 库贡献你的创意作品！ ### 提交步骤 1. Fork 本仓库 2. 在 `public/stickers/` 文件夹内添加你的 PNG 图片 3. 提交 PR ### 设计建议 推荐使用 **gemini-3-pro-preview** 生成 Sticker。以下是推荐的 Prompt： ```text 将角色变形并设计一张 LINE 贴纸。姿势和文字排版要富有创意，变化丰富，设计独特。 对话应为简体中文，参考 sticker 示例。 使用文本"[YOUR_TEXT]"，动作是[YOUR_ACTION]。 图片整体使用浅灰色 RGB(240, 240, 240) 背景，文字和角色周围有白色描边。 ``` **示例：** ```text 将角色变形并设计一张 LINE 贴纸。姿势和文字排版要富有创意，变化丰富，设计独特。 对话应为简体中文，参考 sticker 示例。 使用文本"干饭"，动作是开心地吃饭。 图片整体使用浅灰色 RGB(240, 240, 240) 背景，文字和角色周围有白色描边。 ``` ## 请求新 Sticker 如果你有想要的 Sticker 创意，欢迎提交 Issue！ ### Issue 格式 ```markdown **Sticker 名称：** [中文名称] **描述：** [简要描述这个 sticker 的内容、场景、表情等] **文本建议：** [希望在 sticker 上显示的文本] **参考：** [可选：参考其他 sticker 或参考图片] ``` **示例：** ```markdown **Sticker 名称：** 加班中 **描述：** Lynn 酱疲惫地工作，眼神无神，咖啡杯在旁边 **文本建议：** 又是加班的一天 **参考：** 参考 "在忙.png" 的风格 ``` ## Agent 接入 贴纸库同时提供三种 agent 接入方式，详见 [docs/sticker-agent-stack.md](docs/sticker-agent-stack.md)： - **Catalog API**：`packages/sticker-catalog/catalog.json`，覆盖 80 张静态贴纸和 181 张动态贴纸。 - **REST / MCP**：`npm run stickers:api` 启动本地 API（含 `/mcp`），`npm run stickers:mcp` 启动 MCP stdio 服务。 - **DeepSeek Harness 插件**：安装 `packages/dsh-sticker` 后，agent 可以在合适的时候调用 `send_sticker`，贴纸直接显示在对话里；匹配时优先选择动态贴纸。模型会根据提示词中的适用时机主动选择；任务相关的 `tools/post-execute` hook 会在修改类工具结束后提示模型自行决定是否发一张贴纸。 插件本身只有约 70 KB，不打包任何贴纸图片/WebM； 图片和动态图按需从 `https://sticker.stv.pm` 加载。贴纸媒体和完整 catalog 都不会进入模型上下文。 ```bash npm run stickers:build # 生成 catalog、public/catalog.json、MCP 静帧和插件元数据 npm run stickers:api # REST API + MCP HTTP，默认 127.0.0.1:4319 npm run stickers:mcp # MCP stdio npm run stickers:verify # 端到端校验 npm run stickers:pack # 打包 dsh-lynn-sticker 插件 ``` 插件安装：在 Plugin Manager 中添加本地 bundle 目录 `/absolute/path/to/packages/dsh-sticker`， 或发布后安装 npm 包。`sticker.stv.pm` 已提供 `/catalog.json`，插件会按 TTL（默认 5 分钟） 在后台刷新贴纸元数据；贴纸图片和 WebM 也直接按需从站点加载。MCP 客户端配置示例和上下文开销 说明见 [docs/sticker-agent-stack.md](docs/sticker-agent-stack.md)。 ## 协议 本项目中的所有 Sticker 作品采用 **CC BY 4.0** 协议。 - ✅ 可以自由使用、修改和分享 - ✅ 必须署名原作者 - ❌ **禁止商用** 详见 [CC BY 4.0 协议](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) ## 技术栈 - **框架：** Next.js 14 + React 18 - **样式：** Tailwind CSS - **动画：** Framer Motion - **图标：** Lucide React ## 本地开发 ```bash # 安装依赖 npm install # 启动开发服务器 npm run dev # 访问 http://localhost:3000 ``` ### 同步已发布的动态贴纸 资源及来源、顺序和 SHA-256 记录分别保存在 `public/stickers/animated/` 与 `src/data/animated-stickers.json`，运行网站无需 OpenSticker 项目。需要从发布工作目录重新同步时： ```bash node scripts/sync-animated-stickers.mjs ~/code/OpenSticker/.workspace/lynn-telegram ``` 脚本只导入 `pack-plan.json` 中已发布的条目，并核对 `published.json` 的数量和每个 WebM 的 SHA-256。 --- Made with ❤️ by [Steven Lynn](https://x.com/Stv_Lynn)

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-session-title-convention

按工作区约定自动整理 DeepSeek Harness 会话标题：

```
【<阶段><状态>】<工作区>｜<模块>｜<创建日期 MMDD>｜<问题简述>
```

插件本身不含任何具体项目信息；工作区名、模块词表、生效目录全部来自配置。未配置 `workspace` 时，工作区名取会话 `cwd` 的目录名。

> **English** — A DeepSeek Harness host plugin that rewrites automatically generated session titles into a configurable `【stage+status】workspace｜module｜MMDD｜brief` form. Human renames are never touched. The convention's stage vocabulary is Chinese; everything else (workspace label, module rules, scope, time zone) is configuration.

## 安装

```bash
# npm（推荐：市场里能一键安装、能检查更新）
install_bundle dsh-session-title-convention

# 或直接从 GitHub
install_bundle github:TangUsers/dsh-session-title-convention

# 或写进 profile 的 package.json
#   "dsh-session-title-convention": "^0.1.0"
```

装完需要重启宿主才生效：Desktop 退出重开，Web 重启服务（Host 插件不热加载）。

安装即生效，**默认作用于所有会话**——见下方「生效范围」。只想在特定仓库里用，先配 `roots`。

## 行为

- 监听 `session/title` 事件：来源为 `fallback` / `provider`（即模型自动生成的标题）且不符合约定时改写；来源为 `user`（人工改名）时永不改动。
- `fallback` 标题延迟 8 秒再处理，等 provider 生成更好的标题；`provider` 标题立即处理。
- 模块按 `moduleRules` 依次匹配当前标题；都不命中时用 `defaultModule`。
- 日期取会话 `header.createdAt` 的月日，四位数（如 `1103`），时区由 `timeZone` 决定，默认本机时区。
- 仅处理 `cwd` 位于 `roots` 之下、非 subagent、非 seeded 的会话；`roots` 为空表示所有工作区。
- `sweepOnStart` 打开时，启动 2 秒后把最近 `sweepMaxAgeMinutes` 分钟内仍是非合规自动标题的会话一并整理。默认关闭。
- 改写走 `sessionTitle.rename()`，结果被标记为 `user` 来源并固定，所以插件不会和人抢标题，也不会反复改写自己的输出。

### 生效范围

`roots` 默认为空，也就是**每个工作区的每个会话**都会被改写成上面的格式。安装前请确认这是你要的；否则先限定目录：

```yaml
- id: session-title-convention
  config:
    roots:
      - /path/to/repo
```

标题只会被改写一次（随后即固化为 `user` 来源），但一旦改写就在会话列表里长期可见。

## 工具

注册 `session_title` 工具，代理可显式调整阶段/状态，不必整名重写：

```json
{ "stage": "实现", "status": "🟢", "module": "会话治理", "brief": "xxx" }
```

只传需要改的字段，其余沿用当前标题。阶段词表固定为 `盘点 / 设计 / 实现 / 验证 / 收口 / 归档`，状态为 `🟢 🟡 🔴 ✅ 🧊`；约定允许阶段为空。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里按插件 id 覆盖配置（这是本机配置，不会随插件分发）：

```yaml
- id: session-title-convention
  config:
    workspace: 某个工作区名
    roots:
      - /path/to/repo
    defaultModule: 通用
    timeZone: Asia/Shanghai
    moduleRules:
      - ['权限|授权|菜单', 权限治理]
      - ['迁移|migration|V\\d+__', 数据库迁移]
```

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace` | `''` | 工作区名；空则取会话 cwd 目录名 |
| `roots` | `[]` | 生效目录；空 = 所有会话 |
| `defaultStage` | `''` | 默认阶段；约定允许省略 |
| `defaultStatus` | `🟢` | 默认状态 |
| `defaultModule` | `通用` | 未命中任何规则时的模块 |
| `maxBrief` | `40` | 简述最大长度 |
| `timeZone` | `''` | 日期时区；空 = 本机 |
| `fallbackDelayMs` | `8000` | fallback 标题的延迟 |
| `sweepOnStart` | `false` | 启动时整理存量会话 |
| `sweepMaxAgeMinutes` | `1440` | sweep 只处理该时限内的会话；0 = 不限 |
| `moduleRules` | `[]` | `[正则, 模块]` 或 `{pattern, module}` |

## 本地开发

```bash
# 用目录绝对路径安装；改完代码后要先卸载再装，才会加载新的模块代际
install_bundle /path/to/dsh-session-title-convention
```

直接改文件不会热更新。

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

It listens to session events and registers a rename tool with cleanup, but the manifest declares only Node and the README does not supply a versioned DSH compatibility contract. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

🇨🇳 中文 • 🇹🇼 繁體中文 • 🇯🇵 日本語 • 🇵🇹 Português • 🇧🇷 Português • 🇰🇷 한국어 • 🇪🇸 Español • 🇩🇪 Deutsch • 🇫🇷 Français • 🇮🇱 עברית • 🇸🇦 العربية • 🇷🇺 Русский • 🇵🇱 Polski • 🇨🇿 Čeština • 🇳🇱 Nederlands • 🇹🇷 Türkçe • 🇺🇦 Українська • 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt • 🇵🇭 Tagalog • 🇮🇩 Indonesia • 🇹🇭 ไทย • 🇮🇳 हिन्दी • 🇧🇩 বাংলা • 🇵🇰 اردو • 🇷🇴 Română • 🇸🇪 Svenska • 🇮🇹 Italiano • 🇬🇷 Ελληνικά • 🇭🇺 Magyar • 🇫🇮 Suomi • 🇩🇰 Dansk • 🇳🇴 Norsk

Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together.

Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents. Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code and Warp can search your memory, but their sessions aren't recorded.

--- ## Quick Start **Installing for someone as an AI agent?** Run `npx claude-mem install --runtime worker` on their computer in an interactive terminal (enable PTY in your shell tool). It first asks in the terminal which agents to set up and, for Claude Code, whether to disable native auto-memory (and whether to overwrite an existing install). Relay each question to the user and type their answer, or pass `--ide ` to skip the first one. Keep the installer running. When it prints **Continue setup in your browser**, open that URL in the user's browser if the installer hasn't already opened it. Let the user go through setup and make their own choices, including the usage-analytics question the installer may ask at the end. If you can't run an interactive terminal on their computer, give them the command to run locally. ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer finds the agents on your machine and asks which ones to set up. Then just start working: observations stream in from your first prompt, and your second session in a project opens with memory from the first. (Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code and Warp get memory search only, so their sessions don't add to it.) The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link, no card required to sign in). Choosing the **claude-mem observer** then starts its **30 Day Free Trial** on a checkout page that asks for a payment method; once it completes, the installer saves your memory key. With the observer, memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider: the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Your memory lives in `~/.claude-mem` on your machine. Cloud sync is opt-in. Anonymous usage analytics are on by default; `npx claude-mem telemetry disable` turns them off ([what's collected](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/telemetry)). Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### Other agents `npx claude-mem install` covers every supported agent. To set up one agent directly, pass `--ide`. **OpenCode** (1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2). Restart OpenCode after installing. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers). The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` **Antigravity CLI** ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` **OMP (Oh My Pi):** ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` **Pi and DeepSeek Harness** use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` **Grok Bot:** see [Grok Bot](#grok-bot) below. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` The full list of `--ide` values is in `npx claude-mem --help`. #### Grok Bot Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Opt-in awareness push:** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Enable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=true` and set `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_AGENT_IDS` to your agent UUIDs (empty by default). #### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. ## What You Get - 🧠 **The next session starts where the last one left off.** Each session opens with a compact index of past observations, layered so the agent opens full details only when it needs them, and the header can show what each layer costs in tokens. - 🔍 **Find anything you worked on.** The mem-search skill searches your project history in three steps (index, timeline, details), so the agent spends tokens only on what it opens. - 🖥️ **Watch it work, and keep track of yours.** My Work shows live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work). Memory, sessions and settings remain at `/viewer`. - 👥 **Share with your team, if you want.** TeamBrain is an optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. [Set up a team](https://cmem.ai/teambrain/start). - 💻 **Search from Claude Desktop.** Search your memory from Claude Desktop conversations. - 🔒 **Keep secrets out.** Wrap anything in `` tags and it never gets stored. - 🖼️ **Screenshots, kept by default.** Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under `~/.claude-mem/media-v1/` and show them in My Work, upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled. Turn it off with the "Keep images" switch in Settings ([details](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration#screenshots-and-images)). - ⚙️ **Choose what gets injected.** Fine-grained settings for what context a new session starts with. - 🤖 **Nothing to remember to do.** It runs on its own once installed. - 🔗 **Point back to past work.** Every observation has an ID you can cite through the worker API or open in the web viewer. --- ## Documentation 📚 **[View Full Documentation](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/)** - Browse on official website ### Getting Started - **[Installation Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation)** - Quick start & advanced installation - **[Usage Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/getting-started)** - How Claude-Mem works automatically - **[Search Tools](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools)** - Query your project history with natural language - **[Cloud Sync](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cloud-sync)** - Back up your memory to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write ### Best Practices - **[Context Engineering](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/context-engineering)** - AI agent context optimization principles - **[Progressive Disclosure](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/progressive-disclosure)** - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy ### Architecture - **[Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview)** - System components & data flow - **[Architecture Evolution](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture-evolution)** - The journey from v3 to v5 - **[Hooks Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/hooks-architecture)** - How Claude-Mem uses lifecycle hooks - **[Hooks Reference](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/hooks)** - Every hook entry explained - **[Worker Service](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/worker-service)** - HTTP API & Bun management - **[Database](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database)** - SQLite schema & FTS5 search - **[Search Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/search-architecture)** - Hybrid search with Chroma vector database ### Configuration & Development - **[Configuration](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** - Environment variables & settings - **[Development](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** - Building, testing, contributing - **[Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** - Common issues & solutions --- ## How It Works 1. **Your agent works.** Hooks in your agent hand each tool call (what it reads, edits and runs) to a small local worker. 2. **The observer takes notes.** A second agent turns that activity into short observations, and writes a summary when the session ends. 3. **The next session starts with them.** When a session starts, your agent gets a compact index of the observations that matter for this project, and fetches full details only when it needs them. Memory injection starts on your second session in a project. To front-load a whole repo instead, run `/learn-codebase` (~5 minutes on a typical repo, optional). See [Architecture Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview) for details. ### How it fits together For contributors, the main parts and where they live: - **The `claude-mem` command** (`src/npx-cli/index.ts`): install, repair, doctor, start, search and the rest. The installer puts a small launcher on PATH so hooks can run `claude-mem` directly. - **Hooks** (`src/cli/hook-command.ts`, one adapter per agent in `src/cli/adapters/`): each agent event runs one shell-free command, such as `claude-mem hook claude-code `. For Claude Code that's Setup (`claude --init` / `--maintenance`), SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SubagentStop and SessionEnd. - **The worker** (`src/services/worker-service.ts`, routes in `src/services/worker/http/routes/`): a local HTTP service managed by Bun. It takes tool activity from the hooks, runs the observer, and serves the viewer and search. - **The observer** (prompts in `src/sdk/`, one provider per model source in `src/services/worker/`, such as `ClaudeProvider.ts` and `OpenRouterProvider.ts`): turns tool activity into observations and summaries. - **Storage** (`src/services/sqlite/`): SQLite at `~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db` holds sessions, observations and summaries. Chroma adds semantic search on top of SQLite's keyword search (`src/services/worker/search/`). - **Context** (`src/services/context/`): builds the block a new session starts with. - **Search** (`src/servers/mcp-server.ts`, `plugin/skills/mem-search/`): the MCP tools and the mem-search skill that drives them. - **The viewer** (`src/ui/viewer/` at `/viewer`, `src/ui/my-work/` at `/`): memory, sessions and settings, plus My Work. - **The built plugin** (`plugin/`): written by `npm run build`; edit `src/`, not the generated scripts. The words we use for each of these, and the story they tell, are in [docs/story.md](docs/story.md). --- ## MCP Search Tools Search runs through three MCP tools in a token-efficient three-step workflow. The mem-search skill drives it for you: **The three steps:** 1. **`search`** - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result) 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around interesting results 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result) **Step by step:** - Your agent uses MCP tools to search your memory - Start with `search` to get an index of results - Use `timeline` to see what was happening around specific observations - Use `get_observations` to fetch full details for relevant IDs - **~10x token savings** by filtering before fetching details **Available MCP Tools:** 1. **`search`** - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs) **Example Usage:** ```typescript // Step 1: Search for index search(query="authentication bug", type="bugfix", limit=10) // Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456) // Step 3: Fetch full details get_observations(ids=[123, 456]) ``` The worker also offers tools for code navigation (`smart_search`, `smart_outline`, `smart_unfold`), saving a note on purpose (`save_memory`) and tracking work in progress. See [Search Tools Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools) for detailed examples. --- ## System Requirements - **Node.js**: 20.19 or later in the 20.x line, or 22.12 or later - **A supported agent**: Claude Code (latest, with plugin support) or any agent in [Other agents](#other-agents) - **Bun**: JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing) - **uv**: Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing) - **SQLite 3**: For persistent storage (bundled) --- ### Windows Setup Notes If you see an error like: ```powershell npm : The term 'npm' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet ``` Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation. Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs `claude-mem` directly, and `npx claude-mem install` places that launcher at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe` and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report `Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem"`, run `npx claude-mem doctor` and see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting#claude-mem-command-not-found-in-hooks). --- ## Configuration Settings are managed in `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings. To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set `"CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true"` in that file, or enable **Include all sources at session start** in the viewer settings. The default is `"false"`, which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources. See the **[Configuration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** for all available settings and examples. ### Mode & Language Configuration Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the `CLAUDE_MEM_MODE` setting. This option controls both: - The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation) - The language used in generated observations #### How to Configure Edit your settings file at `~/.claude-mem/settings.json`: ```json { "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE": "code--zh" } ``` Modes are defined in `plugin/modes/`. To see all available modes locally: ```bash ls ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack/plugin/modes/ ``` #### Available Modes | Mode | Description | |------------|-------------------------| | `code` | Default English mode | | `code--chill` | Records fewer observations, keeping only what would be painful to rediscover | | `code--[lang]` | Same as `code`, with observations and summaries written in another language | Built-in language codes: `ar`, `bn`, `cs`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `es`, `fi`, `fr`, `he`, `hi`, `hu`, `id`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `nl`, `no`, `pl`, `pt-br`, `ro`, `ru`, `sv`, `th`, `tr`, `uk`, `ur`, `vi`, `zh`. For example, `code--ko` writes observations and summaries in Korean. See [Modes](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/modes) for each language's name, the email investigation mode, and custom modes. > Note: All of these modes are built in. No additional installation or plugin update is required. #### After Changing Mode Restart Claude Code to apply the new mode configuration. --- ## Development See the **[Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** for build instructions, testing, and contribution workflow. --- ## Troubleshooting Start with `npx claude-mem doctor`. It checks Bun, uv, the hook launcher and the worker, and tells you what to fix. See the **[Troubleshooting Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** for common issues and solutions. --- ## Bug Reports Create comprehensive bug reports with the automated generator: ```bash cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack npm run bug-report ``` ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please: 1. Fork the repository 2. Create a feature branch 3. Make your changes with tests 4. Update documentation (user-facing words follow [docs/story.md](docs/story.md)) 5. Submit a Pull Request against `main` Releases ship from `main` and are published to npm. See [Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development) for contribution workflow. --- ## License Claude-Mem is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. We chose Apache-2.0 because durable agentic memory should be easy to embed in developer tools, local agents, MCP servers, enterprise systems, robotics stacks, and production agent harnesses. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for full details. See [docs/license.md](docs/license.md) and [docs/ip-boundary.md](docs/ip-boundary.md) for licensing scope and the open/commercial boundary. --- ## Support - **Documentation**: [docs/](docs/) - **Issues**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues) - **Repository**: [github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) - **Official X Account**: [@Claude_Memory](https://x.com/Claude_Memory) - **Official Discord**: [Join Discord](https://discord.com/invite/J4wttp9vDu) - **Author**: Alex Newman ([@thedotmack](https://github.com/thedotmack)) --- **Built with Claude Agent SDK** | **Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and more** | **Made with TypeScript** --- ### What About CMEM? CMEM is a token created by a 3rd party but officially embraced by the creator of Claude-Mem (Alex Newman, @thedotmack). The token acts as a community catalyst for growth and a vehicle for bringing CMEM to the developers and knowledge workers that need it most. Official BASE CA: 0x76b1967eec0ccaeb001bbbb2b40dc4badba31ba3

# dsh-theme-blue

This release targets DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 source Web with the public settings icon slot. See [environment details](docs/dsh-0.2-compatibility.md).

蓝色浅色与深色配色、设置导航图标和可撤销的界面样式。

Blue light and dark palettes, settings glyphs and reversible interface styles.

通过皮肤商店启用或停用本主题时，配色覆盖、样式和设置图标随插件生命周期一起生效或清理；停用后恢复底层主题及官方图标。浅色、深色和跟随系统仍由 DSH 的外观设置管理。商店收录方式见[皮肤市场](docs/marketplace.md)。

Marketplace enable/disable controls this plugin's token layer, stylesheet and settings glyphs together. Disabling restores the underlying theme and original icons. DSH Appearance settings continue to control light, dark and system modes. See [marketplace integration](docs/marketplace.md).

“新会话”按钮使用蓝色主题的浅色和深色底色。

网页桌宠的气泡、对话输入框和积分卡片使用 DSH 默认字体。气泡使用深色文字和 98% 不透明白底。碎碎念文字最小 12px，行距为字号的 1.6 倍；关闭蓝色主题后恢复桌宠原有样式。

Web pet bubbles, chat input and score cards use the DSH default font. Bubbles use dark text on a 98% opaque white background. Whisper text stays at least 12px with a 1.6 line height; disabling the blue theme restores the pet styles.

与 `dafy-whale-theme` 同时启用时，左上角只显示一组大肥鱼图标和标题，避免上游品牌样式在新版 DSH 的嵌套元素中重复显示。关闭大肥鱼主题后恢复原有品牌区域。

When enabled alongside `dafy-whale-theme`, the sidebar shows one whale mark and title. The original identity returns when the whale theme is disabled.

桌面视口宽于 1280px 时，设置窗口宽 1120px、高度最多 900px，保留官方窗口留边以及导航和内容的独立滚动。较窄视口沿用原有布局；卸载主题后恢复官方尺寸。

设置导航为 16 个设置项提供功能图标。图标通过公开的 `settings.section.icon` 插槽按设置项 ID 注册，每项只显示一个图标，菜单重排或语言变化时保持对应；未收录项沿用官方图标，卸载主题后恢复原样。Lucide 图标在构建时嵌入，无额外网络请求，许可见 [第三方声明](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

Settings navigation registers 16 semantic glyphs through the public `settings.section.icon` slot. Each section id selects one glyph, independently of order and locale. Unknown sections keep the official icon; unloading restores the originals. SVGs are bundled without extra network requests.

设置弹窗中的复选框和现有滑动开关使用同一组主题滑条，保留标签点击、键盘、禁用状态和保存事件。尺寸与颜色由 `themes/blue/style.css` 中的 `--dsh-switch-*` 变量控制；继承的颜色变量无法解析时在控件处回退到 DSH 主题令牌，支持通过 portal 挂载的弹窗，关闭状态的圆点沿用官方颜色。聊天任务列表保持原样，卸载主题后恢复原始样式。

Settings checkboxes and existing switches share themed tracks while retaining labels, keyboard input, disabled states and save events. The `--dsh-switch-*` variables in `themes/blue/style.css` control dimensions and colors; unresolved inherited colors fall back to DSH tokens at each control, including dialogs mounted through portals. Off-state thumbs retain the official color. Chat task lists remain unchanged; unloading restores the original styles.

## 安装

锁定公开仓库的提交后，通过 DSH 官方入口安装：

```powershell
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add github:vb2250158/dsh-theme-blue#<commit>
```

插件包声明 `dsh.bundle`，安装后会把自己的配置层加入 profile。

## 配置

插件配置保存在 DSH profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`。多电脑同步仓库只保存仓库地址、固定提交、启停状态和配置，不保存本仓库源码。

## 验证

```powershell
npm test
npm run build
npm pack --dry-run
```

维护环境的生命周期集成测试使用当前 DSH 源码构建，不读取运行中的 profile：

```powershell
$env:DSH_SOURCE_ROOT = '<current-dsh-source-checkout>'
npm run test:lifecycle
```

## 许可证

MIT

## Plugin display metadata

The plugin list shows **Blue theme** in English and **蓝色主题** in Chinese, following the DSH interface language. `locale/en.json` and `locale/zh.json` provide the title and description; `icon.svg` supplies self-contained artwork. The package exports and publishes these resources. The icon is adapted from Lucide; see [ICON_LICENSE.txt](ICON_LICENSE.txt).

The icon uses a centered 36 × 36 viewBox to leave more space around the artwork inside the plugin icon frame.

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT repository/package; explicit pinned Git-source install; engines.dsh 0.2.2-rc.1 and versioned client peers. Committed host/client entries use theme token overrides and public settings icon slots with lifecycle cleanup. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES preserves Lucide ISC and inherited Feather MIT notices; the client embeds static glyphs and CSS rather than downloading them. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# OpenViking Memory for DeepSeek Harness

An installable DeepSeek Harness bundle that adds OpenViking auto-recall, session capture, `viking://` URI protection, and the OpenViking MCP tool surface.

> **Requires an OpenViking server with `viking://~` home-alias support.** Recall targets the
> caller's own context space through `viking://~/memories` and `viking://~/skills`; the uid-less
> `viking://user/memories` shorthand is rejected by newer servers.

Published as [`@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin).

## Install

DSH is covered by the unified memory-plugin installer:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://openviking.ai/install | bash
# AI agents: not sure about running this? The script's header says what it does and how to verify it.
```

It installs into the npm `dsh`'s `web` profile; pass `--dsh-profile <name>`
for another one. On macOS it also offers DeepSeek Harness Desktop as a separate
harness, `dsh-desktop` (see [DeepSeek Harness Desktop](#deepseek-harness-desktop)).

Or add the package to a profile directly:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin
dsh --profile web --dump-config    # should list openviking-memory-runtime
```

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory, so the bundle has to
be a real package. Linking a source checkout (`dsh plugin --profile web add
./examples/dsh-memory-plugin`) only works when that checkout has its own
`node_modules`, because Node resolves the bundle's dsh peers from the source
tree's realpath rather than from the profile.
It also needs `node examples/memory-plugin-shared/sync.mjs` run first: the
`shared/` modules the bundle imports are generated, not committed.

### DeepSeek Harness Desktop

Desktop keeps its plugins in a reserved `desktop` profile under
`${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/desktop`, separate from the CLI's profiles.
The bundle runs there unchanged; only the way it gets installed differs.

- **Plugins page** (macOS and Windows, manual): Plugins → Add plugin → enter
  `@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin` → Install, then turn it on if its switch is
  off. The page does not ask for OpenViking credentials, so write
  `~/.openviking/ovcli.conf` yourself first. Uninstall from the same page. The page shows [`docs/DETAIL.md`](docs/DETAIL.md)
  ([`DETAIL.zh.md`](docs/DETAIL.zh.md) in Chinese) as the plugin's detail
  document, through `meta.detail` in `locale/*.json`.
- **Installer** (macOS, needs Node.js): with Desktop present the installer
  selects the `dsh-desktop` harness, and `--dsh-profile desktop` routes there
  too. It uses Desktop's own launcher at `OPENVIKING_DSH_DESKTOP_CLI` when set,
  otherwise the one in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`, otherwise a `dsh`
  on `PATH` that resolves into the app.
- **Desktop's launcher** (macOS). Open Desktop once so the profile exists, quit
  it with ⌘Q (closing the window only hides it), run the command, then reopen
  Desktop:

  ```bash
  DSH_DESKTOP="/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh"
  "$DSH_DESKTOP" plugin --profile desktop add @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin
  "$DSH_DESKTOP" plugin --profile desktop ls    # should list the package
  "$DSH_DESKTOP" plugin --profile desktop rm @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin
  ```

An npm-installed `dsh` refuses `--profile desktop`, and no `dsh` boots that
profile or runs `--dump-config` on it, Desktop's own launcher included. To
confirm an install, use `plugin --profile desktop ls` or check that
`profiles/desktop/package.json` lists the package under `dsh.profile.bundles`.
On Windows, install from the Plugins page and configure the connection in
`~/.openviking/ovcli.conf`; the installer does not cover Windows. Desktop has
no Linux release.

## Requirements

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.1.0-rc.6` or later, below `1.0.0` (see [DSH version compatibility](#dsh-version-compatibility))
- Node.js `^22.19.0` or `>=24` for the bundle itself. The host decides in
  practice: DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` and later need Node.js `>=24.9`, and Desktop ships
  its own runtime, so it needs no system Node.js.
- A reachable OpenViking server

The bundle has no runtime npm dependencies. Its message structures come from
`createUserMessage` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`), its tool surface from
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, and its skill provider from
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` — peerDependencies that DSH itself already
installs. Keep those packages in the host installation rather than adding
individual DSH core packages to the profile. DSH initializes profiles with
`nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, then makes the host packages
available through its module fallback at boot. A missing-peer warning during
`dsh plugin add` alone does not prove startup is broken.

Everything under `shared/` and `skills/` is generated by
`node examples/memory-plugin-shared/sync.mjs` — edit
`examples/memory-plugin-shared/lib/` and `examples/skills/`, never the vendored
copies.

Rule search uses a server build advertising `rule_search` on `/mcp`. The bundled
`openviking-rule-search` skill requires plugin `0.5.33` or later. Upgrade both
and reconnect DSH; the tool is an on-demand constraint check.

### DSH version compatibility

The peer range is `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <1.0.0-0`. DSH checks each `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`
peer when it loads a plugin, with pre-releases included in the range, so this
admits every 0.x release and pre-release from `0.1.0-rc.6` on, including ones
published after this bundle. The bundle touches a small DSH surface —
`createUserMessage` and `boundContextSummary` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` and
the plugin entry points of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` — so the range is not narrowed to the
releases tested so far.

Verified releases: `0.1.0-rc.6`, `0.1.5-rc.1`, `0.1.5-rc.2`, `0.1.7-rc.2`,
`0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`, `0.2.1-rc.2`, and `0.2.1-rc.3` (built from the
same source tag as Desktop `0.2.1-rc.3`). A daily job
(`.github/workflows/host-compat.yml`) runs the bundle's tests against the
releases DSH's `latest`, `next`, and `alpha` dist-tags point at, installs each
of those releases from npm, adds the packed bundle to a `web` profile and checks
`--dump-config` lists it, and opens an issue when any of that fails, so a breaking release is usually caught before users
reach it; if the bundle still fails to start on a new release, pin DSH to a
verified one and open an issue. Every one of those checks uses npm `dsh` on
Linux, because Desktop is not on npm and has no Linux build. A further smoke step
emulates Desktop's launcher with the same release: it initializes a `desktop`
profile the way Desktop's first launch does, adds the bundle through
`runCli({ manageDesktopProfile: true })`, and checks that the profile lists it,
that npm `dsh` still refuses that profile, and that no `dsh` dumps its config. Real Desktop builds are checked by
hand. DSH 1.0 and later, pre-releases included, fall outside the
range and DSH refuses to load the bundle; `dsh plugin allow-version` grants an exact-version
exemption if you accept the risk. Local devDependencies and `overrides` stay
pinned to rc.6 to exercise the minimum supported contract.

## Troubleshooting startup

If startup reports that `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` does not export `assertNever`,
inspect the affected profile before changing dependencies:

```bash
dsh --version
dsh plugin --profile web why @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill
dsh plugin --profile web why @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem
dsh plugin --profile web why @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm
```

Replace `web` with the affected profile name. Check its `package.json`,
`pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` under
`${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/<profile>/`, including dependency overrides.
`dsh-skill@0.0.1-rc.1` imports `assertNever` from the old location. A profile-local
copy can shadow the newer host package and break both DSH's own skill loader
and this plugin. As of 2026-09-14, the skill and skill-filesystem npm `latest`
tags still point to `0.0.1` release candidates; installing either without a
version is not an upgrade strategy.

If these old packages are direct profile dependencies added only to satisfy
this plugin, remove those constraints and let DSH supply its matching packages:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill @deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem
dsh plugin --profile web add @openviking/dsh-memory-plugin@latest
dsh --profile web
```

If another plugin requires them, update that plugin's constraints instead of
removing them blindly. Keep `autoInstallPeers: false` and `nodeLinker: hoisted`
in the profile's pnpm settings. Do not patch the import in `node_modules`: a
mixed DSH package family can have other incompatible interfaces. Updating this
memory plugin alone does not remove conflicting profile-local packages.

Use `dsh --profile <profile>` to start a named profile. `dsh web` is an alias for
the stock `web` profile, not a subcommand to append after `--profile`.

## Design notes

### Why injection uses pre-step user messages, not the system prompt

Recall and profile context enter through the `agent/pre-step` waterfall as
durable, source-attributed user messages
(`source: { kind: 'plugin:openviking-memory', … }`). The producer-owned kind is
required by DSH session format v4; the plugin still recognizes legacy
`kind: 'plugin'` messages while older sessions are replayed.
They are deliberately **not** added to the system prompt: a DSH preset whose
persona declares `complete: true` (the stock `minimal` preset does) restores
that persona as the sole prompt section after assembly, silently discarding
every other contribution — a system-prompt-based memory plugin loses its
context under such presets with no error. Pre-step injection also makes each
injection a session event that replays, is visible to compaction, and never
reaches `request/header`.

### What triggers recall

Recall runs on a pre-step whose entering batch contains user-authored input.
The query is built only from those messages: user-role messages with
`source.kind` absent or `user`. Messages that DSH or other plugins inject
(`time-context`, `plugin:*` notices, this plugin's own blocks) and tool results
are excluded, using the same rule capture uses. A batch made only of injected
context sends no search request.

### How the tool surface is mounted

`mcp.mjs` mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` on `servers/mcp-proxy.mjs`, the
same stdio proxy every other OpenViking memory integration starts, so the model
gets the server's full tool set instead of a hand-maintained subset and the
transport behaves identically across harnesses. Pointing the bridge straight at
the server's `/mcp` endpoint does not work: with `stateless_http=True` the
server still answers `GET /mcp` with an idle 200 SSE stream, and once the MCP
SDK client opens that standalone stream it stops resolving POST responses, so
`tools/list` never returns. The proxy owns the transport itself and is
unaffected.

The bundle's resolved connection — url, MCP url, key, account, user and auth
mode — travels to the proxy through the child environment, because DSH scrubs
credential-shaped names out of the inherited env and a subprocess cannot see the
Cordis patch. It goes with `OPENVIKING_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=env`, so the proxy reads
no config file and reaches the server exactly as the runtime does, including
with no key when the runtime has none. A changed `ovcli.conf` therefore takes
effect for the tools when DSH restarts the bundle, as it does for the runtime.

Two consequences follow from the proxy being one process per profile:

- **MCP actor scope is process-level.** With the default `recallPeerScope: all`, MCP tool calls omit the actor peer header. With `actor`, they use the peer resolved at boot. Automatic recall, capture, and commit resolve their peer from each session's workspace.
  Desktop boots the bundle in its profile directory, which is no repository, so
  there the boot peer is empty and `actor`-scoped tool calls fall back to broad
  recall. Set `actor_peer_id` in `ovcli.conf` or `OPENVIKING_PEER_ID` to give
  them a peer; either one also overrides the workspace peer of every session.
- **`remember` is not session-scoped.** The server's MCP `remember` stores into
  its own short-lived session rather than the live `dsh-<session-id>` stream —
  the same behavior the Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor integrations have.
  Automatic capture still records the conversation itself.

The bridge and the skill provider are mounted last in `apply()`, after every
lifecycle registration, so a proxy that cannot start holds up nothing above it.

### Why the skill gets its own provider

`skills.mjs` registers a second `ctx.skills` provider with
`includeDefaultRoots: false` and `bundledSkillDir` pointing at `skills/`. DSH
reads this host-owned bundle directly rather than asking a workspace filesystem
to resolve a path outside its root. The provider discovers no project or user
roots, so the bundle does not duplicate that catalog or override
higher-priority project skills. Those roots belong to DSH's own
`skill-filesystem`: `dsh-base`'s host-level row in `headless`, `acp`, and
`sdk`, whose app bundles keep it, and per-preset rows in `web` and `desktop`,
where `dsh-web-app` disables the host row and the `standard`, `ptc`, and
`cordis` agent presets each mount their own `skill-filesystem` and
`tool-skill`. The bundle's provider registers at host level, which every
preset reads, so those agents see the bundled skills. The `minimal` preset mounts no `tool-skill`, so its agents
see no skills, these included, and `sdk-minimal` has no `skills` service, so the
provider never starts there.

## Configuration

OpenViking credentials use the same resolution order as the other memory plugins:

1. `OPENVIKING_*` environment variables
2. `~/.openviking/ovcli.conf`
3. `~/.openviking/ov.conf`

Common environment variables:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `OPENVIKING_URL` / `OPENVIKING_BASE_URL` | OpenViking server endpoint |
| `OPENVIKING_API_KEY` / `OPENVIKING_BEARER_TOKEN` | Bearer credential |
| `OPENVIKING_ACCOUNT` | Trusted-mode account |
| `OPENVIKING_USER` | Trusted-mode user |
| `OPENVIKING_PEER_ID` | Explicit actor peer |
| `OPENVIKING_WORKSPACE_PEER` | Derive a peer from each DSH session workspace's git identity by default; `0` sends no peer |
| `OPENVIKING_RECALL_PEER_SCOPE` | `all` for cross-workspace recall or `actor` for isolation |

The profile's `cordis.patch.yml` can also carry plugin config:

```yaml
- id: openviking-memory-runtime
  config:
    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:1933
    recallMaxTokens: 2000
    scoreThreshold: 0.35
    captureToolResults: true
    skipSubagentSessions: true
    commitTokenThreshold: 20000
    mcpToolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
```

Recall normally uses `POST /api/v1/search/search` with `mode: "context"`.
`recallMaxTokens` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_MAX_TOKENS`) sets this request's
`max_tokens` budget for server-assembled context. When it is unset, the plugin
omits `max_tokens` and uses the server's default budget.

`recallLimit` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_LIMIT`) scales the category quotas for context
recall; it is not a strict cap on the final number of entries. When explicitly
set, it allocates at least one slot to each of the six categories: events,
entities, preferences, experiences, resources, and skills. For example,
`recallLimit: 4` sends six one-slot quotas, so the result can contain more than
four entries. Lowering it does not expand the set of categories searched.
Actual results still depend on matching content, score filtering, deduplication,
and the token budget. When unset, the server's coding preset supplies the quotas.

The older size settings apply to fallback recall, not the primary context request:

- `recallTokenBudget` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_TOKEN_BUDGET`) controls the estimated
  token budget of the locally rendered block when both server-side context and
  the legacy `/api/v1/search/recall` endpoint are unavailable and recall falls
  back to raw search results.
- `recallMaxContentChars` (`OPENVIKING_RECALL_MAX_CONTENT_CHARS`) limits each
  item's content in that local fallback. It also sets the legacy `/recall`
  request's `max_chars` to `max(1000, recallMaxContentChars * recallLimit)`.

## Behavior

- Agent startup injects the OpenViking profile, the available-memory index, and the `<available-skills>` catalog through `agent.inject()`, and registers the per-session disposal commit. On DSH `0.1.7` and later this runs from the serial `agent/created` event (`{ agent, source, signal? }`), which holds queued input until it settles; DSH `0.1.0-rc.6` and `0.1.5` emit `agent/created` without `source` and start the session through `agent/session-start` instead. Startup runs once per agent, and `agent/pre-step` delivers the profile only if startup did not.
- `agent/pre-step` retrieves with the current step input and appends a durable plugin message to that same step.
- `session/event` captures user, assistant, and optionally tool-result messages without scraping a transcript.
- `turn/end` checks the OpenViking pending-token threshold and commits when required.
- `skipSubagentSessions: true` excludes sessions marked with `header.origin: subagent` from automatic profile, recall, capture, and commit; it defaults to `false`.
- `syncTurns: false` stops every new write: no captured messages, no threshold or shutdown commit. Writes queued while the toggle was on are still replayed by the background drainer once the server recovers — they were captured with the toggle on. Profile injection and recall are unaffected; it defaults to `true`.
- `skillCatalog` (default `true`) and `skillCatalogTokenBudget` (default `1200`; `0` also turns the catalog off) govern `<available-skills>`. The catalog comes from one `GET /api/v1/skills?node_limit=200` call: the user's own skills first, then those shared under `viking://agent/skills` minus any whose name the user also owns, each description cut to about 40 tokens. Its budget is separate from `profileTokenBudget`. When the descriptions do not fit, the catalog lists names only (with a `... +N more` tail if even the names do not all fit); when not even one name fits, it shrinks to a one-line count; with no skills, or a server without the endpoint, it is omitted.
- Failed writes enter the shared OpenViking pending queue. A background drainer (default every 60s, `OPENVIKING_PENDING_DRAIN_INTERVAL_MS`) probes the server health and replays the queue in-process, so a transient write failure recovers without restarting dsh; it does not consume the session-start retry budget. Session-start replays keep consuming retries as before.
- `tools/pre-execute` denies a DSH filesystem tool (`read`, `glob`, `grep`, `edit`, `write`, `str_replace_editor`) whose path argument is a `viking://` URI, pointing the model at the bridged `mcp__openviking__*` tools instead. A `write` or `edit` under a skill directory (`viking://~/skills/...`, `viking://user/<id>/skills/...`, `viking://agent/skills/...`) points at `mcp__openviking__add_skill` instead, which creates or replaces a whole skill from its `SKILL.md` text. A `grep` whose pattern is `viking://` text still runs.
- `tools/post-execute` lets a `bash` command (`pwsh` on Windows, where DSH mounts it in place of `bash`) that carries a `viking://` URI run unchanged and attaches a notice for the model: use the bridged tools if it meant OpenViking content, or ignore the notice when the URI is intentional data such as an `ov` argument or an HTTP payload.

Each DSH session maps to `dsh-<session-id>` in OpenViking. IDs that contain Windows-invalid path characters are normalized to a readable underscore form plus a stable hash, so two native IDs cannot collapse onto the same OpenViking session; already-portable IDs keep their existing mapping. Existing sessions whose native IDs require normalization start a new OpenViking session after this upgrade. Workspace-derived actor peers are resolved per session and sent on every session-specific request: the peer is the git identity of the session's workspace — the normalized `origin` URL (`git@github.com:volcengine/OpenViking.git` becomes `github.com-volcengine-openviking`), else the repository root path, that fallback keeping the older rule where every non-letter-or-digit character becomes `-`. With the default peer settings, no peer is sent outside a git repository, and what is remembered there goes to the user-level space `viking://user/<you>/memories`. One repository therefore keeps one peer across subdirectories, worktrees, clones and machines, while a fork's different origin keeps it separate. Memories written under the older path-derived peer stay reachable: the default `recallPeerScope: all` sweeps every peer under the user.

Workspace peer settings are loaded from `session.header.cwd` when the session first uses memory. A workspace can set `peer.id` to name its project explicitly, or `peer.source` to choose a preset or template chain. For example, `<root>/.openviking/config.json` can contain:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "peer": { "id": "my-project" }
}
```

The shared loader also applies `config.local.json` and machine registry overrides. Explicit host `peerId`, environment overrides and pinned `ovcli.conf` credentials retain their existing precedence. The resolved peer stays fixed for the session's runtime state; new sessions load the current workspace settings. A session without a cwd falls back to the process's working directory.

## Tools

The model sees the OpenViking MCP tools under the bridge's server-qualified
names — `mcp__openviking__search`, `mcp__openviking__read`,
`mcp__openviking__list`, `mcp__openviking__tree`, `mcp__openviking__grep`,
`mcp__openviking__glob`, `mcp__openviking__remember`,
`mcp__openviking__write`, `mcp__openviking__edit`,
`mcp__openviking__forget`, `mcp__openviking__add_resource`,
`mcp__openviking__add_skill`, `mcp__openviking__rule_search`, and the rest of
whatever the connected server
advertises. The list re-syncs when the server announces a change, so a server
upgrade adds tools without a bundle release.

`mcp__openviking__forget` performs permanent deletion. The calling model should
use it only when the user explicitly requests deletion.

The bundle also serves the shared `openviking-memory`, `openviking-skills`,
`ov-experience-memory`, and `openviking-rule-search` skills from `skills/`
through its own isolated `ctx.skills` provider, so the
model gets the same guidance the other integrations ship: when to search, read,
and write, and how to find, use, create, share, and migrate OpenViking skills.

## Testing

```bash
npm ci          # installs the exact-pinned dsh devDependencies the tests exercise
npm run check   # syntax check every shipped module + package/PLUGIN_VERSION agreement
npm test        # node --test *.test.mjs — runs in the repo's PR workflow
```

The `0.3.2` compatibility check installed the packed bundle through
`dsh plugin add` in isolated profiles and exercised DSH `0.1.0-rc.6`,
`0.1.5-rc.1`, and `0.1.5-rc.2` with matching core packages. It covered Web startup
and browser loading, skill discovery/read, MCP tool calls, profile/recall
injection, user/assistant capture, resume deduplication, threshold commits, and
disposal commits. The check used a local HTTP/MCP fixture and a deterministic
model adapter on macOS with Node.js 26.5.0; it verifies harness integration, not
real-server memory extraction. The rc.2 CLI also exited cleanly on SIGTERM.

The startup failure from issue #4944 was reproduced by adding the reported
old skill packages to an rc.2 profile; removing those direct dependencies and
reinstalling the bundle restored the same integration checks. A clean rc.2
profile with the published `0.3.0` bundle did not reproduce that import error.

`live-recall.test.mjs` is an opt-in end-to-end gate against a real OpenViking
server: it stores a sentinel memory through a session commit, waits for
extraction, and asserts recall returns that sentinel — the property no stub
can certify. Enable it with `OPENVIKING_E2E=1` plus the normal credential
chain; it skips otherwise (including in CI until a server secret exists).

### Client-side recall compression

Compression stays off by default. To use DSH's configured model instead of the
server query planner, merge this into `~/.openviking/ovcli.conf` and restart DSH:

```json
{"plugin":{"dsh":{"recallCompress":"client","recallCompressTimeoutMs":10000}}}
```

The plugin makes one tool-free `ctx.llm.stream()` call using the agent's
`options.provider` and `options.model`. `recallCompressModel` optionally selects
another model on that same provider; `recallCompressThinking` supplies a
provider-supported reasoning effort. Credentials and endpoints belong to DSH's
provider configuration, not OpenViking's server credentials. DSH does not use
`recallCompressBaseUrl` or the CLI compressor detection settings. “Client-side”
means the call runs through DSH; inference is on-device only if that DSH provider
points to a local model service. Model switches implemented solely by host request
middleware are not inferred from `agent.options`; configure the compressor model
explicitly or restart with the intended model.

`client` never requests server rewrite. `auto` prefers the host compressor when
its model/service are available, otherwise retains server `rewrite: "auto"`.
`server` and `off` keep their existing behavior. An unavailable host compressor in
`client` mode leaves the retrieved context uncompressed. Short input skips the
model call; the shared input limit, cited-digest handling and fallback still apply.
Timeouts, unsuccessful streams and invalid digests fall back to budgeted original
fragments; an explicitly irrelevant result injects nothing. Cancellation stops
waiting and signals the adapter. An adapter that ignores abort may continue its
request, but cannot inject its late result. Auxiliary messages are not appended
to the session or captured as memories. Digest caches are separated by connection,
identity, session and model. Shared compression status is logged through DSH.

The compressor contract is checked against the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`
`0.1.0-rc.6` service/types: `LlmRuntime.stream`, `BlockAssembler`, successful
`finish.reason.kind === "stop"`, and `GenerateOptions.signal`. The adapter uses no
agent creation, prompt assembly, tools, or session append API. Unit and packaged
service smoke tests cover Linux; real-model quality/latency and Desktop behavior
still require deployment validation.

Shared local memory, cross-agent handoff, and code recovery across 43 coding agents.
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Hermes and 36 more agents already save every session to disk.
deja indexes all of it locally in one Go binary — zero LLM calls, 0.7 ms in-process lookup, ~4% index footprint.

Every driver, corpus and scoring rule is in this repository: head-to-head · all benchmark runs

## Search it yourself `deja` with no arguments opens a terminal search across every agent's history — starting with the sessions behind your uncommitted changes, then recent work in the current project.

- **Navigate:** `↑↓` picks a session, `↵` opens at the match, `/` searches inside a session, `]` `[` jump between turns, `^s` toggles date/relevance sort (`deja search --sort date`). - **Filter:** by agent (`codex:`), time (`today`, `yesterday`, `week`, `month`), or project (`in:`). - **Resume or hand off:** `r` reopens the session in its native agent; `o` continues it in another agent with its goal, decisions and open work. - **Recover deleted chats:** `tab` switches between this project, all projects, and **Deleted** (sessions an agent purged that deja still holds); `R` restores one, `D` deletes (`deja delete `), `?` lists all keys. Prefer a browser? `deja view` exports the store — sessions, the recall audit trail, and promoted notes — into one local HTML file ([try the live demo](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/view/)). With `DEJA_TUI=0` (or `deja brief`), `deja` prints a plain-text summary. ## Highlights - **Starts full on day one.** Months of existing transcripts across all [forty-three agents](#supported-harnesses) are searchable immediately — fix a bug in Codex and Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode recalls it. - **Survives `/compact` and context resets.** Over 43 measured compactions, summaries kept 77% of decisions and 0.2% of commands; deja hands back the exact commands, errors, and decisions ([how](docs/compaction.md)). - **Cross-agent handoff (`deja handoff`).** Hit a rate limit or get stuck in Claude Code? Hand the active session's goal, decisions, touched files, and open work straight into Codex, Cursor, or OpenCode. - **Undo overwritten code (`deja restore` & `deja blame`).** Indexes opened files, commands with exit codes, and exact `Edit` spans so `deja restore ` recovers code an agent clobbered even before `git commit` (`deja blame :`). - **Automatic recall via hooks & MCP.** Surfaces prior sessions at session start, before a file edit or command runs, and when a command fails. - **Tracks decision lifecycle & staleness.** `deja promote --state rejected` marks a reverted approach so later hits warn why it was dropped (`--state accepted` takes the mark back), and hits report when files touched by a session have changed since. - **Travels with the repository.** `deja repo add` commits the decisions and dead ends you pick into `.deja/memory.jsonl`; a teammate's agent recalls them after a clone ([repo memory](#memory-in-the-repository)). - **Incremental local index.** Append-only `records.bin` plus token buckets in `~/.cache/deja`, with per-file watermarks in `manifest.gob` so repeat passes only read changed files (~50 ms freshness check; 4% index footprint on a 5.7 GB / 358k-message corpus). Zero LLM calls, no cloud account, and automatic credential redaction at index time ([architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [privacy](#privacy)). ### Your own work, wrapped `deja stats --card` draws your yearly agent activity in the terminal or writes an SVG for your GitHub profile ([convert to PNG in browser](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/card/)).

## Install `install.sh` places the `deja` binary in `~/.local/bin`, and `deja install --auto` wires MCP recall and hooks into every detected agent and builds the initial index (~10s).

Open a new session in any wired agent and it already knows what you solved in that repository — or ask it directly (`have we dealt with jwt refresh rotation before?`).
Homebrew, Windows (Scoop / winget), npm, plugin marketplaces, and binary-only setup `brew install deja-vu`, `nix run github:numtide/llm-agents.nix#deja-vu`, `go install github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/cmd/deja@latest`, or `npx @vshulcz/deja-vu "query"` to try it without installing anything. Desktop apps that take MCP servers as bundles can open the `.mcpb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/releases/latest); it carries the binary. Codex CLI, opencode, Claude Code, Qwen and OpenClaw can also install the plugin bundle directly from their own marketplaces or registries (see [Harnesses with a package of their own](#harnesses-with-a-package-of-their-own), plus [`cursor-plugin/`](cursor-plugin/) for Cursor and [`antigravity-plugin/`](antigravity-plugin/) for Antigravity). Copilot CLI installs the marketplace bundle too, though it takes only the skill there — use `deja install copilot-auto` for hooks and MCP: ```sh codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu && codex plugin add deja-vu@deja-vu opencode plugin add opencode-deja claude plugin marketplace add vshulcz/deja-vu && claude plugin install deja-vu@deja-vu ``` On Windows the install script exits with `unsupported OS` — it is a shell script. Use Scoop, from the main bucket every Scoop install already has, or winget, which ships with Windows: ```powershell scoop install deja-vu winget install vshulcz.deja-vu ``` Or take `deja-vu__windows_amd64.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/vshulcz/deja-vu/releases/latest) and put `deja.exe` on your `PATH`, e.g. in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`. The binary alone is a complete install for searching: index, search, `show`, `ctx`, `blame`, `--json` and redaction need nothing else. `deja install` is what wires MCP into your agents and turns on session-start recall — worth having, and optional. On a binary-only setup `deja doctor` reports every MCP target as `config missing`, or `not-wired` where the agent is installed, which is that setup working as intended. `deja warmup` also leaves a skill at `~/.agents/skills/deja-search/SKILL.md` that teaches an agent the CLI contract — `deja recall`, `ctx`, `blame`, how to read the recall page and ask for the next one — so it knows history is searchable without MCP. The copy in the repo is [`skills/deja-search/SKILL.md`](skills/deja-search/SKILL.md). `deja install --all` is `--auto` without the session-start recall: agents answer from memory when they decide to call it, rather than starting each session with it. The [agent setup guide](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/agents.html) covers what each harness supports, aider's read-only context file, and the Windows `cmd /c deja mcp` wrapper.
What gets written into each agent's own guidance file Install also writes user-level guidance for the harnesses it detects: Claude Code, Codex, opencode, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Qwen, Kimi Code, pi, Senpi, Copilot, VS Code Copilot Chat, Goose, OpenClaw, Hermes, Roo Code, omp, Amp, prime-agent, DeepSeek Harness, Continue, Crush, CodeBuddy Code, WorkBuddy, Zed, TRAE CLI, TRAE IDE, Muse Code, CodeWhale, ZCode and Junie each get it in their own guidance file (or under the configured `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). Re-run rewrites deja's skill or marked block without changing surrounding user content. Use `deja install --all --no-guidance` to opt out; Grok Build and Devin CLI get the shared skill in `~/.agents/skills`, which is what they read; the `~/.grok/GROK.md` written beside it is for the unrelated community CLI that shares that directory. Cursor has no user-level instructions file, so it gets the shared skill in `~/.agents/skills` — one of the four places Cursor reads skills from — read only when something looks relevant rather than every session. Kilo Code, gajae-code, Kimchi, Command Code, Cherry Studio and Reasonix get the skill, MiniMax Code gets it inside the plugin package, and Kiro the skill and a steering file, from their own install target.
## Memory in the repository Sync moves history between your own machines. To hand the people you work with the few things your agents learned the hard way, put them in the repository: ```text $ deja repo candidates 4cd7e7bb9c rejected Reverted the retry with jitter: it broke idempotency because the sender re-signs each attempt with a new delivery id. (session s1, claude 2026-08-03) $ deja repo add 4cd7e7bb9c added 1 entry to .deja/memory.jsonl nothing is committed: review with `git diff .deja/` and commit it like code ``` Candidates come from this project's history in every agent: promoted and remembered notes, reversals reported in a session, and what sessions settled. Nothing is written until you pick, every entry is redacted on the way in, and one that still matches a secret rule is refused. The file is JSON lines sorted by a content hash, with a `merge=union` attribute beside it, so parallel additions merge; deleting a line removes an entry. After a clone, the entries come back at session start and in recall, in any agent deja is wired into, marked as from the repository and framed as untrusted like the rest. `{"activations":{"auto":{"repo":false}}}` in the trust policy keeps them out of the hooks. [More](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/repo-memory.html). ## Privacy Indexing and search are local. The network is used only by `deja update`, `deja sync ssh`, the version check in `deja doctor`, `deja embed` against an endpoint you configure (and, once it has built the semantic sidecar, each search, which sends the query to that endpoint), and a once-a-day look at the latest release from an interactive command. That look sends no session data; `DEJA_OFFLINE=1` turns it off, and so does `DEJA_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE` set to any value, which also hides the note a new version prints on its first run. Credentials are stripped as the index is built: cloud and provider keys, tokens and JWTs, PEM blocks, passwords in URLs or stated in prose. Each becomes `[redacted:]` and the text around it stays searchable. The source transcripts still hold them ([one machine had 84 in 42 sessions](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/credentials-in-transcripts.html)): `deja secrets` names those sessions without printing a value, and `deja secrets --scrub` rewrites the ones it can, keeping the original beside the file. `deja forget` drops sessions and keeps them dropped across rebuilds. `~/.config/deja/exclude` skips a project per line, or a whole store with `harness:opencode`. The [security model](docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md) has the data flows and what redaction cannot catch. ## CLI Bare `deja` in a terminal opens [the search screen](#search-it-yourself). With a query, or any command below, it prints and exits: ```text $ deja "jwt refresh token" [claude] api · Jul 8 · 8f31c0a9 — 2 matches login started failing after refresh token rotation; jwt kid mismatch in tests fixed by reloading jwks cache after rotateKey and adding a clock-skew test [codex] web · Jul 1 · b77d91e2 — 1 match refresh token cookie needed SameSite=Lax in local callback flow ``` **Ask your history** | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `deja ` | Search every history. Multi-word is AND and quoted phrases require contiguous text; a query with no exact match then tries word forms and close spellings, which is where a substring reaches its word (`code` finds `opencode`). `--sort date` lists the newest match first. | | `deja` | In a terminal, the full-screen search above. `deja brief` prints the text summary instead: today's sessions, what deja served, recent work and a search to try. | | `deja wip` | What the last session in this directory was doing: the task, what it settled, the files in flight, the last command and whether it failed — derived from the transcript, not from a note someone remembered to write. | | `deja blame [:line]` | Which sessions discussed a file, what was decided, and why. With a line: the commit that last changed it, and the session that wrote that line or the text the commit replaced. `--attribution` prints the line answer alone, as JSON with `--json`, and `--git-note` records it in `refs/notes/deja`. | | `deja origin [rev\|range]` | Which session and user turn produced a commit or commit range, matched against recorded edit spans (`attributed`, `uncertain`, or `unknown`). | | `deja review [rev\|range]` | Prior sessions and settled notes (`.deja/notes.jsonl` and personal notes) for the files changed in a working-tree diff, commit, or range. | | `deja files ` | The other direction: which files the work on a subject actually touched. | | `deja how ` | How this machine actually runs a thing, with the real flags, from what agents ran before. | | `deja fix ` | What this machine ran after that same error before, when the error did not come back. Never a merge, a force push or a deletion. | | `deja friction` | Errors that hit three or more separate sessions, with the harnesses named. | When the first word of a bare query has at least four characters and is one edit from a command name, deja names that command on stderr and then searches as usual. `deja search ` skips the suggestion.
Using what it finds, and moving it between machines **Use what it finds** | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `deja ctx ` | Markdown digest of the best match, with the code it changed, ready to pipe into a prompt. | | `deja recall ` | The page the MCP recall tool gives an agent: about 4 KB, this project first (`DEJA_RECALL_GLOBAL=1` ranks every project the same). For skills and scripts that run deja through the shell. | | `deja resume ` | Reopen a found session in its native harness. `--app` opens a Codex session in the ChatGPT desktop app. | | `deja restore ` | Hand back a span an agent replaced, from the `old_string` its edit recorded. Never writes over the original. | | `deja promote ` | Distill a session into a curated note with provenance, tags and a lifecycle state (`--repo` writes to `/.deja/notes.jsonl` for the team). Notes outrank raw transcripts. | | `deja share ` | A sanitized session digest for a colleague, with secrets already scrubbed. | **Move it and check it** | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `deja sync export/import/ssh` | Move memory between machines. Watermarked, append-only, idempotent. | | `deja repo candidates`, `deja repo add ` | Move memory between people: write the decisions and dropped approaches you pick into the repository's `.deja/memory.jsonl`, redacted, for review and commit. Whoever clones it gets them in recall. | | `deja view` | Your whole memory as one local HTML file ([live demo](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/view/)). No server, and the file never leaves the machine. | | `deja stats` | Your agent work, wrapped. `--card` draws it in the terminal, `--card .svg` writes one for a profile, `--html` a browsable timeline. | | `deja secrets [--scrub]` | Which sessions' source transcripts carry credentials, and what kind. Never prints a value. `--scrub` rewrites the ones it can, original kept beside the file. | | `deja rules [sync]` | Keep your standing rules in `~/.config/deja/rules.md`; `sync` copies them as a marked block into every installed agent's global rules file. | | `deja rules candidates [--json] [--limit n] [--since 90d] [--project name] [--repo]` | The turns where you corrected an agent, across every tool (or scoped to `--repo` / `--project`), numbered with their session. Ask your agent to suggest rules and it groups them; nothing is written until you pick. | | `deja doctor [--deep]` | Self-diagnosis, and with `--deep`, proof of the index against the sources. | | `deja mcp` | The stdio MCP server, which is what `deja install` wires in. |
Full reference: [commands](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/commands.html) and [JSON output](docs/json-output.md). ### MCP tools The server exposes one tool, `deja`, with a `mode`; `deja install` wires it in. One tool costs 477 tokens of definitions a turn, against 8,283 for the largest of the seven servers measured in [day zero](https://vshulcz.github.io/deja-vu/guide/day-zero.html). The six older tool names (`recall`, `recall_context`, `blame`, `fix`, `how`, `remember`) still answer. `deja mcp --context-search` is a separate server with a single `context_search` tool, for Qwen Code's External Context MCP Profile v1 ([Qwen page](docs/registry/qwen.md)).
Arguments and return shapes | Tool | Arguments | Returns | | --- | --- | --- | | `deja` | `mode`, `q`, `harness?`, `project?`, `limit?` | Depends on the mode, below. | `q` carries whatever the mode asks about. The per-mode names below are still accepted; they are no longer declared, because the schema is read every turn whether or not the tool is called. | Mode | `q` is | Also reads | Returns | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `recall` | 1-3 exact terms: a file path, an error string, a flag or identifier | `harness?`, `limit?`, `offset?` | Dense matching snippets, capped at 4KB. | | `context` | the same as recall | `harness?` | Markdown digest of the best-matching session, with the code it changed. | | `blame` | a file path | `harness?`, `project?`, `since?`, `limit?`, `all?` | Sessions that discussed a file. | | `fix` | the failing output, verbatim | `limit?` | What this machine ran, or changed, after that same error before. | | `how` | the tool or target, e.g. `go test` | `project?`, `limit?` | The real invocation, from what agents ran here. | | `orient` | nothing — it asks about the project | `project?`, `limit?` | The commands past sessions ran here and the files they worked in. | | `remember` | one durable fact or decision | `project?`, `tags?` | Stores a durable decision for later recall. `project` `repo:` (or `repo:rejected`, `repo:gotcha`) writes it into this repository's `.deja/memory.jsonl` instead, uncommitted. | | `handoff` | a session id or harness name; empty for the newest session here | `harness?` | Another session's goal, standing instructions, latest conclusions, passed checks and where it stopped, to continue it. |
