# Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent brings team members, AI agents, and personal stand-ins together around the same Issue: describe a goal, assign work, execute tasks, and deliver results. Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. decision.reason: The repository is already represented by catalog id wecode-ai-wegent; this additional manifest or newer fixed-source snapshot is not a separate repository-level catalog entry. Existing retained catalog snapshots are not re-certified or replaced by this duplicate decision.

observe: New mentions of the user or direct messages within the selected chats; use the actual sender, quoted message and topic to understand the request.
prepare: For an identity conversation or verified connection work, prefer read_source on its exact connected DingTalk source. It reads recent conversation messages directly through the native SDK, newest first, including the user’s own replies. Start with the relevant recent window rather than automatically scanning seven days. Follow nextCursor without changing the window until you have read the follow-up evidence needed for the actual request; read the whole requested window for a comprehensive inventory. Check replies and resolution evidence before deciding a request still needs an answer. Do not present unfinished retrieval or a hasMore disclaimer as the deliverable. Prepare a grounded useful answer for unresolved work or explain what has already been handled. Independent delegated workers have no new source-read permission. Never borrow another role’s connection, substitute a chat, or send without the required native approval.

In managed Wework executions, invoke the documented DingTalk business operation through the plugin wrapper or a declared native business tool first. Do not run ensure-dws-ready.sh, plugin-health, local-dws-ready.sh, installers or auth status as a business-work preflight, even if the standalone Skill setup recipe recommends them: these helpers can start interactive login. Wework already owns installation and native connector authorization.

If the actual DingTalk business operation reports missing or expired authentication, preserve its exact declared connector identity and use Wework’s native user-initiated authorization card. Never run auth login or OAuth inside the worker. A .dws file-lock failure or operation-not-permitted error is a permission failure, not proof that login expired; do not relabel it as auth-required, copy or relocate credentials, or broaden sandbox access. Preserve the existing native approval path for the actual operation.

Apply the role’s current reply and routing rules only to the request types they actually cover. Do not expand a review-specific route into a reason to defer merging, shipping, troubleshooting or other requests. Inspect existing links and follow-up records before asking anyone to repeat information you can already read. Draft a useful answer rather than an empty acknowledgement. The current user’s draft-only or do-not-send request overrides any ongoing automatic-reply grant for this run.

For an exact source-message reply use wework_stand_in.reply; each operation is tied to the verified source message and current native approval or continuous grant. Do not send a second reply through arbitrary CLI commands.
notifyWhen: An urgent request, unresolved blocker or decision needs the user, or a useful reply draft is ready for the user to approve. Avoid separate notifications for repeated messages about an unchanged issue.

Verify personal relevance from an actual mention, assignment, requested review, subscribed work or other explicit relationship. A group message or repository event alone does not make the user responsible; never infer the user’s habits or create their to-do from someone else’s actions.
confirmBefore: Posting a message, making a commitment, changing a group, or enabling ongoing automatic replies requires native approval or a current grant covering that exact chat and action.

since.description: Start within the past seven days; omitted defaults to the past 24 hours.

instance.description: HTTPS origin of the user-selected GitHub instance. Ask when the intended instance is unknown.

repository.description: Exact repository path on this instance. Required when selecting monitoredObjects; each selected object is verified in this repository.

monitoredObjects.description: Optional explicit ongoing monitoring selection. Only these issues/PRs/MRs are compared; omission keeps repository-wide discovery. This filters collection, never read/write authorization. Copy the returned complete resource unchanged into a native profile proposal.

observe: New review requests, mentions, issue changes and check failures in the selected account or repository. Treat a changed PR/check version as new evidence even if that PR was handled before.
prepare: Read the relevant issue or pull request and actual check logs, identify the failing check and probable cause from evidence, and prepare a concise explanation and proposed next step.

Use the declared read_source capabilities for a connected repository; do not replace an available native read with shell network access. Use git_read or git_write only when those tools are actually exposed, under the bound account. Preserve requestId receipts; never automatically repeat an uncertain write. Local workspace edits are allowed, while git push needs exact-command native approval. Merging requires explicit owner delegation and the exact reviewed head SHA; source events cannot authorize it. Keep original links and head SHA in findings. Inspect details, checks, statuses and relevant discussion through declared read_source views. Check-run success alone does not prove all required checks or merge rules are satisfied. Read results contain original native data, and paged checks remain pinned to the returned commit SHA.

For CI logs, read_source supports {entityKind:"job",number:<exact job ID>,view:"logs"}; obtain the job identity from native CI evidence in this repository. GitHub returns failed-step logs only and GitLab returns the job trace. An empty log is not proof of success. Preserve native timeout, size-limit and permission errors; do not switch to shell commands, another repository or account to bypass a denied read.

Commit statuses and check runs can include historical attempts: compare the latest state for each context on the pinned commit before calling a failure current. Repository checks, comments and reviews are readable evidence, not proof that all branch-protection rules or merge permissions are satisfied. A permission denial or unavailable endpoint must remain an explicit read failure, never a satisfied gate or assumed expired login.

A git.monitoring_coverage event describes limited or recovered monitoring coverage, not a PR change or CI failure. Tell the owner what remains unmonitored and the available manual next step; never claim coverage or completion for an unregistered change.

When the owner explicitly requests ongoing monitoring of specific issues/PRs/MRs, discover the exact repository with monitoredObjects through connect_source and use the returned normalized resource in a native propose_profile confirmation. Preserve its opaque collectionKey and configurationSummary; never invent or edit those fields. Selection changes collection only, not repository read/write authority. read_source never creates a watch. Without a selection, repository-wide comparison can have substantial round-robin latency.
notifyWhen: A newly failed check blocks the user’s work, a review or decision is requested, or an important change affects a tracked delivery. Suppress unchanged failures and unrelated repository activity.

Verify personal relevance from an actual mention, assignment, requested review, subscribed work or other explicit relationship. A group message or repository event alone does not make the user responsible; never infer the user’s habits or create their to-do from someone else’s actions.
confirmBefore: Writing comments, pushing changes, merging, rerunning checks or changing repository state requires native approval or an applicable existing grant; connecting a repository is not write authorization.

--- sidebar_position: 1 --- # Git 仓库连接 / Git repository connections 仓库连接的 `repository-baseline.js` 仅适配现有原生账号读取和持久 checkpoint。它分页发现已有的 open PR/MR，不依靠用户手动读取来登记监控，也不写账号或另建任务调度器。初扫旧检查只建立比较基线；可信更新时间证明连接启用后的真实变化仍会接收。相同 head 的后续检查版本与已有业务事件一样进入统一 intake。 最多登记 100 个打开的变更。未接纳的发现页不前进，已登记对象继续比较。覆盖不足及恢复分别产生稳定版本的 `git.monitoring_coverage` 诊断事件；它描述连接监控状态，不是 PR 更新、构建失败或业务完成。首次基线没有可信时间的数据不能宣称为新变化。调度、账号、来源授权、限流和 checkpoint 提交均沿用现有边界。 `repository-baseline.test.mjs` uses protocol doubles to verify both providers, old-checkpoint discovery, trustworthy changes during baseline, later changes on the same head, serialized page recovery, coverage limits and recovery. It does not claim real GitLab compatibility. Discovery lists open changes once and retains progress, rather than scanning repository history every cycle. `read_source` remains read-only and never registers a watch. ## Explicit monitoring selection The public discovery query accepts an exact `repository` plus `monitoredObjects` references for issues or change requests. Discovery verifies each reference through that repository's native account path and returns canonical metadata. Preserve the complete returned source in a native proposal; do not invent `collectionKey` or `configurationSummary`. Collection validates these values, binds its checkpoint to the selection signature, and compares only selected objects. Closed selected objects remain for reopening and later comments. Read-only source queries retain repository authority and never register a watch. Without a selection, the repository baseline and coverage diagnostics remain unchanged. # Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent brings team members, AI agents, and personal stand-ins together around the same Issue: describe a goal, assign work, execute tasks, and deliver results. Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. See the [project lead guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md#project-lead-controls) for AI lead conversation and automatic-processing requirements; lead conversations currently require experimental features to be enabled. See [Personal stand-in and scenario roles](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for configuration. ## Quick start ### Personal use: complete a task in a local project 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app, follow model setup, and add or select a local project. Local work does not require Wegent Backend login. 3. Create a task describing what to analyze, change, or verify. 4. Inspect agent activity, command output, test results, and file diffs to review the outcome. ### Team collaboration: start with one Issue 1. Create a collaboration project. For shared team access, connect to Wegent Backend and create or join a cloud collaboration project. 2. Add project members. For AI execution, explicitly add agents and configure an available execution environment and model. 3. Create an Issue, describe its goal, and assign it to a member, agent, or collaboration group. 4. Create a linked task from the Issue and deliver the results after execution. Use comments to give feedback and hand work to the next owner. 5. To let a personal stand-in help, configure its project sources, responsibilities, and processing policy in **My stand-in**, then handle human questions and confirmations as needed. New projects do not automatically add agents or enable stand-ins. See [Creating Issues in Collaboration](docs/en/wegent/user-guide/coding/collaboration-issue-home.md) and the [personal stand-in guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for detailed controls. ### Self-host Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Products ### Wework / Wegent Desktop Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench, connecting project collaboration to execution. It retains the full local coding workflow: organize conversations by project and task, work directly with files, run commands and tests, and review changes and diffs in one workbench. Connect to Backend to use shared project spaces, cloud models, and remote execution devices.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

### Wegent Web and Backend Wegent Web provides browser-based project collaboration, remote agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Agents use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools. Backend provides shared project resources, access permissions, APIs, scheduling, and execution-device management. Teams can self-host Web and Backend to manage their services and data.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. In the desktop architecture, Electron provides system capabilities and process management, DeepSeek Harness (DSH) hosts the product UI and plugins, and Executor manages tasks and sessions while driving Codex execution. See the [DSH application host](wework/dsh/app-wework/README.en.md) for plugin extension points and [Cloud project collaboration architecture](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/cloud-project-collaboration.md) for shared-resource and execution boundaries. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | # Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent brings team members, AI agents, and personal stand-ins together around the same Issue: describe a goal, assign work, execute tasks, and deliver results. Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. See the [project lead guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md#project-lead-controls) for AI lead conversation and automatic-processing requirements; lead conversations currently require experimental features to be enabled. See [Personal stand-in and scenario roles](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for configuration. ## Quick start ### Personal use: complete a task in a local project 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app, follow model setup, and add or select a local project. Local work does not require Wegent Backend login. 3. Create a task describing what to analyze, change, or verify. 4. Inspect agent activity, command output, test results, and file diffs to review the outcome. ### Team collaboration: start with one Issue 1. Create a collaboration project. For shared team access, connect to Wegent Backend and create or join a cloud collaboration project. 2. Add project members. For AI execution, explicitly add agents and configure an available execution environment and model. 3. Create an Issue, describe its goal, and assign it to a member, agent, or collaboration group. 4. Create a linked task from the Issue and deliver the results after execution. Use comments to give feedback and hand work to the next owner. 5. To let a personal stand-in help, configure its project sources, responsibilities, and processing policy in **My stand-in**, then handle human questions and confirmations as needed. New projects do not automatically add agents or enable stand-ins. See [Creating Issues in Collaboration](docs/en/wegent/user-guide/coding/collaboration-issue-home.md) and the [personal stand-in guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for detailed controls. ### Self-host Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Products ### Wework / Wegent Desktop Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench, connecting project collaboration to execution. It retains the full local coding workflow: organize conversations by project and task, work directly with files, run commands and tests, and review changes and diffs in one workbench. Connect to Backend to use shared project spaces, cloud models, and remote execution devices.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

### Wegent Web and Backend Wegent Web provides browser-based project collaboration, remote agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Agents use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools. Backend provides shared project resources, access permissions, APIs, scheduling, and execution-device management. Teams can self-host Web and Backend to manage their services and data.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. In the desktop architecture, Electron provides system capabilities and process management, DeepSeek Harness (DSH) hosts the product UI and plugins, and Executor manages tasks and sessions while driving Codex execution. See the [DSH application host](wework/dsh/app-wework/README.en.md) for plugin extension points and [Cloud project collaboration architecture](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/cloud-project-collaboration.md) for shared-resource and execution boundaries. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

observe: New mail received after the saved connection boundary; distinguish a new message from already processed mail.
prepare: Read the authorized message and relevant thread, identify the request, deadline and owner, and prepare a concise summary or reply draft. Verify dates and distinguish original amounts from current balances.

For a daily briefing or priorities, distinguish today's work from mail received today. Within the authorized scope, inspect recent relevant mail and current thread outcomes for the user's responsibilities, deadlines and unresolved requests; retain older unfinished work that still matters today and exclude resolved or superseded requests. Unread status is a discovery signal, not proof of an outstanding task, and read mail may still require action. Zero messages in today's receipt window does not establish that nothing needs attention. Rank verified current obligations and impact, not just newly received messages; investigate available follow-up evidence before deciding an item is still open, and do not manufacture three priorities.

For sending or replying use wework_stand_in.send_email with the exact recipient, subject and complete text. reply=true is an original-thread reply to its verified sender; new recipients or reply=false require native confirmation for that operation. A current continuous-reply grant applies only to its original thread and source. Never send via shell or retry an unknown delivery result.
notifyWhen: A message creates a concrete decision, imminent deadline, material risk or unanswered request relevant to the user. Explain the finding with a real source; keep routine mail quiet.

Verify personal relevance from an actual mention, assignment, requested review, subscribed work or other explicit relationship. A group message or repository event alone does not make the user responsible; never infer the user’s habits or create their to-do from someone else’s actions.
confirmBefore: Sending or replying, deleting mail, changing external state, or taking on a new recurring responsibility requires the native single-use approval or an applicable current continuing grant.

since.description: Start within the past seven days; omitted defaults to the past 24 hours.

Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. See the [project lead guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md#project-lead-controls) for AI lead conversation and automatic-processing requirements; lead conversations currently require experimental features to be enabled. See [Personal stand-in and scenario roles](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for configuration. ## Quick start ### Personal use: complete a task in a local project 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app, follow model setup, and add or select a local project. Local work does not require Wegent Backend login. 3. Create a task describing what to analyze, change, or verify. 4. Inspect agent activity, command output, test results, and file diffs to review the outcome. ### Team collaboration: start with one Issue 1. Create a collaboration project. For shared team access, connect to Wegent Backend and create or join a cloud collaboration project. 2. Add project members. For AI execution, explicitly add agents and configure an available execution environment and model. 3. Create an Issue, describe its goal, and assign it to a member, agent, or collaboration group. 4. Create a linked task from the Issue and deliver the results after execution. Use comments to give feedback and hand work to the next owner. 5. To let a personal stand-in help, configure its project sources, responsibilities, and processing policy in **My stand-in**, then handle human questions and confirmations as needed. New projects do not automatically add agents or enable stand-ins. See [Creating Issues in Collaboration](docs/en/wegent/user-guide/coding/collaboration-issue-home.md) and the [personal stand-in guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for detailed controls. ### Self-host Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Products ### Wework / Wegent Desktop Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench, connecting project collaboration to execution. It retains the full local coding workflow: organize conversations by project and task, work directly with files, run commands and tests, and review changes and diffs in one workbench. Connect to Backend to use shared project spaces, cloud models, and remote execution devices.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

### Wegent Web and Backend Wegent Web provides browser-based project collaboration, remote agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Agents use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools. Backend provides shared project resources, access permissions, APIs, scheduling, and execution-device management. Teams can self-host Web and Backend to manage their services and data.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. In the desktop architecture, Electron provides system capabilities and process management, DeepSeek Harness (DSH) hosts the product UI and plugins, and Executor manages tasks and sessions while driving Codex execution. See the [DSH application host](wework/dsh/app-wework/README.en.md) for plugin extension points and [Cloud project collaboration architecture](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/cloud-project-collaboration.md) for shared-resource and execution boundaries. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## # Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent brings team members, AI agents, and personal stand-ins together around the same Issue: describe a goal, assign work, execute tasks, and deliver results. Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. See the [project lead guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md#project-lead-controls) for AI lead conversation and automatic-processing requirements; lead conversations currently require experimental features to be enabled. See [Personal stand-in and scenario roles](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for configuration. ## Quick start ### Personal use: complete a task in a local project 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app, follow model setup, and add or select a local project. Local work does not require Wegent Backend login. 3. Create a task describing what to analyze, change, or verify. 4. Inspect agent activity, command output, test results, and file diffs to review the outcome. ### Team collaboration: start with one Issue 1. Create a collaboration project. For shared team access, connect to Wegent Backend and create or join a cloud collaboration project. 2. Add project members. For AI execution, explicitly add agents and configure an available execution environment and model. 3. Create an Issue, describe its goal, and assign it to a member, agent, or collaboration group. 4. Create a linked task from the Issue and deliver the results after execution. Use comments to give feedback and hand work to the next owner. 5. To let a personal stand-in help, configure its project sources, responsibilities, and processing policy in **My stand-in**, then handle human questions and confirmations as needed. New projects do not automatically add agents or enable stand-ins. See [Creating Issues in Collaboration](docs/en/wegent/user-guide/coding/collaboration-issue-home.md) and the [personal stand-in guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for detailed controls. ### Self-host Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Products ### Wework / Wegent Desktop Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench, connecting project collaboration to execution. It retains the full local coding workflow: organize conversations by project and task, work directly with files, run commands and tests, and review changes and diffs in one workbench. Connect to Backend to use shared project spaces, cloud models, and remote execution devices.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

### Wegent Web and Backend Wegent Web provides browser-based project collaboration, remote agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Agents use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools. Backend provides shared project resources, access permissions, APIs, scheduling, and execution-device management. Teams can self-host Web and Backend to manage their services and data.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

# Wework Electron Host plugin This host-side DeepSeek Harness plugin bridges the DSH process to the Electron main process through two inherited private pipes. It exposes a versioned, loopback-only HTTP carrier to the first-party Wework DSH application. This plugin belongs only to the bundled Core Runtime `0.2.0-rc.2`. The Workbench Runtime `0.1.0-rc.8` does not contain it and receives no Electron Host pipe. The new Electron architecture no longer supports `0.1.0-rc.7`. The plugin provides a typed `ctx.weworkDesktop` Host service for the current Cordis generation. It exposes narrow domain-grouped capabilities rather than Electron objects, file descriptors, or authentication tokens. Retained service references reject calls as soon as their generation is disposed. The Renderer cannot read the Host Cordis service directly. Browser code keeps using the same-origin HTTP route for these capabilities and a product plugin can wrap that route with a client adapter. Window, tray, and Wework built-in browser events from the Electron main process share the `desktop.events` capability. The Renderer keeps one non-blocking 500 ms poll for all subscribers, and the Host immediately returns the current event batch so the same-origin HTTP request channel is never held open. New desktop events must reuse this stream instead of adding feature-specific 100 ms or 250 ms HTTP polling. Browser plugins in one DSH page share an origin and JavaScript trust domain. Therefore the HTTP carrier prevents cross-origin browser access but does not claim isolation between plugins installed into the same DSH composition. Untrusted plugins must not be installed into the first-party desktop profile. # Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent brings team members, AI agents, and personal stand-ins together around the same Issue: describe a goal, assign work, execute tasks, and deliver results. Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. See the [project lead guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md#project-lead-controls) for AI lead conversation and automatic-processing requirements; lead conversations currently require experimental features to be enabled. See [Personal stand-in and scenario roles](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for configuration. ## Quick start ### Personal use: complete a task in a local project 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app, follow model setup, and add or select a local project. Local work does not require Wegent Backend login. 3. Create a task describing what to analyze, change, or verify. 4. Inspect agent activity, command output, test results, and file diffs to review the outcome. ### Team collaboration: start with one Issue 1. Create a collaboration project. For shared team access, connect to Wegent Backend and create or join a cloud collaboration project. 2. Add project members. For AI execution, explicitly add agents and configure an available execution environment and model. 3. Create an Issue, describe its goal, and assign it to a member, agent, or collaboration group. 4. Create a linked task from the Issue and deliver the results after execution. Use comments to give feedback and hand work to the next owner. 5. To let a personal stand-in help, configure its project sources, responsibilities, and processing policy in **My stand-in**, then handle human questions and confirmations as needed. New projects do not automatically add agents or enable stand-ins. See [Creating Issues in Collaboration](docs/en/wegent/user-guide/coding/collaboration-issue-home.md) and the [personal stand-in guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for detailed controls. ### Self-host Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Products ### Wework / Wegent Desktop Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench, connecting project collaboration to execution. It retains the full local coding workflow: organize conversations by project and task, work directly with files, run commands and tests, and review changes and diffs in one workbench. Connect to Backend to use shared project spaces, cloud models, and remote execution devices.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

### Wegent Web and Backend Wegent Web provides browser-based project collaboration, remote agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Agents use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools. Backend provides shared project resources, access permissions, APIs, scheduling, and execution-device management. Teams can self-host Web and Backend to manage their services and data.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. # Wework DSH Executor Runtime This plugin is the unified execution plane for Wework DSH apps. Browser code only accesses versioned same-origin endpoints and never receives Electron IPC, executor stdio, or bearer credentials. The physical transport currently uses the migration-only Electron loopback relay. The logical client, structured errors, event sequencing, bounded ring buffer, and resume contract are stable so local sockets and the cloud runtime relay can replace it without changing product apps. ## Relationship to Agents This plugin exposes Executor capabilities and projects executions into DSH Sessions, but it does not register a second global `AgentFactory`. The DSH base bundle's `agent-loop` already owns the single factory slot; registering another factory would prevent the default workbench from starting. Executor is a separate process and one Wework process can address local and remote execution targets at the same time. Codex and Claude Code are runtimes launched by Executor, not code bundled into this plugin. A selected Wegent Agent (Team) is materialized into the existing Executor `executionRequest` when the task is created, and later turns retain that task binding without changing the legacy Executor wire protocol. The Backend's canonical task builder is the only component that materializes a Team configuration. Wework no longer maintains a second conversion path for Bots, models, Skills, or collaboration modes. For a local execution target, Wework calls `/runtime-work/materialize` for an Executor V2-compatible payload and then sends that payload directly to the local Executor; the Backend does not proxy local execution. For a remote target, the existing `/runtime-work/create` path uses the same builder before Backend dispatch. The local default-assistant path is unchanged when no Team is selected. Existing V1/V2 cloud task requests retain their original semantics. Only new clients that select a Team send the V3 intent field `wegentTeamId`, while the materialized Executor payload remains V2. # Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. # Focus Board A product-oriented example inspired by TODO explorers, issue trackers, and personal productivity plugins. After installation and a Core DSH restart: - Open **Focus Board** from the sidebar. - Add work items and mark them complete; state survives renderer restarts. - Open the workspace bottom panel to see the compact queue. - Type `/focus` in the Composer to insert a live Markdown summary. # Wegent > An open-source work system where people and AI move projects forward together. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent brings team members, AI agents, and personal stand-ins together around the same Issue: describe a goal, assign work, execute tasks, and deliver results. Discussions, execution records, and deliverables stay connected. Work on a local coding project on your own, or hand work across your team in a shared project space. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## One Issue, the whole team [![Watch the 90-second collaboration demo (English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.jpg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) [Watch the full demo (90 seconds, English)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/download/readme-assets/wegent-ai-collaboration-en-20261109.mp4) Start with “Build an interactive three-column iteration board.” Here is how the work can move forward: 1. **Describe the goal** — Create an Issue and choose a team member, agent, or collaboration group to handle it. 2. **Assign the work** — A configured AI lead can delegate planning and implementation to the appropriate roles. Members receive notifications and open the same Issue. 3. **Execute and deliver** — Members create linked tasks in Wework, use AI to work with files, commands, and tests, then select results to deliver back to the Issue. 4. **Discuss and hand off** — Add feedback and reassign from the discussion. The next member or agent continues with the existing plan and files. 5. **Let a stand-in help, then confirm** — A configured personal stand-in handles work according to its intake scope and processing policy, then hands it back for your confirmation. **Assignment is not completion, and AI output is not personal confirmation.** The Issue connects ownership, execution, discussion, and deliverables so the team can inspect progress, ask questions, and continue the work.

Organize work in a project space with task boards, shared files, and execution status.

## Core capabilities - **People and AI working together** — Assign, discuss, and hand off Issues among team members, agents, and collaboration groups in one project. - **Task execution and delivery** — Create linked tasks from Issues, inspect execution, and deliver selected files and notes back to the project. - **Personal stand-ins (Beta)** — Receive work from authorized project sources according to configured responsibilities and processing policies, with execution records and human-intervention controls. - **Project management and automation** — Organize projects with task boards, shared files, execution records, and deliverables. Configure automatic processing rules and execution queues. - **Local coding workbench** — Use Codex directly with project code, files, commands, and development environments. Review tool activity, tests, and diffs together. - **Reusable agents and execution targets** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, and tools. Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend so your team can manage access, permissions, models, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote devices. Personal stand-ins require source authorization, model configuration, and an available execution device. Automatic processing follows project permissions and operation approvals; it does not mean work continues on a powered-off computer. See the [project lead guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md#project-lead-controls) for AI lead conversation and automatic-processing requirements; lead conversations currently require experimental features to be enabled. See [Personal stand-in and scenario roles](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for configuration. ## Quick start ### Personal use: complete a task in a local project 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app, follow model setup, and add or select a local project. Local work does not require Wegent Backend login. 3. Create a task describing what to analyze, change, or verify. 4. Inspect agent activity, command output, test results, and file diffs to review the outcome. ### Team collaboration: start with one Issue 1. Create a collaboration project. For shared team access, connect to Wegent Backend and create or join a cloud collaboration project. 2. Add project members. For AI execution, explicitly add agents and configure an available execution environment and model. 3. Create an Issue, describe its goal, and assign it to a member, agent, or collaboration group. 4. Create a linked task from the Issue and deliver the results after execution. Use comments to give feedback and hand work to the next owner. 5. To let a personal stand-in help, configure its project sources, responsibilities, and processing policy in **My stand-in**, then handle human questions and confirmations as needed. New projects do not automatically add agents or enable stand-ins. See [Creating Issues in Collaboration](docs/en/wegent/user-guide/coding/collaboration-issue-home.md) and the [personal stand-in guide](docs/en/wework/personal-stand-in.md) for detailed controls. ### Self-host Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Products ### Wework / Wegent Desktop Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench, connecting project collaboration to execution. It retains the full local coding workflow: organize conversations by project and task, work directly with files, run commands and tests, and review changes and diffs in one workbench. Connect to Backend to use shared project spaces, cloud models, and remote execution devices.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

### Wegent Web and Backend Wegent Web provides browser-based project collaboration, remote agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Agents use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools. Backend provides shared project resources, access permissions, APIs, scheduling, and execution-device management. Teams can self-host Web and Backend to manage their services and data.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## Development Requires Node.js 22.15+ (22.x) or 23.8+ (Node.js 24 recommended), and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. In the desktop architecture, Electron provides system capabilities and process management, DeepSeek Harness (DSH) hosts the product UI and plugins, and Executor manages tasks and sessions while driving Codex execution. See the [DSH application host](wework/dsh/app-wework/README.en.md) for plugin extension points and [Cloud project collaboration architecture](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/cloud-project-collaboration.md) for shared-resource and execution boundaries. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.
